topics.title_zh: 家乡
topics.title_en: Hometown

questions.question_en: Where is your hometown?
questions.answer_en: My hometown is Shenzhen, a first-tier city in the south of China, next to Hong Kong. I've lived here my whole life, so it really feels like home, and honestly, I can't imagine living anywhere else.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 深圳是一线城市，毗邻香港；从小住在这里，感觉就像家一样。

questions.question_en: Is that a big city or a small place?
questions.answer_en: It's a huge city, one of the biggest in China, with skyscrapers everywhere. The thing is, it feels young and modern rather than old and crowded, which I quite like. More than seventeen million people live here.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 深圳是中国最大的城市之一，高楼林立；但感觉年轻现代不老旧，人口超一千七百万。

questions.question_en: Please describe your hometown a little.
questions.answer_en: Well, Shenzhen is a modern coastal city in southern China, famous for its tech industry. There's a seaside area in Bao'an with the tallest ferris wheel in Asia, at Bay Glory, and I love spending weekends there.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 深圳是南方现代沿海城市，科技产业发达；宝安欢乐港湾有亚洲最高摩天轮，周末常去。

questions.question_en: How long have you been living there?
questions.answer_en: I've lived in Shenzhen my entire life, actually, so around twenty years now, since I was born here. My parents moved to the city before I was born, and we've never really thought about leaving since then.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 出生起就住在深圳约二十年；父母在出生前搬来，从没想过离开。

questions.question_en: Do you think you will continue living there for a long time?
questions.answer_en: Yes, definitely. I'm planning to stay in Shenzhen after graduation because all my friends are here and the job opportunities are great. Honestly, I can't see myself settling down anywhere else in the future.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 毕业后打算留在深圳，朋友都在、机会多；未来想在深圳定居。

questions.question_en: Do you like your hometown?
questions.answer_en: Oh, absolutely, I do. I mean, it's where I grew up, so I have a really strong attachment to it. Even the little things, like the food and the weather, make me happy about living there.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 非常喜欢；深圳是长大的地方，有深厚感情，连食物和天气都让人开心。

questions.question_en: Do you like living there?
questions.answer_en: To be honest, I really enjoy it. Life there is super convenient, the transport is efficient, and the city is always full of energy. There's always something new to explore, like a fresh restaurant opening every week.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 生活很方便，交通高效，城市有活力；总有新东西可探索。

questions.question_en: What do you like (most) about your hometown?
questions.answer_en: The thing I value most is how developed the infrastructure is, like the metro, hospitals and schools are all within easy reach. On top of that, the weather stays mild all year, so it's never really cold.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 最看重基础设施发达，地铁医院学校都近；且全年天气温和不太冷。

questions.question_en: Is there anything you dislike about it?
questions.answer_en: Well, not much comes to mind, because I really do love living there. If I had to pick something, it'd be the cost of living, which is pretty high, and the summers can get uncomfortably hot and humid.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 很难挑毛病；若要选，就是生活成本高，夏天又热又潮湿。

questions.question_en: What's your hometown famous for?
questions.answer_en: Shenzhen is famous for its tech industry, with companies like Tencent based there and Ma Huateng, its founder, as a local legend. It's also known for Deng Xiaoping's special economic zone, which turned a fishing village into a global city.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 以科技产业闻名，腾讯总部在此、马化腾是本地名人；也是邓小平经济特区，由渔村变全球都市。

questions.question_en: Did you learn about the history of your hometown at school?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, we actually did cover it in history class. I remember learning that Shenzhen used to be a small fishing village until it became a special economic zone, which is pretty amazing when you look at how it looks today.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 历史课学过深圳从渔村变成经济特区的历史，对比今天很惊人。

questions.question_en: Are there many young people in your hometown?
questions.answer_en: Oh, definitely, tons of them. Shenzhen is known as a young city, you know, full of university graduates who move there for work. Walking around the streets, I often feel like most people I see are under thirty.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 年轻人数不胜数；深圳是座年轻城市，毕业生都来工作，街上大多是三十岁以下。

questions.question_en: Is your hometown a good place for young people to pursue their careers?
questions.answer_en: Definitely, it's one of the best. The job market is huge, especially in tech and finance, and salaries are high compared to other cities. That's why so many young people move to Shenzhen to chase their dreams.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 绝对是很好的选择；就业市场大，科技金融机会多、工资高，适合追梦。

questions.question_en: Have you learned anything about the history of your hometown?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, quite a lot, actually. The most interesting thing I picked up is that Shenzhen was just a fishing village forty years ago, and now it's a massive international city. That transformation fascinates me.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 学过不少；最感兴趣的是深圳四十年前还是渔村，如今已是国际化大都市。

questions.question_en: Did you learn about the culture of your hometown in your childhood?
questions.answer_en: Hmm, to some extent, yes. At school we learned that Shenzhen is a city of migrants, so its culture is quite open and diverse. Growing up, I also experienced that blend of Cantonese and modern city culture myself.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 童年学过深圳是移民城市，文化开放多元；亲身感受过粤语文化与现代都市文化交融。

topics.title_zh: 工作或学习
topics.title_en: Work or Studies

questions.question_en: What work do you do?
questions.answer_en: Well, I'm actually still a student, studying Computer Science and Technology at university. So I don't have a job yet, but I treat my coursework as my main responsibility and spend most of my time programming.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 我是学生，主修计算机科学与技术，学业即主业。

questions.question_en: Why did you choose to do that type of work (or that job)?
questions.answer_en: I chose this field mainly because I've been crazy about computers since I was a kid, you know, playing games and tinkering with the settings. That curiosity just naturally pushed me toward computer science, and I've never regretted that choice.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 从小喜欢玩电脑、折腾设置，顺理成章选了计算机。

questions.question_en: Do you like your job?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, I really enjoy it, honestly. The thing is, I get to play with AI tools every day, which I genuinely love. Last week I even used an AI assistant to debug a project, and it saved me ages.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 挺喜欢的，天天能玩 AI 工具，上周 AI 还帮我调试了项目。

questions.question_en: What requirements did you need to meet to get your current job?
questions.answer_en: Well, I'm not working yet, but to get into this program I needed decent grades in math and physics, plus a solid foundation in English. I mean, the entrance exam was pretty competitive, so I had to prepare quite seriously.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 还没工作；进这专业靠数理化成绩加英语基础，入学考试竞争激烈。

questions.question_en: Do you have any plans for your work in the next five years?
questions.answer_en: Definitely, yeah. I plan to finish my degree first, and then I'd love to work as a software engineer, probably specializing in AI. I've actually been chatting with AI a lot lately, and that direction just feels right for me.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 先读完学位，之后想当软件工程师，方向偏 AI。

questions.question_en: What do you think is the most important at the moment?
questions.answer_en: I'd say building solid programming fundamentals is the most important thing right now. You know, data structures and algorithms, because everything else builds on top of that. Honestly, without those basics, nothing else makes sense.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 眼下最重要的是打牢编程基本功，比如数据结构和算法。

questions.question_en: Do you want to change to another job?
questions.answer_en: Not really, no. I'm quite happy with the path I've chosen, and switching now wouldn't make much sense. I mean, I've already invested so much time in programming, so I'd rather keep improving than start from scratch.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不想换，编程已投入很多时间，宁愿继续深耕。

questions.question_en: Do you miss being a student?
questions.answer_en: Ha, I'm actually still a student, so I don't miss it yet. But honestly, I can imagine missing this phase later, since student life is pretty relaxed compared to working full time.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 我现在还是学生，还没资格怀念，但能想象以后会怀念。

questions.question_en: What technology do you use at work?
questions.answer_en: Well, since I'm a student, I mainly use a laptop and a tablet for studying. My laptop handles the heavy stuff like coding, and my tablet is handy for reading papers and taking notes in lectures.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 学习主力是笔记本电脑和平板，电脑写代码、平板看文献。

questions.question_en: Who helps you the most? And how?
questions.answer_en: Definitely my girlfriend, without a doubt. She helps me a lot with my studies, mostly by encouraging me when I'm stuck or stressed about exams. Actually, her support really keeps me motivated to keep going.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 女朋友帮最多，主要是在学习上鼓励我、给我打气。

questions.question_en: What subjects are you studying?
questions.answer_en: I'm studying Computer Science and Technology, so the subjects are mostly programming, data structures, operating systems, and things like that. We also have some math courses, like linear algebra and probability, which I find quite challenging actually.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 学的都是编程、数据结构、操作系统，还有线性代数这类数学课。

questions.question_en: Do you like your subject?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, I really do. I mean, computer science lets me build things from nothing, which feels kind of magical. And these days I often talk to AI for assignments, which honestly makes learning way more fun.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 喜欢，计算机能从零造出东西很神奇，加上常跟 AI 聊作业。

questions.question_en: Why did you choose to study that subject?
questions.answer_en: Well, honestly, I've loved playing with computers since I was little, you know, messing around with games and settings. So when it came to choosing a major, computer science just felt like the obvious choice for me.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 小时候就爱摆弄电脑和游戏，选专业时计算机自然是首选。

questions.question_en: Do you think that your subject is popular in your country?
questions.answer_en: Oh, definitely, computer science is incredibly popular in China right now. Basically everyone sees it as a path to a well-paid job, so lots of students are rushing into it, which is both good and a bit worrying.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 计算机在国内超火，大家觉得能拿高薪，都在往里挤。

questions.question_en: Do you have any plans for your studies in the next five years?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, I plan to finish my bachelor's degree and then probably do a master's, maybe abroad if I can manage it. I'm also hoping to work on some AI projects on the side, since that's where my real interest lies.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 计划本科毕业后读研，可能出国，同时做点 AI 项目。

questions.question_en: What are the benefits of being your age?
questions.answer_en: I think the biggest benefit is having tons of energy and time to learn, you know, to make mistakes and fix them. Like, right now I can try all kinds of new things without too much pressure.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 这个年纪最大的好处是精力足、试错成本低。

questions.question_en: Do you want to change your major?
questions.answer_en: No, not at all. I'm really into what I'm studying, especially the AI side of things, so changing majors never really crossed my mind. I mean, I chose this path because I love it, not because of any pressure.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 完全不想换，尤其喜欢 AI 方向，是真心喜欢才选的。

questions.question_en: Do you prefer to study in the mornings or in the afternoons?
questions.answer_en: I'd say afternoons, definitely. I'm not really a morning person, so my brain doesn't fully wake up until around two o'clock. Actually, most of my productive coding sessions happen late in the afternoon or even in the evening.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 更喜欢下午学习，不是晨型人，下午到晚上效率最高。

questions.question_en: How much time do you spend on your studies each week?
questions.answer_en: Quite a lot, honestly. I'd say around forty hours a week, which includes lectures, homework, and my own coding practice. Plus, I usually spend a couple of extra hours chatting with AI to figure out tricky concepts.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 每周大约四十小时，加上用 AI 弄懂难题的时间。

questions.question_en: Are you looking forward to working?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, definitely, though I'm a bit nervous too. I'm excited to apply what I've learned in real projects and actually get paid for doing what I love. Still, working full time will be a whole new challenge.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 期待工作，想把所学用到真实项目里，但也知道全职是挑战。

questions.question_en: What technology do you use when you study?
questions.answer_en: I mainly use my laptop and tablet when I study. The laptop is for coding, while the tablet is great for reading textbooks and taking notes. And I rely a lot on AI tools to explain things I don't understand.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 电脑写代码加平板读教材记笔记，还常用 AI 工具答疑。

questions.question_en: What changes would you like to see in your school?
questions.answer_en: I'd love to see more hands-on projects and real-world case studies in our courses, you know, instead of just theory. Also, it would be great if the school offered more AI-related courses, since that's clearly where the industry is heading.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 希望课程多点实战项目，并开设更多 AI 相关课程。

topics.title_zh: 家 / 住所
topics.title_en: Home/Accommodation

questions.question_en: What kind of house or apartment do you want to live in in the future?
questions.answer_en: In the future, I'd love to own a bigger apartment, maybe with an extra room for myself, since I currently share a room with my brother. Having my own space to use my computer freely sounds really appealing.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 未来想住更大的房子，有自己的房间不跟弟弟挤，方便用电脑。

questions.question_en: Are the transport facilities to your home very good?
questions.answer_en: Actually, yes, they're quite convenient. There's a bus stop right outside my community, and the metro station is within walking distance, so I can reach most of Shenzhen without much trouble.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 交通很方便，小区门口有公交站，地铁站走路就到。

questions.question_en: Do you prefer living in a house or an apartment?
questions.answer_en: Well, I'd say an apartment, since that's what I've grown up with. A house with a garden sounds nice in theory, but an apartment in the city is far more practical.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 更喜欢公寓，从小住习惯了，城市里公寓更实用。

questions.question_en: Please describe the room you live in.
questions.answer_en: My room isn't very big, but it's pretty cosy. I share it with my younger brother in a bunk bed, and there's a desk near the window where I work on my computer. It gets a bit crowded sometimes, to be honest.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 房间不大但温馨，和弟弟睡上下床，窗边有桌子用电脑。

questions.question_en: What part of your home do you like the most?
questions.answer_en: Honestly, I like my own room the most, even though it's shared. That's where my desk and computer are, so it's basically my little world where I spend most of my time.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 最喜欢自己的房间，因为桌子电脑都在那儿，基本是我的小天地。

questions.question_en: How long have you lived there?
questions.answer_en: I've been living in this apartment for as long as I can remember, basically my whole life. We moved here when I was quite young, so this place holds a lot of memories for me and my family.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 从小就住这儿，基本住了一辈子，满满回忆。

questions.question_en: Do you plan to live there for a long time?
questions.answer_en: Probably, yeah. It's close to everything, and the neighborhood is quiet, which I really appreciate. Since I'd like to stay in Shenzhen after graduation, I imagine I'll be here for quite a while yet.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 应该会住很久，小区安静交通方便，毕业后也想留在深圳。

questions.question_en: What's the difference between where you are living now and where you have lived in the past?
questions.answer_en: To be honest, I've basically lived in this same neighborhood my whole life, so there's no big difference for me. I suppose the area has grown busier over the years, with more buildings going up, but our apartment itself hasn't changed much.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 基本一直住这个小区，区别不大，就是周边新盖了些楼。

questions.question_en: Can you describe the place where you live?
questions.answer_en: I live in an apartment, you know, a three-bedroom one with my family in Shenzhen. My brother and I actually share a room with a bunk bed, which is pretty fun. There's a desk where I sit and use my computer most of the day.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 深圳三室一厅，跟弟弟睡上下床，桌边整天用电脑。

questions.question_en: What room does your family spend most of the time in?
questions.answer_en: Probably the living room, since that's where we all gather to eat dinner and watch TV together. My grandfather likes to sit there in the afternoon, and my parents often chat there after work. It's the heart of our home, really.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 客厅，全家一起吃饭看电视，爷爷也爱待那儿。

questions.question_en: What's your favorite room in your apartment/house?
questions.answer_en: My favorite room has to be my bedroom, no question. I mean, that's where my computer is, and I spend hours there studying and gaming with my brother. The bunk bed makes it feel like a little den for the two of us.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 最喜欢卧室，电脑在那儿，和弟弟一起学习打游戏，上下床像小窝。

questions.question_en: What makes you feel pleasant in your home?
questions.answer_en: I think what really makes me feel good is the quiet environment. The neighborhood is peaceful, so I can focus on my computer without distractions. Also, having my whole family around makes the place feel warm and lively, which I really value.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 小区安静能专心用电脑，加上家人在身边很温暖。

questions.question_en: Do you think it is important to live in a comfortable environment?
questions.answer_en: Definitely, I think it matters a lot. A comfortable home helps you relax and recharge after a stressful day, and it also affects your mood and even your health. For me, a quiet place to study and rest is essential.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 非常重要，舒适的家能放松充电，安静的环境对学习休息很关键。

questions.question_en: Do you live in an apartment or a house?
questions.answer_en: I live in an apartment, specifically a three-bedroom one that my parents bought. It's our family home, where I've lived with my parents, my grandfather and my siblings for as long as I can remember.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 住的是父母买的三室一厅公寓，一家几代人一起住。

questions.question_en: Who do you live with?
questions.answer_en: I live with my parents, my grandfather and my siblings, so our family is quite large. With five of us or more under one roof, the apartment always feels busy, but I actually enjoy having everyone around.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 和爸妈、爷爷、兄弟姐妹一起住，一家五口以上很热闹。

questions.question_en: What do you usually do in your apartment?
questions.answer_en: Most of my time at home goes to my computer, to be honest. I study, browse videos, chat with friends, and sometimes play games, all at my desk in my room. I don't really go out much, so that's my daily routine.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 在家基本就是对着电脑，学习、刷视频、聊天打游戏都在书桌前。

questions.question_en: What kinds of accommodation do you live in?
questions.answer_en: It's a standard apartment block, and our unit is a three-bedroom one, so I guess you could call it typical urban accommodation. Nothing fancy, but it's comfortable enough for our whole family.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 普通小区三室一厅，标准城市住宅，不算豪华但住得舒服。

topics.title_zh: 你居住的地区
topics.title_en: The area you live in

questions.question_en: Do you like the area that you live in?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, I like it, honestly. I live in Xin'an Street, and there's a place called Qianhai nearby where you can see the sea and lots of parks. The people are friendly as well, so it's quite comfortable to live in.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 喜欢，因为前海离得近、能看海，还有好多公园，周围人也友善。

questions.question_en: Where do you like to go in that area?
questions.answer_en: I often go to Qianhai, actually. There are plenty of parks there, and you can see the sea, which is great for a walk after work. Sometimes I just sit by the water and relax for a while.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 常去前海，公园多又能看海，下班后去散散步、坐坐很放松。

questions.question_en: Do you know any famous people in your area?
questions.answer_en: Not really, I don't think so. The people in my neighborhood are mostly ordinary folks, like office workers and students, so nobody famous as far as I know. But everyone seems quite nice and friendly, I guess.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 没听说有名人，邻居都是普通上班族和学生，不过人都挺和善的。

questions.question_en: What are some changes in the area recently?
questions.answer_en: Well, my own neighborhood hasn't really changed that much, to be honest. But a brand new residential community has been built nearby recently, and I've noticed a lot of new families moving in, which makes the place feel livelier.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 自己小区变化不大，倒是周边新建了一个住宅小区，搬来很多新家庭。

questions.question_en: Do you know any of your neighbors?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, I know quite a few of them, like the family living next door. We don't really chat much, though, probably just a quick hello now and then, but they seem really friendly and easy to get along with.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 认识几个邻居，但很少深聊，顶多打个招呼，人都挺和善好相处。

questions.question_en: Are the people in your neighborhood nice and friendly?
questions.answer_en: To be honest, yes, they are. Most of them are friendly, even though we don't really talk to each other that often. When we meet in the elevator or downstairs, they always greet you with a smile, which I appreciate.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 都挺友善的，虽然不常聊天，但在电梯或楼下碰到都会微笑打招呼。

questions.question_en: Do you live in a noisy or a quiet area?
questions.answer_en: It's quiet, I'd say. My apartment is in a residential community, so there's not much traffic noise at night. Occasionally you hear construction from the new community nearby, but it's not too bad, and I sleep well.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 挺安静的，小区夜里没什么车流噪音，偶尔能听到附近新建小区的施工声。

topics.title_zh: 你居住的城市
topics.title_en: The city you live in

questions.question_en: What city do you live in?
questions.answer_en: Well, I live in Shenzhen, which is one of the biggest first-tier cities in China, down in the south. It's a modern, fast-growing metropolis, so there's always something new going on around me.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 我住在深圳，中国南方的一线城市，现代化大都市，变化很快。

questions.question_en: Do you like this city? Why?
questions.answer_en: To be honest, yes, I really do. I like the convenience and all the opportunities it offers, especially in tech and business. The thing is, though, the pace of life is a bit too fast for me sometimes.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 喜欢，方便、机会多，但节奏太快有时有点累。

questions.question_en: How long have you lived in this city?
questions.answer_en: Actually, I've lived here my whole life, ever since I was born. Shenzhen is my permanent home, and I've watched it grow and change over the years, which has been quite interesting to experience.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 从出生就住这里，深圳就是我的永久家园。

questions.question_en: Are there big changes in this city?
questions.answer_en: Oh yes, absolutely. Shenzhen is constantly changing, you know, new metro lines, new skyscrapers and whole districts keep appearing. It's one of the most rapidly developing cities in the country, honestly.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 变化非常大，新地铁、新大楼、新城区不断出现。

questions.question_en: Is this city your permanent residence?
questions.answer_en: Yes, it is. I was born here and I consider Shenzhen my permanent residence. All my family and friends are here too, so I can't really imagine living anywhere else long-term.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 是的，深圳是我的永久居住地，家人朋友都在这里。

questions.question_en: Are there people of different ages living in this city?
questions.answer_en: Definitely. Shenzhen attracts people of all ages, from young graduates chasing opportunities to retired people who have settled here. It's quite a diverse mix, which makes the city feel lively and never boring.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 各年龄段都有，年轻人和退休的人很多，城市很有活力。

questions.question_en: Are the people friendly in this city?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, I'd say so. Most people here are quite friendly and helpful, even though it's a huge city. I mean, strangers will happily give you directions or help you carry things, which surprised me at first.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 挺友善的，虽然城市大，但陌生人也很热心帮忙。

questions.question_en: Is the city friendly to children and old people?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think it is, actually. There are plenty of parks and playgrounds for kids, and the metro and buses are really convenient for the elderly. The city seems well designed for both groups, which I appreciate.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 对小孩老人很友好，公园多，地铁公交都方便。

questions.question_en: Do you often see your neighbors?
questions.answer_en: Not really, to be honest. I see them occasionally in the lift or at the entrance, and we say hello, but we don't chat much. It's the same for a lot of people in big cities, I guess.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不常碰见，电梯里遇到就打个招呼，大城市都这样。

questions.question_en: What's the weather like where you live?
questions.answer_en: Well, the weather in Shenzhen is hot and humid for most of the year. Summers are particularly sticky and uncomfortable, but winters are mild, which is actually quite pleasant compared to other parts of China.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 天气湿热为主，夏天黏糊糊的，冬天温和舒服。

questions.question_en: Would you recommend your city to others?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I would, definitely. Shenzhen is such a prosperous and bustling city, full of energy and opportunities. I'd recommend it to anyone who wants a vibrant career, though I'd warn them about the fast pace.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 会推荐，深圳很繁华、机会多，但要适应快节奏。

topics.title_zh: 公园
topics.title_en: Parks

questions.question_en: Did you like going to parks as a child?
questions.answer_en: Oh yeah, definitely. I loved going to parks when I was little, you know, running around and playing with friends on the swings. We'd go almost every weekend, and I always looked forward to it.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 小时候很喜欢去公园，和小伙伴荡秋千、奔跑，几乎每周都去，特别期待。

questions.question_en: Do you still like going to parks now?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, I do, actually. I still go now, especially to Shenzhen Bay Park. It's right by the sea, so the view is amazing, and it's perfect for relaxing after a long week.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 现在还爱去，最喜欢深圳湾公园，靠海景色美，很适合放松。

questions.question_en: Would you like to see more parks in your city?
questions.answer_en: Absolutely, I would. I mean, Shenzhen is quite crowded, so more green spaces would give people somewhere quiet to unwind. Plus, parks make a city feel much more liveable, honestly.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 希望多建公园，深圳太拥挤，需要更多绿地让人放松，城市也更宜居。

questions.question_en: Are there any parks you want to go to in the future?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, quite a few, actually. I'd love to explore more parks along the coast, like the ones near Shenzhen Bay, because I love the sea breeze. Honestly, I'd rather spend a day in a park than in a mall.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 想探索更多沿海公园，比如深圳湾一带，相比商场更愿意待在公园。

topics.title_zh: 太空与星星
topics.title_en: Outer space and stars

questions.question_en: Have you ever learned about outer space and stars?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, I have, actually. We covered a bit in school, you know, basic stuff about planets and the solar system, and I've also picked up a lot from sci-fi movies like Iron Man, which got me curious about space.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 学校学过星球和太阳系的基础知识，也从钢铁侠这类科幻片里了解到不少。

questions.question_en: Do you like science fiction movies? Why?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, I really do. I mean, films like Iron Man take you to worlds you'll never see in real life, and the futuristic technology is just fascinating to watch. Plus, they always make me wonder what space is actually like.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 喜欢科幻片，钢铁侠展示的未来科技很迷人，还让人好奇太空真实的样子。

questions.question_en: Do you want to know more about outer space?
questions.answer_en: Oh, definitely. I'd love to learn more about things like black holes and space travel, you know, just to satisfy my curiosity. The thing is, there's still so much we don't know, and that's what excites me.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 想了解更多太空知识，比如黑洞和太空旅行，未知的东西最吸引我。

questions.question_en: Do you want to go into outer space in the future?
questions.answer_en: Hmm, honestly, no, I don't. I find space fascinating from a distance, but actually going there sounds terrifying, since it's dangerous and so far from home. I'd rather just keep learning about it here on Earth.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不想亲自去太空，觉得太危险、离家太远，更愿意在地球上学习太空知识。

topics.title_zh: 建筑
topics.title_en: Building

questions.question_en: Are there tall buildings near your home?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, quite a few, actually. Shenzhen is full of high-rises, so there are lots of tall apartment blocks and office towers near my place. You can see them from almost every street, honestly.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 家附近高楼很多，深圳到处是住宅和写字楼，几乎每条街都能看到。

questions.question_en: Do you take photos of buildings?
questions.answer_en: Not really, to be honest. I prefer photographing nature and scenery instead, since buildings just don't interest me that much. I mean, I can appreciate a nice skyline, but I wouldn't stop to take a photo of it.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不怎么拍建筑，更喜欢拍自然风景，虽然能欣赏天际线但不会特意去拍。

questions.question_en: Is there a building that you would like to visit?
questions.answer_en: Not really, honestly. The thing is, I'm actually afraid of heights, so visiting tall landmarks doesn't appeal to me at all. I'd rather stay on the ground and enjoy buildings from street level, you know.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 没有特别想参观的楼，因为怕高，宁愿在地面从街边欣赏建筑。

questions.question_en: Do you want to live in a tall building?
questions.answer_en: Definitely not, to be honest. Since I'm afraid of heights, living up on the twentieth floor would make me pretty uncomfortable. I'd much prefer a low-rise apartment, you know, somewhere closer to the ground.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不想住高楼，因为怕高，住二十层会很不舒服，更想住低层公寓。

topics.title_zh: 科学
topics.title_en: Science

questions.question_en: Do you like science?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, kind of, I'd say I like it a moderate amount. I'm not a science geek or anything, but I find it interesting. My interest really started back in primary school, when we did simple experiments in class.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 还行，说不上痴迷但挺感兴趣，兴趣从小学做简单实验时开始。

questions.question_en: When did you start to learn about science?
questions.answer_en: I guess it was in primary school, when science became a proper subject on our timetable. I remember being quite curious about it then, especially the nature experiments we did, like growing plants and watching them change.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 小学科学课成为正式科目，那时开始对自然实验特别好奇。

questions.question_en: Which science subject is interesting to you?
questions.answer_en: For me, it has to be astronomy, space science in general. I've always been fascinated by the idea of other planets and galaxies, and how tiny we are in the universe. It just makes me curious about what's out there.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 最喜欢天文太空，宇宙里其他行星星系和人类的渺小很吸引我。

questions.question_en: What kinds of interesting things have you done with science?
questions.answer_en: Well, I used to watch a science show called 'Approaching Science' when I was young, which covered lots of strange phenomena. I've also been to a science museum a few times, and I remember enjoying the hands-on exhibits there.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 小时候看《走近科学》节目，也去过科技馆，喜欢那里的互动展品。

questions.question_en: Do you like watching science TV programs?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, I quite like them, actually. As a kid I used to watch a program called 'Approaching Science', which explained everyday mysteries simply. I don't watch them as much now, but they still fascinate me.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 喜欢看科学节目，小时候常看《走近科学》，现在看得少了但仍觉得有意思。

questions.question_en: Do Chinese people often visit science museums?
questions.answer_en: Not that often, honestly. Most people I know would rather spend a day off shopping or eating out, so science museums usually stay fairly quiet unless there's a school trip. I've been a few times myself, though.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 中国人不常逛科技馆，多数人周末更爱逛街吃饭，除非学校组织参观。

topics.title_zh: 汽车
topics.title_en: Cars

questions.question_en: Did you enjoy traveling by car when you were a kid?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, I really did. As a kid I loved going on car trips, even short ones to the supermarket, because I could just sit back and watch the city go by. There was something exciting about being on the road.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 小时候喜欢坐车出门，连去超市都兴奋，可以坐着看窗外街景。

questions.question_en: What types of cars do you like?
questions.answer_en: I'm really into SUVs, to be honest. They have plenty of space, which matters to me because I'm quite tall, and they're comfortable for long drives. A big interior makes the whole ride much more pleasant.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 喜欢 SUV，空间大，我个子高坐着舒服，长途也舒适。

questions.question_en: Do you prefer to be a driver or a passenger?
questions.answer_en: Definitely a driver. I genuinely enjoy being behind the wheel and having control over the route, especially on roads I know well. As a passenger I get a bit restless, to be honest, because I can't do anything but wait.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 更喜欢当司机，享受掌控方向盘和路线的乐趣，当乘客会觉得无聊。

questions.question_en: What do you usually do when there is a traffic jam?
questions.answer_en: I just look out the window, honestly. I'd rather watch the street life, the shops and the people, than stare at my phone. It keeps me calm, and sometimes I even spot interesting little scenes.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 堵车时就看窗外，看街景和行人而不刷手机，这样能保持平静。

questions.question_en: Do you think car colors are important?
questions.answer_en: Not really, no. To me, what matters is the performance, the comfort and the price, not the colour. I mean, white and black cars are everywhere anyway, so colour doesn't really stand out anymore.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 颜色不重要，性能、舒适度和价格才重要，满大街黑白车，颜色不突出。

topics.title_zh: 老师
topics.title_en: Teachers

questions.question_en: Do you have a favorite teacher?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I do. My favourite would be my high school IT teacher, Mr Chen, who taught us basic programming. He noticed I loved computers and spent his lunch breaks teaching me extra coding, which I really appreciated.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 有，最喜欢高中信息技术陈老师，他教编程还午休额外辅导我。

questions.question_en: Do you want to be a teacher in the future?
questions.answer_en: Not really, I don't think so. I'm studying computer science and I'd rather work as a software engineer, building things with code. Though I do respect teachers a lot, it's just not the path for me.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不想当老师，我学计算机想当软件工程师，但很尊敬老师这份职业。

questions.question_en: Do you have a teacher from your past that you still remember?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, one primary school teacher still stands out. He criticised my handwriting in front of the whole class, which embarrassed me at the time, but honestly it pushed me to write more carefully after that. I've never really forgotten it.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 记得小学老师当众批评我写字丑，当时很尴尬，但反而让我写字更认真。

questions.question_en: Are you still in touch with your primary school teachers?
questions.answer_en: No, not really. I left primary school years ago, and since then I've just lost touch with all my teachers there. I don't even know where most of them teach now, to be honest.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不联系了，小学毕业多年，和所有小学老师都断了联系。

questions.question_en: In what way has your favourite teacher helped you?
questions.answer_en: My high school IT teacher helped me a lot. He taught me basic programming after class and told me I should consider computer science as my major. That advice stuck with me, and it's why I chose this path.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 高中老师课后教我编程基础，还建议我选计算机专业，影响了我后来的选择。

topics.title_zh: 社交媒体
topics.title_en: Social media

questions.question_en: Have you ever posted anything on social media?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, of course, loads of times. I post photos and short updates about my daily life, like places I've been or meals I've had. It's a nice way to keep in touch with friends who don't live nearby.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 发过很多次，发照片和日常动态，比如去过的地方、吃过的饭。

questions.question_en: When did you start using social media?
questions.answer_en: Quite early, actually, back in primary school. I think it was around then that I made my first account, probably to chat with classmates about homework and games. Social media has just been part of my life since then.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 小学就开始用了，第一个账号用来和同学聊作业和游戏。

questions.question_en: Do you think you spend too much time on social media?
questions.answer_en: Not really, I don't think so. I use it mainly to check messages and catch up on news, but I don't scroll for hours. I'd say maybe an hour a day at most, and I'm fine with that.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不算多，主要看消息和新闻，每天最多一小时，不会刷太久。

questions.question_en: Do your friends use social media?
questions.answer_en: Oh, definitely, all of them do. I don't think I know anyone my age who isn't on at least one platform. It's basically how we share news and make plans these days, so we'd be lost without it.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 朋友全都在用，同龄人几乎没有人不用社交平台。

questions.question_en: What do people often do on social media?
questions.answer_en: All sorts of things, really. Most people share their daily life, post photos, and follow news accounts for updates. Shopping has also become huge on social media lately, with built-in stores and live-stream selling.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 分享日常、发照片、看新闻，现在购物和直播带货也很火。

topics.title_zh: 手表
topics.title_en: Watch

questions.question_en: Do you wear a watch?
questions.answer_en: Not anymore, actually. I used to wear a smart watch, mainly for tracking my runs. The thing is, I didn't end up running much, so it felt unnecessary. Now I just check my phone.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 以前戴智能手表是为了记跑步，但没怎么跑，就觉得没必要，现在只看手机。

questions.question_en: Have you ever got a watch as a gift?
questions.answer_en: Never, honestly. I've received clothes and gadgets as gifts, but never a watch. I guess my family and friends just don't think of watches when they're choosing presents for me.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 从没收过手表做礼物，家人朋友挑礼物时一般不会想到手表。

questions.question_en: Why do some people wear expensive watches?
questions.answer_en: I think it's mostly about status and image. An expensive watch is a visible symbol of success, and for some people it's also a kind of investment or collection. It's more about showing off, I suppose.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 主要是地位和形象，贵表是成功的象征，也有人当投资或收藏。

questions.question_en: Do you think it is important to wear a watch? Why?
questions.answer_en: Not really, to be honest. Since everyone has a phone these days, checking the time is never a problem, so a watch doesn't seem necessary. For me personally, it's just an extra thing to carry.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不太重要，人人有手机随时看时间，对我来说手表只是多带一样东西。

topics.title_zh: 网站
topics.title_en: Websites

questions.question_en: What kinds of websites do you often visit?
questions.answer_en: Mostly video and social platforms, I'd say. I spend a lot of time on Bilibili and WeChat Channels, watching tech reviews and short clips. Traditional news websites rarely get a visit from me.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 主要是视频和社交平台，最常用哔哩哔哩和微信视频号，看科技评测和短视频。

questions.question_en: What is your favourite website?
questions.answer_en: Definitely Bilibili. It has everything, learning videos, tech reviews and entertainment, so I can always find something that catches my interest. Honestly, I often lose track of time there.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 最喜欢哔哩哔哩，学习视频、科技评测、娱乐都有，一刷就忘了时间。

questions.question_en: Are there any changes to the websites you often visit?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, quite a lot, actually. These platforms keep updating their designs and recommendation systems. WeChat Channels, for instance, has grown a lot over the past couple of years, and I've noticed more short videos everywhere.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 变化挺大，平台不断更新设计和推荐算法，视频号这几年增长很快，短视频到处都是。

questions.question_en: What kinds of websites are popular in your country?
questions.answer_en: Video and social media platforms are the biggest, without a doubt. Bilibili, Douyin and Xiaohongshu are everywhere, which makes sense because we live in the internet era and people spend so much of their lives online.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 视频和社交平台最火，哔哩哔哩、抖音、小红书随处可见，因为现在是互联网时代。

topics.title_zh: 镜子
topics.title_en: Mirrors

questions.question_en: Do you like looking at yourself in the mirror? How often?
questions.answer_en: Not really, to be honest. I only glance in the mirror about once a day, usually to check my hair before leaving home. I'm not really a vain person, so I never spend long there.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不太爱照镜子，一天大概一次，出门前看看头发，不是爱臭美的人。

questions.question_en: Have you ever bought mirrors?
questions.answer_en: No, I don't think I have. There's already a full-length mirror at home, so I've never felt the need to buy one myself. It's just not something that crosses my mind when I'm shopping.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 从没买过镜子，家里本来就有穿衣镜，买东西时根本想不起来。

questions.question_en: Do you usually take a mirror with you?
questions.answer_en: No, never. When I'm out and want to check my appearance, I just use my phone camera. A small mirror would only take up space in my bag, so I don't bother.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不会带，出门想照就用手机摄像头，小镜子只会占包里的地方。

questions.question_en: Would you use mirrors to decorate your room?
questions.answer_en: Probably not. Mirrors don't really appeal to me as decoration, and since I rarely look at myself anyway, they wouldn't serve much of a purpose. I'd rather put up posters or something like that.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 大概不会，镜子当装饰不吸引我，反正也不照，宁愿挂海报。

topics.title_zh: 礼物
topics.title_en: Gifts

questions.question_en: Have you ever sent handmade gifts to others?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I have, actually. I once made a handmade card for a friend's birthday and wrote a message inside, which she really appreciated. I think handmade things feel more personal than bought ones.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 送过，曾给朋友手工做生日贺卡并写上留言，手作礼物更有心意。

questions.question_en: Have you ever received a great gift?
questions.answer_en: Well, I've received nice gifts, but nothing that truly surprised me. Most gifts I get are practical things, like clothes or gadgets. Honestly, I don't think I've had that wow moment yet.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 收过不错的礼物，但没遇过特别惊喜的，大多是衣服、小电器这类实用品。

questions.question_en: What do you consider when choosing a gift?
questions.answer_en: The recipient's preferences, definitely. I always try to think about what the person actually likes instead of just picking something expensive. After all, a gift only works if the other person enjoys it.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 最看重对方喜好，会想对方真正喜欢什么，而不是只挑贵的。

questions.question_en: Do you think you are good at choosing gifts?
questions.answer_en: I'd say I'm fairly decent at it. Because I pay attention to what people like, my choices usually hit the mark. That said, I still get it wrong from time to time, honestly.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 还算擅长，因为平时留意对方喜好，选的礼物大多合适，偶尔也会失手。

questions.question_en: What gift have you received recently?
questions.answer_en: An electric shaver, actually. My family gave it to me not long ago, which was quite thoughtful since I'd mentioned needing one. It's simple, but I use it almost every day.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 最近收到家人送的电动剃须刀，因为我提过需要，很贴心，几乎天天用。

topics.title_zh: 宠物与动物
topics.title_en: Pets and Animals

questions.question_en: What's your favourite animal? Why?
questions.answer_en: My favourite animal has to be cats. I mean, I've never owned one, but their fur looks and feels incredibly soft, and they have this calm, independent character that I find really appealing. I always enjoy watching them in videos.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 最喜欢的动物是小猫，因为毛摸起来很软，性格安静独立。

questions.question_en: Where do you prefer to keep your pet, indoors or outdoors?
questions.answer_en: Well, I keep my fish outdoors, actually, in a large tank in the yard. They're basically free-range, swimming around freely, and I only need to feed them, which keeps things simple.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 鱼养在户外院子里的大鱼缸里，散养状态，只需喂食。

questions.question_en: Have you ever had a pet before?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I have, and I actually still keep them. We've had fish for quite a few years now, and they're still around. It's not a demanding pet, just some food and clean water, so looking after them has been easy.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 养过鱼，现在还养着，不费心，喂食换水就行。

questions.question_en: What is the most popular animal in China?
questions.answer_en: I'd say dogs and cats are the most popular animals in China. You see them everywhere, in parks, on the streets, and all over social media. Lots of young people keep them as companions, especially in big cities.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 中国最受欢迎的动物是狗和猫，尤其大城市年轻人爱养。

topics.title_zh: 食物
topics.title_en: Food

questions.question_en: What is your favourite food?
questions.answer_en: My current favourite is a seafood dish called huajia, which are clams, usually stir-fried with garlic and chilli. I love how fresh and juicy they are, and the sauce is really addictive. Honestly, I could eat them every week.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 最爱吃花甲，蒜蓉辣椒炒的，鲜嫩多汁很上瘾。

questions.question_en: What kind of food did you like when you were young?
questions.answer_en: When I was young, I was crazy about latiao, those spicy snack sticks sold at every corner shop. I used to save my pocket money to buy them after school, even though my parents warned me they weren't healthy.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 小时候超爱辣条，攒零花钱放学买来吃。

questions.question_en: Do you eat different foods at different times of the year?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, to some extent. In summer we eat lighter dishes, while in winter we go for heavier, warming meals like hotpot. But the staples at home are basically always chicken, duck, goose and pork, no matter the season.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 季节不同吃法不同，夏天清淡冬天暖和，但家里常备鸡鸭鹅猪肉。

questions.question_en: Has your favourite food changed since you were a child?
questions.answer_en: Definitely, it has changed. As a kid, I only cared about snacks like latiao, but now my taste is completely different. These days I'm much more into proper dishes like clams, so my favourite has shifted to something healthier.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 口味变了，从小爱吃辣条到现在爱吃花甲这类正经菜。

topics.title_zh: 运动队 / 团队运动
topics.title_en: Sports team

questions.question_en: Have you ever been part of a sports team?
questions.answer_en: No, I haven't, to be honest. I've never really been into competitive sports, so I never joined any team at school. I prefer spending my free time on other things, like gaming or chatting with friends online.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 从没加入过运动队，对竞技体育不感兴趣。

questions.question_en: Is team sports popular in your culture?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, I'd say so, especially basketball and football. A lot of my classmates play basketball after school, and the school often holds matches. It's just not really my thing, but I can see why people enjoy it.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 团队运动在国内很流行，篮球足球都多人玩，但我不感兴趣。

questions.question_en: Do you like watching team games? Why?
questions.answer_en: Not really, to be honest. Watching team games just doesn't grab my attention, so I rarely sit through a full match. I'd rather watch something more engaging to me, like esports, which I find genuinely exciting.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不喜欢看团队比赛，更爱看电竞。

questions.question_en: What are the differences between team sports and individual sports?
questions.answer_en: The main difference is cooperation. In team sports, everyone has to work together and coordinate, so you win or lose as a group. Individual sports, on the other hand, depend entirely on your own skill and preparation.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 区别在于配合，团队运动要协作，个人运动全靠自己。

topics.title_zh: 风景
topics.title_en: Scenery

questions.question_en: Do you look out the window at the scenery when travelling by bus or car?
questions.answer_en: Yes, almost always. When I travel by bus or car, I love watching the scenery pass by, especially the fields and villages in the countryside. It's a great way to kill time, and sometimes the views are genuinely stunning.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 坐车坐公交超爱看窗外风景，尤其田野村庄。

questions.question_en: Do you prefer the mountains or the sea?
questions.answer_en: Definitely the sea. I find the sea more relaxing, with the sound of waves and the open horizon, and Shenzhen has plenty of seaside spots to enjoy. Mountains are nice for hiking, but the sea just calms me down.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 更喜欢海，海浪和开阔海平线让人放松。

questions.question_en: Do you like to take scenery pictures?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, I really enjoy it. When I travel, I take lots of scenery photos, like mountains, seas and city skylines, mostly with my phone. Looking back at them later always brings back nice memories of the trip.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 旅行爱拍风景照，山、海、城市天际线都拍。

questions.question_en: What are the most beautiful sights you have seen while travelling?
questions.answer_en: The most beautiful sight I've seen is Jilong Mountain in Yangjiang. I went there with my girlfriend, and the grassland on the mountaintop was just breathtaking, with the clouds rolling below us. I took a ton of photos that day.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 见过最美的风景是阳江鸡笼顶，和女朋友一起，山顶草地云海很震撼。

topics.title_zh: 景色
topics.title_en: Views

questions.question_en: Do you like taking pictures of different views?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I love it. Different views, whether it's the sea, mountains or city streets, each have their own charm, so I like capturing them. My phone album is basically full of travel views and random shots I've taken.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 喜欢拍不同景色，海、山、城市街道各有各的美。

questions.question_en: Do you prefer views in urban areas or rural areas?
questions.answer_en: I prefer urban views, honestly. Skyscrapers, night lights and modern architecture give me a real sense of technology and progress, which I find exciting. Rural views are peaceful, but they don't impress me as much.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 更喜欢城市景色，高楼夜景有科技感。

questions.question_en: Do you prefer views in your own country or in other countries?
questions.answer_en: Views in other countries, to be fair. Foreign cities have this vintage, old-fashioned feel, like old European streets, that you don't really see in China. That contrast with what I'm used to makes them more appealing.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 更喜欢国外景色，欧洲老街道很复古，国内看不到。

questions.question_en: Have you seen an unforgettable and beautiful view or scenery?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, I have. The sunset over the sea at Qianhai, near where I live, was unforgettable. The whole sky turned orange and pink, and the sea reflected it beautifully. I still remember standing there, completely amazed.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 前海的海边日落很美，天空橙粉一片，难以忘怀。

topics.title_zh: 童年活动
topics.title_en: Childhood activities

questions.question_en: What were your favourite activities?
questions.answer_en: My favourite activities as a kid were playing tag and hide and seek with my friends, and also computer games. We'd run around the neighbourhood until it got dark, then head home to play games on the computer.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 童年最爱抓人游戏、捉迷藏和打电脑游戏。

questions.question_en: What were your favourite activities when you were a child?
questions.answer_en: When I was a child, I loved outdoor games with my friends, like tag and hide and seek, and I was also hooked on computer games. Back then, any free moment after school felt like a chance to have fun.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 小时候爱和伙伴玩户外游戏，也迷电脑游戏。

questions.question_en: Did you prefer to do activities alone or with a group of people when you were a child?
questions.answer_en: With a group, definitely. I was happiest when I was playing tag or hide and seek with my friends, since everything felt more fun together. Doing things alone never really appealed to me as a kid. I loved the company.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 小时候喜欢跟一群小伙伴玩，有人陪才开心。

questions.question_en: Are there any differences between the activities you liked when you were a child and those you like now?
questions.answer_en: Yes, quite a few. As a child I loved group activities with my friends, but now I mostly enjoy things alone, like chatting with AI or watching videos on my computer. I guess my hobbies have become much more solitary.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 有变化，小时候爱群体活动，现在更喜欢一个人，比如跟AI聊天。

topics.title_zh: 购物
topics.title_en: Shopping

questions.question_en: Do you like shopping?
questions.answer_en: To be honest, not really. I only go shopping when my girlfriend drags me along, and even then, I'd rather finish quickly and head home. It's just not something I get excited about, really.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 说实话不太喜欢，一般只陪女朋友去，想快点买完回家。

questions.question_en: How often do you go shopping?
questions.answer_en: Not very often, honestly, maybe a couple of times a month at most. Usually it's with my girlfriend, when she needs to buy clothes or things for the house. I don't go browsing on my own, that's for sure.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不太频繁，一个月最多一两次，基本是陪女朋友买衣服或日用品。

questions.question_en: Do you prefer online shopping or in-store shopping?
questions.answer_en: Definitely online shopping. It's so much more convenient, I can order anything without leaving the house, and it arrives in a couple of days. Honestly, not having to go out is the biggest selling point for me.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 绝对喜欢网购，方便、不用出门，两三天就能送到。

questions.question_en: Have you ever returned anything you bought online?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, I have, a few times. Once I ordered a pair of shoes a size too small, so I sent them back and got a refund. The whole process took about a week, which wasn't too bad.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 退过几次，比如鞋码太小就寄回去退款了，流程一周左右。

topics.title_zh: 唱歌
topics.title_en: Singing

questions.question_en: Do you like singing? Why?
questions.answer_en: Honestly, I love it. I sing all the time at home, and somehow it just cheers me up. Even if I'm not good at it, the moment I start, I feel happier, which I think says a lot.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 很喜欢唱歌，在家常唱，就算唱得不好，一开口心情就变好。

questions.question_en: Have you ever learned how to sing?
questions.answer_en: No, I haven't, to be honest. I've never taken any singing lessons or learned proper techniques, I just copy what I hear and sing along. It's all by ear, really, and somehow that's enough for me.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 没学过，从不报班，就是凭感觉跟唱，全靠听。

questions.question_en: Who do you want to sing for?
questions.answer_en: Mostly for my girlfriend, to be honest. I often sing to her when we're chatting or on the phone, even though I'm a bit shy about it. She seems to enjoy it, and it's become a little habit between us.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 主要唱给女朋友听，打电话或聊天时会唱，虽然有点害羞。

questions.question_en: Do you think singing can bring happiness to people?
questions.answer_en: Absolutely, I do. Singing is a great way to let off steam, and I feel that joy firsthand whenever I do it. Even people who aren't good singers can enjoy it, since it's more about the feeling than the performance.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 当然能，唱歌是放松的好方式，重要的是心情而不是唱得专不专业。

topics.title_zh: 人生阶段
topics.title_en: Life stages

questions.question_en: What did you often do with your friends in your childhood?
questions.answer_en: As a kid, I often played tag and hide-and-seek with my friends after school. We'd run around the neighbourhood until it got dark, and sometimes we'd gather at someone's home to play computer games together.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 小时候放学常和朋友玩抓人、捉迷藏，跑遍小区到天黑，有时去别人家打电脑游戏。

questions.question_en: What do you think is the most important at the moment?
questions.answer_en: For me, building solid programming fundamentals is the most important thing right now. I mean, data structures and algorithms come up everywhere in computer science, so getting those right early makes everything else easier.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 眼下最重要的是打好编程基础，数据结构算法到处都用得到，基础好别的都顺。

questions.question_en: Do you have any plans for the next five years?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, I do. I plan to finish my degree first, and then work as a software engineer, probably focusing on AI. I've been talking to AI a lot lately, and that's the direction that genuinely excites me.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 打算先读完学位，再当软件工程师，方向偏AI，最近常和AI交流，很感兴趣。

questions.question_en: How do people remember each stage of their lives?
questions.answer_en: I think people remember each stage through the impactful moments, the ones tied to strong feelings or big events. I mean, I remember the emotional highlights of my childhood clearly, but the ordinary days have mostly faded away.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 人们靠那些印象深刻的时刻记住每个阶段，和强烈情感或大事绑在一起；平淡的日子都淡忘了。

questions.question_en: Do you enjoy being the age you are now?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, I really do. I'm at an age where I can learn, explore and make mistakes without too much pressure. Honestly, being a student gives me the freedom to try new things, which I'm enjoying while it lasts.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 挺享受现在的年纪，能学习、探索、试错压力不大，当学生自由尝试新事物。

questions.question_en: At what age do you think people are the happiest?
questions.answer_en: I'd say childhood, definitely. When you're a kid, you don't really have worries, and every day is about playing and having fun. Looking back, those carefree years were probably the happiest of my life.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 童年最幸福，小孩没什么烦恼，每天就是玩，回头看那些无忧无虑的日子最快乐。

topics.title_zh: 早晨
topics.title_en: Morning time

questions.question_en: Do you like getting up early in the morning?
questions.answer_en: Not at all, to be honest. I'm definitely not a morning person, and I struggle to get out of bed before ten on most days. If I have to wake up early, I feel groggy for hours afterwards.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 一点都不喜欢早起，不是晨型人，早起了会昏昏沉沉一上午。

questions.question_en: What do you usually do in the morning?
questions.answer_en: Well, I tend to stay in bed for a while, scrolling through my phone until I finally get up. After that, I grab a quick breakfast, usually something simple like porridge or bread, and then start my day.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 早上一般赖床刷会儿手机，然后随便吃点粥或面包就开始一天。

questions.question_en: What did you do in the morning when you were little? Why?
questions.answer_en: As a kid, my mornings were totally different, my mum would call me up, I'd lie in bed for a bit, eat breakfast, and then head off to school. I remember the walk to school pretty clearly, actually.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 小时候早上被妈妈叫醒，赖会儿床、吃早饭再走去上学，那段上学路记忆很深。

questions.question_en: Are there any differences between what you do in the morning now and what you did in the past?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, the biggest difference is my wake-up time. I used to get up early for school, but now I sleep in much later, especially when I have no classes. Honestly, the lazy mornings are a real luxury.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 最大区别是起床时间，以前上学得起早，现在没课就睡懒觉，赖床成了享受。

questions.question_en: Do you spend your mornings doing the same things on both weekends and weekdays? Why?
questions.answer_en: Pretty much, yeah. I get up earlier on weekdays for classes and sleep in on weekends, but the routine after waking is the same, breakfast, phone, then getting on with the day. Only the start time really changes.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 差不多一样，工作日早起上课、周末睡懒觉，但起床后的流程都一样，只是开始时间不同。

topics.title_zh: 阅读
topics.title_en: Reading

questions.question_en: Do you like reading?
questions.answer_en: Kind of, I'd say. I didn't read much as a kid, apart from suspense novels, which I was really into. These days I read even less, mainly because studying takes up most of my time and energy.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 一般般，小时候除了悬疑小说读得不多，现在更少，学习占了大半时间。

questions.question_en: Do you prefer to read on paper or on a screen?
questions.answer_en: I'd say paper, without a doubt. Real books feel better in my hands, and I focus more when there's no screen flashing at me. Plus, flipping actual pages somehow makes reading feel more relaxing.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 更喜欢纸质书，拿在手里有感觉，没有屏幕干扰，翻页也更放松。

questions.question_en: When do you need to read carefully, and when not?
questions.answer_en: I read carefully when it's something important, like study materials or textbooks, since every detail matters there. But when it comes to external news or casual posts, I just skim through the headlines and move on.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 学习材料、课本会细读，因为细节重要；外界新闻和帖子就只看标题。

questions.question_en: Do you prefer scanning or detailed reading?
questions.answer_en: It really depends on the situation, I'd say. For study material, I prefer detailed reading, because I need to understand every concept properly. For news and general information, though, scanning is more than enough for me.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 看情况，学习材料要精读，新闻和一般信息扫读就够了。

topics.title_zh: 散步 / 走路
topics.title_en: Walking

questions.question_en: Do you walk a lot?
questions.answer_en: Not really, to be honest. I don't go out of my way to walk, but I do enjoy an evening stroll by the river near my home, since it's quiet and relaxing. That's probably the most walking I do.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 走得不算多，但喜欢傍晚到家旁边的河边散步，安静又放松。

questions.question_en: Did you often go outside to have a walk when you were a child?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, quite often, actually. My parents used to take me for walks in the morning when I was little, usually around the neighbourhood before school. I remember those quiet mornings with them quite fondly.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 小时候爸妈常带我去散步，一般是上学前在小区周边走走，挺怀念。

questions.question_en: Why do people like to walk in parks?
questions.answer_en: I think it's mainly because parks are peaceful and green, a nice escape from busy streets. Walking there lets people relax, get fresh air, and clear their heads, which is hard to do in a crowded city.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 公园安静又绿意盎然，能让人远离喧嚣放松、呼吸新鲜空气、理清思绪。

questions.question_en: Where would you like to take a long walk if you had the chance?
questions.answer_en: I'd love to walk along the coast, since I'm a big fan of the sea. A long walk by the shore, with the breeze and waves, sounds perfect. Honestly, the bay area near my home would be ideal for that.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 想沿着海边走，我很喜欢海，海风配着海浪声，家附近的海湾区域就很理想。

questions.question_en: Where did you go for a walk lately?
questions.answer_en: I went for a walk by the river near my home, actually, just last week. It was a nice evening, so I strolled along the bank for about an hour, watching the water and just unwinding from the day.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 上周去家旁边的河边散步了，傍晚沿河岸走了约一小时，看看水放松一下。

topics.title_zh: 打字
topics.title_en: Typing

questions.question_en: Do you prefer typing or handwriting?
questions.answer_en: I definitely prefer typing, to be honest. I'm on my computer most of the day, so typing feels natural, and it's much faster than writing by hand. Honestly, my handwriting isn't great either, which is another reason.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 更喜欢打字，天天用电脑打字自然又快；手写字不好看也是原因。

questions.question_en: Do you type on a desktop or laptop keyboard every day?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, every day, definitely. I mainly use my laptop keyboard, since I take it with me everywhere, to class and back home. I find laptop keys a bit softer than desktop ones, but I've gotten used to them.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 每天都打字，主要用笔记本键盘，随身带方便；已习惯笔记本较软的键感。

questions.question_en: When did you learn how to type on a keyboard?
questions.answer_en: I first learned to type back in primary school, during our computer classes. We practised basic keyboarding there, and honestly, I picked it up quite quickly because I enjoyed playing around on the machines.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 小学计算机课第一次学打字，因为喜欢玩电脑学得很快。

questions.question_en: How do you improve your typing?
questions.answer_en: Well, for me it was mostly gaming, to be honest. Chatting with teammates during online games forced me to type fast, so my speed improved naturally. These days I get plenty of practice through coursework and chatting with AI.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 靠打游戏和队友打字沟通练快了速度；现在靠写作业和跟AI聊天保持。

topics.title_zh: 整洁
topics.title_en: Tidiness

questions.question_en: Do you like to keep things tidy?
questions.answer_en: To be honest, I'm not really a tidy person. My room tends to get messy, with stuff scattered around the desk and floor, and I don't mind it much. I do tidy up before guests come over, though.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不太爱整洁，房间常常乱糟糟，桌子和地上都是东西；来客人前才收拾。

questions.question_en: Did you use to keep your room tidy as a child?
questions.answer_en: No, not at all, actually. My room was a complete mess when I was a kid, toys and books everywhere. I guess that habit never really changed, because my room is still pretty messy today.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 小时候房间就很乱，玩具书本到处扔；这个习惯到现在没变。

questions.question_en: 待补充
questions.answer_en: Hmm, I'd say it's important up to a point. A tidy space makes it easier to find things and feels more comfortable, but I don't think you need to be obsessive. Honestly, a bit of mess doesn't bother me.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 整洁重要但不用过度；整洁好找东西更舒服，但乱一点也能接受。

topics.title_zh: 音乐
topics.title_en: Music

questions.question_en: Do you prefer sad or happy music?
questions.answer_en: Definitely happy music, no question. Upbeat songs just lift my mood, especially when I'm feeling down or tired. Sad songs are nice once in a while, but they usually bring me down, which is why I skip them.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 更喜欢欢快的歌，能立刻让我心情变好；伤感的歌听了容易低落，所以跳过。

questions.question_en: Does happy music make you feel more excited?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, it really does. When I listen to upbeat songs, my energy just goes up, and I feel much more motivated, even during dull tasks. I actually use happy music to get myself going before studying or exercising.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 会，欢快的歌让我更有能量和动力，学习运动前都会先听来打气。

questions.question_en: 待补充
questions.answer_en: I listen to music all the time, honestly. Mainly during my commute, while studying, and when I'm exercising, since upbeat songs keep me focused and energized. I'd say music is a big part of my daily routine.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 通勤、学习和运动时都听，欢快的歌让我更专注更有劲，音乐是日常的一部分。

topics.title_zh: 爱好
topics.title_en: Hobby

questions.question_en: Do you have any hobbies?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, I do. My main hobby these days is chatting with AI, which sounds a bit unusual, I know. I find it genuinely interesting because the conversations are always different, and I learn new things every time.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 现在的爱好是跟AI聊天，听起来有点特别，但每次对话都不同还能学到新东西。

questions.question_en: Did you have any hobbies when you were a child?
questions.answer_en: Oh yes, definitely. When I was a kid, I was crazy about playing computer games. I'd spend hours after school on them with my friends, and honestly, that passion for computers is what led me to study computer science.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 小时候超爱打电脑游戏，放学就和朋友玩几小时，这份热情也让我选了计算机专业。

questions.question_en: Do you have a hobby that you've had since childhood?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, computer games, absolutely. I started playing them as a kid, and I still enjoy gaming now, though maybe less often. It's funny, but that childhood hobby actually shaped my whole career direction.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 有，电脑游戏从小玩到现在，虽然频率低了，它还影响了我整个职业方向。

questions.question_en: Do you have the same hobbies as your family members?
questions.answer_en: Yeah, partially. My younger brother shares my love for computer games, so we sometimes play together, which is fun. The rest of my family doesn't really game, but we do watch TV together sometimes.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 弟弟和我一样爱打游戏，有时一起玩；其他家人不玩，但会一起看电视。

topics.title_zh: 描述你最喜欢的一座城市
topics.title_en: Describe your favorite city that you have visited

questions.question_en: Describe your favorite city that you have visited
questions.question_zh: 描述你去过的最喜欢的一座城市。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to describe Shenzhen, my home city, which sits right on the southern coast of China, just across the border from Hong Kong. I suppose you could say I've known it my whole life, because I was born there and I've lived there ever since, so it's not really a city I visited, more the city I grew up in. Actually, I still remember exploring different corners of it as a kid, and I keep discovering new parts of it even now.

The thing is, when I think about why Shenzhen means so much to me, a few specific places come to mind. There's Qianhai, where you can walk along the sea and watch the sunset over the bay, and Shenzhen Bay Park, which is great for a relaxing weekend. I also love the area in Bao'an around Bay Glory, which has the tallest ferris wheel in Asia. And of course, the whole city is full of young people chasing opportunities, especially in tech, which gives it that energetic, prosperous feel.

As a result, Shenzhen is my favourite city because it's incredibly convenient, modern and always moving forward. Honestly, with so many job opportunities and such a bustling atmosphere, I can't imagine living anywhere else. All in all, it's more than just a city to me. It's part of who I am.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 我最喜欢的城市是深圳，南方沿海、毗邻香港；我出生在那里长大，前海、深圳湾公园和宝安摩天轮都难忘，生活便利、繁华又充满机会。

questions.question_en: Which is more suitable for young people, urban life or rural life, and which is more suitable for old people?
questions.answer_en: I'd say, generally speaking, urban life suits young people better, while rural life tends to suit older people more. For young people, cities offer jobs, education and a lively social scene, which they need at that stage of life. In my country, for instance, graduates flood into places like Shenzhen for opportunities. That said, it really depends on the individual, because some older people actually enjoy city life, and quite a few young people dream of a quiet countryside lifestyle.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 总体说城市更适合年轻人（机会多、热闹），乡村更适合老人（安静）；但也要看个人性格。

questions.question_en: How do people choose a city to travel to?
questions.answer_en: Well, I think it's a mix of practical and emotional reasons. The main practical ones are budget, distance and time, since most people can't afford a long trip. But emotionally, people are drawn by food, famous sights and, these days, what they see on social media. For example, in my country, a popular series or a trendy photo spot can make a city suddenly famous overnight. Having said that, recommendations from friends probably carry the most weight.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 人们选旅游城市看预算、距离等实际因素，也受美食、景点和社交媒体网红点影响，朋友推荐往往最关键。

questions.question_en: Do you think a tourist city is also a good place to live? Why?
questions.answer_en: Not necessarily, I'd say. A tourist city can be a wonderful place to live because the infrastructure is usually well developed, with good transport, restaurants and entertainment. However, there's a downside, because tourist crowds push up prices, and the streets can get uncomfortably busy during peak seasons. In my country, some coastal tourist towns struggle with that every summer. So on the whole, I think it depends on your tolerance for crowds and your budget, rather than the city itself being good or bad.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 旅游城市基础设施好、吃喝玩乐多，适合居住；但游客多会推高物价、街道拥挤，是否宜居取决于个人承受力。

questions.question_en: Do most people prefer to travel in a modern city or a historical city?
questions.answer_en: I think it largely depends on the person's age and interests, but I'd say young people generally lean towards modern cities, whereas older travellers often prefer historical ones. Modern cities appeal because they offer shopping, nightlife and stunning skylines that look great in photos, like Shanghai or Shenzhen. Historical cities, on the other hand, attract people who want culture and heritage, like Xi'an. That said, more and more people now want a bit of both, mixing modern comfort with history in one trip.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 大体上年轻人偏爱现代城市（购物、夜景、拍照好看），年长者偏爱历史古城；如今更多人想两者兼顾。

questions.question_en: Do you think big cities will continue to attract more people in the future?
questions.question_zh: 你认为未来大城市还会继续吸引更多人吗？
questions.answer_en: I imagine they will, yes, at least in my country. The main reason is that big cities concentrate opportunities, like well-paid jobs and good universities, which small towns simply can't match. For example, Shenzhen grew from a small fishing village into a megacity in just a few decades. Having said that, if remote work keeps expanding, some people may choose cheaper, smaller cities, so the growth might slow down. But I doubt big cities will ever lose their appeal entirely.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 大城市还会继续吸引人，因为机会集中；但如果远程办公普及，增速可能放缓，不过大城市不会失去吸引力。

topics.title_zh: 描述一个无聊的地方
topics.title_en: Describe a boring place

questions.question_en: Describe a boring place
questions.question_zh: 描述一个无聊的地方。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to describe a place I found incredibly boring: the waiting hall of a big hospital in Shenzhen. It's the outpatient building of a hospital near my home, where my grandfather went for a routine check-up last winter.

I went there with my grandfather and my father around eight in the morning, which turned out to be the busiest time of the day. The hall was packed with patients and rows of plastic chairs, with a huge screen showing queue numbers that barely moved.

While we waited, there was really nothing to do. My grandfather and father chatted a bit, but I just sat there scrolling my phone, since the Wi-Fi was too weak for video. Every few minutes I'd glance up at the screen, hoping our number would come up, but it kept jumping by only a few places. Honestly, three hours felt like a whole day.

The reason it's so boring is that nothing ever happens there. The lighting is flat, the air smells of medicine, and people just sit in silence, staring at their phones or at the wall. There's no conversation, no activity, no sense of time passing, so your mind just goes blank. I remember feeling almost relieved when the check-up finally ended, not because it was good news, but simply because we could leave. All in all, it's the kind of place that makes you realise how precious time is, especially when you're wasting it on a hard plastic chair.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 我讲的是深圳一家大医院的门诊候诊大厅，去年冬天陪爷爷去做常规体检。我和爷爷、爸爸早上八点到，大厅挤满病人、一排排塑料椅、叫号屏几乎不动。等待时没什么可做，Wi-Fi 太弱刷不了视频，只能干坐着，三小时像一整天。之所以无聊是因为那里永远什么都不会发生：灯光发白、空气有药味、没人说话，脑子一片空白。检查结束离开时反而松了口气。

questions.question_en: Why do most children think education is boring?
questions.answer_en: I think it's mainly because school education tends to be passive and repetitive. Children sit in class, listen to the teacher, and copy notes, which doesn't engage them the way games or videos do. Another factor is that lessons often feel disconnected from their real interests, which makes it hard for them to see the point. That said, I don't think education itself is boring; it's more about how it's delivered, and I believe more interactive teaching would change that.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 主要因为学校教育偏被动、重复：坐着听讲、抄笔记，不像游戏视频那样吸引人；内容又常和兴趣脱节，看不到意义。但教育本身不无聊，是教学方式的问题，互动式教学能改善。

questions.question_en: Why aren't young people willing to listen to the experiences of older people?
questions.answer_en: There are a couple of reasons. For one thing, young people believe the world has changed so much that old advice no longer applies, especially with technology moving so fast. They also prefer discovering things on their own rather than being told what to do, since making mistakes feels like part of growing up. That said, I think this is short-sighted, because older people's experience of relationships and life choices is still relevant, and many come to appreciate it later.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 年轻人觉得世界变得太快，老经验不再适用，尤其科技时代；也更想自己摸索而不是被说教。但这有点短视，因为人际关系和人生选择上的经验仍然有用，很多年轻人后来才懂得珍惜。

questions.question_en: What can people do when they feel bored?
questions.answer_en: I think the best approach is to treat boredom as a signal to do something meaningful. People can pick up a hobby, go for a walk, or call a friend, which gets them out of the mental rut quickly. Interestingly, some people now deliberately allow themselves to be bored, because it gives their mind space to wander and come up with creative ideas. I'd say boredom itself isn't the enemy; it's what you do with it that matters.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 把无聊当成信号，去做点有意义的事：培养爱好、散步、找朋友聊天，能很快跳出心理低谷。有趣的是现在有人故意让自己无聊，给大脑留白以便产生创意。无聊本身不可怕，怎么利用才重要。

questions.question_en: Why are some teachers' classes boring? Are there any solutions?
questions.answer_en: I'd say boring classes come down to two things: a lack of interaction and relevance. When a teacher just lectures and never asks questions, students' attention drifts, and if the content feels unrelated to their lives, they lose motivation. As for solutions, teachers could introduce discussion, real-world examples, and technology, like quick quizzes or short videos, to break the routine. It takes effort and training, but the payoff is worth it, because an engaged class learns effectively.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 无聊的课通常因为缺互动、内容离生活远。老师只顾讲不提问，学生就走神；内容不相关就失去动力。解决：多讨论、加真实案例、用技术（快速小测、短视频）打破单调。这需要老师投入和培训，但值得，因为投入的课堂学得更有效。

questions.question_en: 待补充
questions.answer_en: To some extent, yes, we get bored more easily these days. With phones and short videos providing instant entertainment, our attention spans have shrunk, so when we're in a situation without stimulation, like waiting in a queue, it feels unbearable. In the past, people were more used to quiet moments and found simple things enjoyable. However, I wouldn't say this is purely negative; it has also pushed people to seek out new experiences and hobbies, which can enrich their lives.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 一定程度是这样。手机和短视频随时提供娱乐，注意力变短，排队这类没刺激的场景就特别难熬；过去的人习惯安静时刻，能从简单事物中找乐趣。但这也不全是坏事，它也推动人们去探索新体验和爱好。
