bullets_zh: 并解释为什么你觉得它很无聊

topics.title_zh: 描述一座你喜欢或不喜欢的高楼
topics.title_en: Describe a tall building you like or dislike

questions.question_en: Describe a tall building you like or dislike
questions.question_zh: 描述一座你喜欢或不喜欢的高楼。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about a tall building I really dislike, the Ping An Finance Centre in Shenzhen, which is where I live. To start with, it's in the heart of the Futian business district, so I walk past it quite often on my way to work. It's mainly used as an office tower, full of banks and financial companies.

In terms of height, it's one of the tallest buildings in the world, around six hundred metres, with more than a hundred floors. As for what it looks like, it's basically a slim glass tower with a pointed top. The whole surface is covered with glass panels that reflect the sky, so it looks elegant from a distance, and at night it's covered in lights, which is quite striking. I have to admit, it's impressive from across the street.

The main reason I dislike it, though, is that I'm afraid of heights, and standing next to a building that tall makes me feel really uneasy. I remember once I went up to the observation deck with friends, and as soon as I looked down from the top, my legs went weak and I had to sit down. Since then, I've avoided going anywhere near the top of a tall building.

So all in all, I can appreciate that it's a modern landmark, but I personally can't enjoy it because of my fear of heights. For me, it's beautiful from the ground, and that's where my comfort ends.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 深圳平安金融中心（约 600 米、100 多层，福田金融区，办公用途）；玻璃幕墙细长塔楼、顶部尖细、夜晚亮灯。因为怕高而不喜欢：曾在观景台向下看腿软，之后避开高楼顶部；虽承认是城市地标，但从地面欣赏就够了。

questions.question_en: Are there many tall buildings in your country?
questions.answer_en: Yes, there are quite a lot, especially in big cities like Shanghai, Shenzhen and Guangzhou. Over the past twenty years, the number of skyscrapers has grown really quickly, mainly because land is scarce and the population keeps rising. In my city, you can see dozens of towers over two hundred metres tall. That said, in smaller cities and rural areas, most buildings are still fairly low.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 大城市（上海、深圳、广州）摩天楼很多；近二十年因土地稀缺、人口增长而快速增多；小城市和农村仍以低层建筑为主。

questions.question_en: What are the differences between those tall buildings in your country?
questions.answer_en: I think the differences mainly come down to function and design. Commercial towers, like the Ping An Finance Centre, are built for offices, so they're tall and slim, packed with glass and steel. Residential buildings, on the other hand, tend to be a bit lower and wider, with balconies and apartment windows. Some older towers have a more traditional look, while newer ones are quite futuristic. So really, the design often reflects what the building is used for.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 差异主要在功能与设计：写字楼高而细、玻璃钢幕墙；住宅楼较矮较宽、带阳台；新老塔楼风格不同；设计往往反映用途。

questions.question_en: Why are different places laid out and designed differently?
questions.answer_en: I believe it's mainly down to geography, history and the local economy. In coastal or mountainous areas, the land itself shapes how a city is planned, so buildings have to fit the landscape. Cities with a long history, like Beijing, keep narrow old streets, whereas newer cities are designed around wide roads and modern districts. The economy also plays a role, because richer cities can afford grander and taller buildings. So ultimately, every city reflects its own conditions.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 主要取决于地理、历史和经济：沿海或山地地形影响布局，古城保留窄老街巷，新城规划宽阔道路，经济实力决定建筑规模与高度。

questions.question_en: Why do some people feel nervous when they visit very tall buildings?
questions.answer_en: I think it's mostly a psychological reaction rather than a real danger. When people stand at a great height, their brain often warns them that something is unsafe, even though they're perfectly safe behind glass. For some people this fear is mild, while for others it's quite strong and hard to control. Having said that, many people actually enjoy the excitement of high places, so I suppose it really depends on the person.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 主要是心理反应：站在高处时大脑发出危险信号，即使实际很安全；恐惧程度因人而异，也有人很享受这种刺激。

topics.title_zh: 描述一座有趣的建筑
topics.title_en: Describe an interesting building

questions.question_en: Describe an interesting building
questions.question_zh: 描述一座有趣的建筑。
questions.answer_en:
OK, I'd like to talk about the Shenzhen Bay Sports Centre, which people here call the "Spring Cocoon". It's in the Nanshan district of my city, right next to Shenzhen Bay Park, so it's quite close to the sea.

As for what it looks like, that's actually the most striking thing about it. The building has a huge oval shape, and the roof is made of white steel frames that curve and cross each other, like a giant silkworm cocoon, which is exactly where the nickname comes from. Inside there's a big open courtyard, and the whole structure is surrounded by glass, so it looks really bright and modern, especially at night when the lights come on.

The main function of the building is as a sports and event venue. It was built for the World University Games back in 2011, and these days it's used for all sorts of things, like swimming competitions, concerts and public sports. People can go there to play basketball or use the gym, and I've actually been there a couple of times to watch events.

I think the reason it's so interesting to me is that it looks nothing like the normal box-shaped buildings around it. I mean, it really stands out as a landmark, and it's a great example of how a modern city can use creative architecture. Every time I pass by, it catches my eye, and I feel a little proud that my city has such a distinctive building.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲的是深圳湾体育中心（春茧），在南山区、紧邻深圳湾公园靠海；外形是白色钢架曲线交织的巨型椭圆，像蚕茧，夜晚灯光下很现代；主要作为体育和活动场馆，2011年大运会建，现在用于游泳比赛、演唱会和公众健身；之所以有趣是因为它和周围方盒子建筑完全不同，是城市地标，每次路过都让人骄傲。

questions.question_en: What types of buildings are popular in your country?
questions.answer_en: Well, I'd say modern high-rise buildings are the most popular in my country at the moment, especially in big cities. Most new residential areas are made up of tall apartment blocks, because land is expensive and cities are crowded. At the same time, there's also a growing interest in traditional architecture, I think, since a lot of people enjoy visiting ancient temples and old streets. So it really depends on where you are, to be honest.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 目前国内最流行的是现代高层建筑，尤其大城市，住宅多为高层公寓楼，因为地贵人多；同时也有对传统建筑的兴趣，很多人爱逛古寺老街；所以因地区而异。

questions.question_en: Is it worth spending a lot of money on the exterior appearance of a building?
questions.answer_en: I think it's worth it up to a point. On the one hand, a nice exterior can make a city more attractive and give people a sense of pride, and famous landmarks often become the symbol of a city. On the other hand, spending too much on the appearance while ignoring the inside could be a waste, because the people using the building care more about comfort and function. So I'd say there should be a balance between the two.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 在一定程度上值得：好看的外立面让城市更有吸引力、带来自豪感，地标还成为城市象征；但过度注重外表而忽略内部是浪费，使用者更在乎舒适和功能；所以应两者平衡。

questions.question_en: Is it more important for a building to look good on the outside or on the inside?
questions.answer_en: To be honest, I think the inside matters more in daily life, because that's where people spend their time. A comfortable interior affects how well people work, study or rest, and nobody really wants to stay in a pretty building that's dark and uncomfortable. Having said that, the outside still matters in a way, since it's the first thing people see and it shapes the image of a neighbourhood. So both matter, but I'd say the inside probably comes first.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 内部更重要，因为那是人们实际待的地方，舒适的室内影响工作学习和休息，没人想待在外表漂亮但阴暗不舒服的楼里；不过外部也有作用，它是第一印象、塑造街区形象；两者都重要但内部优先。

questions.question_en: Why do people like to visit historical sites?
questions.answer_en: I think there are a few reasons. First, historical sites let people connect with the past, I mean, they can imagine how people lived hundreds of years ago, which is a completely different experience from just reading about it in books. Second, these places are often beautiful and unique, so they make great spots for taking photos. Also, visiting them gives people a sense of cultural identity, especially in a country with such a long history.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 有几个原因：历史遗址让人与过去相连，能想象几百年前人们怎么生活，和读书完全不同；这些地方通常美丽独特，适合拍照；还能带来文化认同感，尤其对有悠久历史的国家。

questions.question_en: 待补充
questions.answer_en: I'd say yes, it's reasonable, but it should depend on the situation. If a building needs constant maintenance, then charging a fee makes sense, because repairs cost a lot of money and someone has to cover the cost. However, for public buildings, I think the fee should be kept low, or even free for students and elderly people, so that everyone can enjoy them. Otherwise, these places might only be for tourists who can afford it, which doesn't feel fair.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 合理但要分情况：需要持续维护的建筑收费说得过去，维修很花钱；但对公共建筑应收费低些，对学生老人免费，让所有人都能参观，否则就只服务得起付得起的游客，不公平。

questions.question_en: Is it better to live in a new building or an old one?
questions.answer_en: Generally speaking, new buildings are more practical, I think, because they have better facilities, like lifts, good insulation and modern heating systems, and they're usually safer too. That said, old buildings have their own charm, such as thick walls and high ceilings, and some people really enjoy that traditional style. So for me personally, I'd choose a new building for daily comfort, but I can understand why others prefer the character of older ones.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 通常新建筑更实用：设施更好，有电梯、好的隔热和供暖，也更安全；但老建筑有自己的魅力，比如厚墙高天花板，有人喜欢传统风格；个人会选新建筑图舒适，也理解别人偏爱老建筑的气质。

bullets_zh: 并解释为什么你觉得它有趣

topics.title_zh: 描述一个你觉得非常有趣/出名的城市
topics.title_en: Describe a city that you think is very interesting/famous

questions.question_en: Describe a city that you think is very interesting/famous
questions.question_zh: 描述一个你觉得非常有趣/出名的城市。
questions.answer_en:
The city I'd like to talk about is Shenzhen, which sits right on the southern coast of China, next to Hong Kong. It was a small fishing village just over forty years ago, but now it's one of the country's most prosperous and fastest-growing metropolises.

I first heard about Shenzhen from the news and from my parents, because it's often described as a symbol of China's reform and opening up. Later, when I started paying attention to technology, I realised that many of the tech companies I use every day, like Tencent and DJI, are based there.

What Shenzhen is most famous for is being a tech hub and a special economic zone. Places like Qianhai are packed with skyscrapers and startups, and the whole city seems to be designed around innovation and business. The average age there is quite young, which gives the streets a really energetic, bustling atmosphere.

The reason I find it so interesting is the contrast between its past and its present. I mean, the idea that a fishing village could transform into a world-class city within one generation is almost unbelievable, and it says a lot about how fast China has changed. I think Shenzhen is a place where you can literally see the future being built, and that's why it fascinates me so much.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 深圳，位于中国南部沿海、紧邻香港。四十多年前还是小渔村，如今是最繁华、发展最快的都市之一。从新闻和父母那里听说它，它是改革开放的象征；后来关注科技，发现腾讯、大疆等公司都在这里。它因科技中心和特区出名，前海满是摩天大楼和创业公司，城市年轻、街道热闹。有趣之处在于过去与现在的反差：一代人从渔村变成世界级城市，仿佛能看到未来正在被建造。

questions.question_en: What advantages can tourism bring to a city?
questions.answer_en: I think tourism can bring quite a lot of benefits to a city. For one thing, it creates jobs in hotels, restaurants and transport, which is important for local employment. It also brings in money from outside, so the government can spend more on roads and public facilities. On top of that, tourism builds a better reputation, because visitors spread the word about what they've seen. Having said that, these benefits only appear when tourism is managed properly.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 旅游带来就业（酒店、餐饮、交通）、外部资金（政府可投入公共设施）、提升城市声誉。但前提是管理得当。

questions.question_en: Why do some young people like to live in cities?
questions.answer_en: Well, there are a few main reasons. Firstly, cities offer far more job opportunities, especially in tech and finance, which young people find attractive. Secondly, the lifestyle suits them better. I mean, there are countless cafes, gyms and events, so it's easier to make friends and have fun. Another factor is convenience, since everything is close by. City life does come with high rents and stress, but for most young people, the chance of a better future outweighs those drawbacks.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 工作机会多（科技、金融）、生活方式丰富（咖啡馆、健身房、活动）、生活便利。虽有高房租和压力，但年轻人认为发展机会更重要。

questions.question_en: Do most elderly people live in the city or in the countryside?
questions.answer_en: In China, I'd say the majority of elderly people live in the countryside, because many of them grew up there and feel more at home among familiar neighbours. However, a growing number are moving to cities, especially when their children settle there and need help with childcare, so the picture is changing. Generally speaking, though, I think the countryside is still where most older people spend their retirement, because the pace of life is slower and the air is cleaner.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 多数老人住在农村（熟悉的环境、邻里），但越来越多老人搬去城市帮子女带孩子。总体而言农村仍是多数老人养老之地，节奏慢、空气好。

questions.question_en: Do you think well-developed tourism will have negative effects on local people?
questions.answer_en: To be honest, I think it can, even though tourism is generally positive. When a city becomes too popular, housing prices and the cost of daily goods tend to rise, which makes life harder for residents. Crowded streets and attractions can also be stressful for nearby residents. That said, whether the effect is negative depends on how the city manages it. If the government controls the number of visitors and protects public spaces, the downsides can be kept under control.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 过度旅游会推高房价和物价、让居民生活更累。但影响好坏取决于管理：若政府控制游客数量、保护公共空间，负面影响可控。

questions.question_en: What are the benefits of urbanization?
questions.answer_en: Urbanization brings several clear benefits. For a start, it concentrates resources, so hospitals, schools and transport networks can serve far more people efficiently. It also creates a stronger economy, because businesses can share workers, suppliers and ideas in one place. In addition, city life tends to offer more chances for education and self-improvement, which is why so many young people move there. Of course, rapid urbanization needs to be planned carefully, otherwise it can lead to housing problems and pollution.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 城市化集中资源（医院、学校、交通效率更高）、促进经济（共享人才与供应链）、提供更多教育机会。但需合理规划，否则引发住房和污染问题。

questions.question_en: Do you think the big cities in China today will become even larger in the future?
questions.answer_en: I imagine some of them will keep growing, though not as quickly as before. On the one hand, big cities still attract young people with better jobs, so the population will likely keep rising for a while. On the other hand, the government has been encouraging development in smaller cities, and remote working makes it possible to live elsewhere, which could slow the growth. The largest cities might expand further, but medium-sized cities will see the most growth.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 大城市短期内仍会增长（吸引年轻人），但政府鼓励中小城市发展、远程办公普及会减缓增速。未来超大城继续扩张，但增长主力可能是中型城市。

topics.title_zh: 描述一个你游览得很开心的城市
topics.title_en: Describe a city you enjoyed visiting

questions.question_en: Describe a city you enjoyed visiting
questions.question_zh: 描述一个你游览得很开心的城市。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about Nanning, which is the capital city of Guangxi province in the south of China. I went there with my girlfriend about a year ago, during a long holiday, and we stayed for roughly four days.

Actually, the trip was her idea. She had visited Nanning before and kept saying how relaxed the city felt, so we decided to spend the break there instead of staying in Shenzhen, where we both live.

While we were there, we did quite a lot. On the first day, we climbed Qingxiu Mountain, which was a bit tiring, but the view from the top over the whole city made it worthwhile. We also walked around Guangxi University, and I remember it felt much quieter and greener than the campuses back home. In the evenings, we went to the night market and tried lots of local dishes, like laoyou noodles, which is a famous rice noodle dish from Nanning. To be honest, I ate way too much, but I have no regrets.

The reason I enjoyed it so much is that the whole trip was genuinely relaxing. The city has a slower pace of life than Shenzhen, with trees and parks everywhere, and my girlfriend was really happy, which made me happy too. Looking back, it wasn't a fancy trip, just good food, good company and a change of scenery. So that's why Nanning is a city I really enjoyed visiting.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 南宁是广西首府，位于中国南部；一年前和女朋友去旅游，待了大约四天。是女朋友提议的，她去过南宁说很放松。活动：爬青秀山看全城景色、逛广西大学、晚上去夜市吃老友粉等本地美食。喜欢的原因：节奏比深圳慢、绿化多、女朋友开心、美食好吃，换个环境很放松。

questions.question_en: What kinds of facilities do big cities have?
questions.answer_en: Big cities usually offer a wide range of facilities. To start with, there's the transport system, including the metro, buses and high-speed rail, which make getting around convenient. Then there are shopping malls, hospitals, schools and universities, which cover people's daily needs. Most cities also have cultural facilities, such as museums, libraries and parks, which improve quality of life. I think it's this combination that makes a city feel comfortable to live in.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 大城市设施齐全：交通（地铁/公交/高铁）、商场、医院、学校，还有博物馆、图书馆、公园等文化设施；正是这些组合让城市生活方便舒适。

questions.question_en: Do you think modern cities are suitable for young people or old people?
questions.answer_en: I'd say modern cities suit young people more, at least in most cases. Young people benefit from the job opportunities and the overall convenience. Older people, on the other hand, often prefer quieter surroundings and stronger community ties, which cities tend to lack. That said, it depends on the individual. Some elderly people appreciate easy access to hospitals and shops. So on balance, modern cities work better for the young, though they can suit older people too.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 现代城市更适合年轻人：就业机会多、生活便利；老人更偏好安静和社区感，但看个人，有的老人也享受就医购物的便利。总体偏年轻人。

questions.question_en: Before you travel to a city, what factors would you consider?
questions.answer_en: For me, a few things matter. First, the budget, because accommodation and transport can be expensive, so I usually set a rough limit before I go. Then the weather, since I don't enjoy sightseeing in extreme heat or heavy rain. And perhaps most importantly, what the city has to offer, like food, culture or natural scenery, because I want the trip to feel worthwhile. When I planned my trip to Nanning, the local food was the biggest draw for me.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 出行前考虑三点：预算（吃住行可能贵）、天气（不喜欢酷热暴雨）、城市特色（美食/文化/自然风光）；去南宁就是被美食吸引的。

questions.question_en: What are the disadvantages of living in a very famous city?
questions.answer_en: There are quite a few, actually. The most obvious one is the cost of living, since famous cities usually have expensive housing and high daily expenses, which puts pressure on ordinary people. Another downside is overcrowding, especially at tourist attractions, which makes them hard to enjoy during peak seasons. I also think there's a subtler problem: famous cities can become over-commercialised and lose their local character. So while they're exciting to visit, living there day to day can be exhausting.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 著名城市缺点：生活成本高（房价贵）、拥挤（旅游旺季难享受）、过度商业化导致本地特色流失；适合旅游但长期居住很累。

questions.question_en: Do you prefer to visit well-developed cities or cities with a long history?
questions.answer_en: I'd probably choose cities with a long history, though it depends on the mood I'm in. Developed cities can feel a bit similar, with the same malls and skyscrapers, whereas historic cities offer something unique, like old streets, traditional food and their stories. Having said that, developed cities are more comfortable to travel in, with better transport and hotels. So I lean towards historic cities for the experience, though I appreciate the convenience of modern ones too.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 更倾向历史名城：有古街、传统美食和故事；发达城市虽方便但千篇一律。视心情而定，两者都欣赏。

questions.question_en: For those who live in cities, is it because they want to or have to?
questions.answer_en: I think it's a mix, but for many people it's more of a necessity. The main reason is work, because most job opportunities are concentrated in cities, which means people have to move there to make a living. Having said that, once they've settled in, many of them come to enjoy it, thanks to the convenience and the lifestyle. So I'd say people mostly move to cities because they have to, but many end up staying because they want to.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 多数人搬进城市是不得不（工作机会集中在城市），但定居后很多人真正喜欢上城市生活；先因为需要，后因为想要。

topics.title_zh: 描述你童年时期的一个朋友
topics.title_en: Describe a friend from your childhood

questions.question_en: Describe a friend from your childhood
questions.question_zh: 描述你童年时期的一个朋友。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about my childhood friend Zeng, who was my classmate in primary school. We were in the same class from the first grade, and we actually sat next to each other for a couple of years, so we got to know each other really well.

We met at school, in our classroom, and honestly, we became friends almost immediately. I remember he was one of the first people I talked to on my very first day, and after that we were basically inseparable.

As for what we did together, we spent most of our free time playing games in the schoolyard. Our favourites were tag and hide-and-seek, and we'd run around until we were completely out of breath. Sometimes we'd also trade snacks at lunch, which sounds silly now, but it felt like a big deal back then.

The reason I liked him so much was that he was just so much fun to be around. He always came up with new games and new ways to make me laugh, and he never made me feel left out. Looking back, I think he taught me how to enjoy the simple things in life.

Unfortunately, we lost contact after we finished primary school, because we went to different middle schools. I still think about those days sometimes, and I'm grateful for the friendship we had.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲童年好友 zeng，小学同班同桌，常一起玩抓人和捉迷藏；他有趣、从不让我落单，教会我享受简单快乐；小学毕业后去了不同中学就失去联系。

questions.question_en: Do you still keep in touch with your friends from childhood? Why or why not?
questions.answer_en: To be honest, I don't keep in touch with most of my childhood friends, and I think that's quite common. The main reason is that we went to different schools and gradually drifted apart, since we no longer shared the same daily life. I mean, when you're a child, friendship is built on being together every day, so once that disappears, it's hard to maintain the connection.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不常联系，因为去了不同学校、生活不再交集，慢慢疏远；孩子的友谊靠天天在一起维系。

questions.question_en: How important is childhood friendship to children?
questions.answer_en: I'd say childhood friendship is extremely important, probably more than most people realise. For one thing, it's how children learn social skills like sharing, cooperating and resolving conflicts. On top of that, having a close friend gives children a sense of security and belonging, which supports their emotional development. So I believe these early friendships shape how children relate to others later in life.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 童年友谊极其重要：孩子借此学会分享、合作、解决冲突，朋友带来安全感和归属感，影响日后的人际关系。

questions.question_en: What do you think of communicating via social media?
questions.answer_en: From my perspective, social media has made communication much more convenient, since you can stay in touch with people across any distance. That said, I think it also has downsides, because messages can easily be misunderstood without tone of voice or facial expressions. So while it's a useful tool, I don't think it can fully replace the warmth of talking to someone in person.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 社交媒体让沟通更方便、能跨距离联系；但缺少语气和表情容易误解，无法完全替代当面交流的温暖。

questions.question_en: Do you think online communication through social media will replace face-to-face communication?
questions.answer_en: I don't think it will completely replace face-to-face communication, although it will probably keep growing. The reason is that people naturally crave real human contact, and things like body language and eye contact simply can't be transmitted online. For important moments, like weddings or funerals, people will always want to be physically present. So I'd say online communication will complement, rather than replace, in-person interaction.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不会完全取代面对面交流：人天生渴望真实接触，肢体语言和眼神无法线上传递，重要场合人们仍会到场；线上是补充而非替代。

questions.question_en: What's the difference between having younger friends and older friends?
questions.answer_en: Generally speaking, younger friends tend to be more energetic and open to new ideas, whereas older friends usually offer more experience and practical advice. For example, an older friend might warn you about mistakes they've already made, while a younger friend is more likely to join you in trying something new. I think both are valuable, but they serve quite different purposes in your life.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 年轻朋友更有活力、乐于尝试新事物；年长朋友经验丰富、能给出实用建议；两者各有价值、作用不同。

questions.question_en: Has technology changed people's friendships? How?
questions.answer_en: Yes, technology has changed friendships in quite significant ways. For one thing, it's now possible to maintain friendships across long distances, which wasn't easy before. However, I think the quality of interaction has changed too, because people often communicate through short messages rather than deep conversations. So friendships have become easier to maintain, but perhaps a bit shallower in some cases.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 科技大幅改变了友谊：能跨距离维系友情，但交流常变成短消息而非深入对话，友谊更容易维持却可能更浅。

topics.title_zh: 描述你认识的一个做生意成功的人
topics.title_en: Describe a person you know who has a successful business

questions.question_en: Describe a person you know who has a successful business
questions.question_zh: 描述你认识的一个做生意成功的人。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about my uncle, my mother's sister's husband, who runs a very successful business. I've known him my whole life, since he's part of the family, and we see him regularly at family gatherings.

As for how I got to know him, well, he's been around since I was a child, so I've always known him as a warm and hardworking person. I remember he used to visit our home during festivals, and he always seemed busy, often taking phone calls about work even during dinner.

To be honest, I don't know all the details of his business, but I know he started it from scratch about fifteen years ago, with just a small team. Over the years, it has grown into a company that employs dozens of people, and he now owns several branches.

The reason I think his business is successful is that it has survived and grown for so long, which is not easy in such a competitive market. On top of that, he's clearly earned the trust of his customers, because his company keeps getting repeat orders.

Looking back, I really admire his determination. He started with almost nothing and built something solid through years of hard work, and that's what I find most impressive about him.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲姨丈，从小认识、逢年过节常见面；约十五年前白手起家，如今公司雇了几十人、开了多家分店；成功在于经营多年不倒、赢得客户信任、有回头客，令人佩服他的坚持。

questions.question_en: Why do some people start their own business?
questions.answer_en: There are several reasons why people start their own business. Firstly, many people want independence, because they're tired of working for someone else and want to control their own schedule. Secondly, some are attracted by the potential for higher income, since a successful business can earn far more than a salary. Of course, there's also the desire to pursue a personal passion, which can be a strong motivator.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 创业原因多样：想要独立自主、不受雇于人；追求更高收入；以及想实现个人热情。

questions.question_en: Should governments provide financial support to start-ups?
questions.answer_en: I think governments should provide some financial support to start-ups, although it needs to be done carefully. The main reason is that new businesses create jobs and drive innovation, which benefits the whole economy. However, support shouldn't be given blindly, because many start-ups fail, and public money needs to be used wisely. So I'd say targeted support, like tax breaks or low-interest loans, is the best approach.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 政府应提供一定支持但要谨慎：新企业创造就业、推动创新，但很多会失败，公共资金要花得明智；定向支持如减税、低息贷款最合适。

questions.question_en: Do most people prefer shopping at big stores or small stores?
questions.answer_en: Generally speaking, I think most people prefer big stores for everyday shopping, mainly because they offer lower prices and a wider range of products. That said, small stores still have their appeal, especially for things like fresh food or personalised service, where you can build a relationship with the owner. So I'd say it depends on what people are buying, but for convenience, big stores usually win.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 日常购物多数人偏好大店，价格低、选择多；但小店在生鲜和个性化服务上有优势；取决于买什么，论便利大店通常胜出。

questions.question_en: What makes a business successful?
questions.answer_en: In my view, several factors contribute to a successful business. Firstly, understanding what customers actually need is essential, because a business that solves a real problem will always find buyers. Secondly, good management matters a lot, since even a great product can fail without proper planning and financial control. On top of that, I think adaptability is crucial, because markets change quickly, and businesses that can't adjust tend to fall behind.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 成功要素：真正理解客户需求、解决实际问题；良好管理、合理规划与财务控制；以及适应市场变化的灵活性。

questions.question_en: What makes a business fail?
questions.answer_en: I think the most common reason businesses fail is poor financial management, because many owners run out of cash before their business becomes profitable. Another factor is failing to adapt, since consumer habits change quickly, and a business that ignores new trends will lose customers. Also, some businesses fail simply because there isn't enough demand for what they offer, no matter how hard the owners work.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 失败主因：财务管理不善、盈利前就耗尽资金；不能适应消费习惯变化；以及产品本身缺乏足够需求。

topics.title_zh: 描述一个喜欢在家里或花园种植物的人
topics.title_en: Describe a person who loves to grow plants

questions.question_en: Describe a person who loves to grow plants (e.g. vegetables, flowers) at home or in the garden
questions.question_zh: 描述一个喜欢在家里或花园种植物(蔬菜、花等)的人。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about my grandfather, who lives with us and is completely obsessed with growing plants. He's in his seventies and retired a few years ago, so he spends most of his time on the balcony, tending to his little vegetable garden.

As for what he grows, it's mostly everyday vegetables: greens, scallions and a few chili pepper plants. He keeps them in foam boxes, which he lines up along the balcony railing, and they've actually grown into quite a lush little patch over the years.

In terms of how he grows them, he's surprisingly methodical about it. Every morning, without fail, he waters each box and checks the leaves for pests, and he often talks to himself about which plants need more sun. He also saves seeds from one season to the next, which I find quite clever. The scallions we use for cooking at home are basically all from his boxes, and he's always proud to tell us how well the latest crop is doing.

The reason he loves it so much, I think, is that it gives him a sense of purpose after retirement. He says home-grown vegetables are safer to eat, since he knows exactly what goes into them, and honestly, it's become his favourite pastime. Watching him, I can see that caring for those plants keeps him active and happy, and that's why I think it means so much to him.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲的是我爷爷，退休后整天在阳台用泡沫箱种菜。种的是青菜、小葱和几棵辣椒，泡沫箱沿阳台栏杆排成一排。他每天早上雷打不动地浇水、检查叶子有没有虫，还会留种子。家里炒菜用的葱基本都是他种的，他总得意地跟我们说这茬长得多好。他爱种菜是因为退休后有了寄托，觉得自家种的菜吃着放心，也成了他最喜欢的消遣。

questions.question_en: What are the advantages of growing vegetables or flowers at home?
questions.answer_en: I think there are several clear advantages. For one thing, it gives people access to fresh, chemical-free produce, which is healthier than what you often find in supermarkets. It's also a great way to relax, since caring for plants takes your mind off daily stress. On top of that, it saves money in the long run, and it makes the home look more lively and pleasant. So overall, it's a hobby that benefits both your health and your mood.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 好处很多：能吃到新鲜无农药的菜，比超市的更健康；照顾植物还能放松减压；长期看省钱，家里也更有生气。总之对健康和心情都有益。

questions.question_en: Do many people grow vegetables or flowers at home in your country?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I'd say it's becoming quite common, especially among older people. In my country, many retired people grow vegetables on their balconies or rooftops, partly because they enjoy it and partly because they trust home-grown food more. Younger people tend to grow flowers or succulents instead, since they're easier to look after and look nice indoors. So while the trend is widespread, the style of growing differs a lot between generations.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 越来越普遍，尤其老年人。很多退休老人在阳台或屋顶种菜，既因为喜欢也因为更信任自家种的菜。年轻人则更爱种花或多肉，好养又好看。趋势很广，但两代人的种法差别很大。

questions.question_en: Is it easy to grow plants at home?
questions.answer_en: It depends on the plant, to be honest. Some plants, like succulents and herbs, are very forgiving and basically grow themselves, so they're perfect for beginners. Others, like vegetables, need more attention, the right amount of sunlight and regular watering, which can be tricky in an apartment. That said, with a bit of research and patience, most people can manage it. I'd say the main challenge is consistency, since plants need care every day, not just when you remember.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 看种什么。多肉、香草这类很好养，基本不用管，适合新手；蔬菜则需要光照和定期浇水，在公寓里有点麻烦。但只要有点研究和耐心，大多数人都能种好。最大的挑战是坚持，植物需要每天照顾。

questions.question_en: Why do people like to grow plants?
questions.answer_en: I think there are a few reasons. For many, it's a way to relax and slow down, since gardening is a calm, hands-on activity that takes your mind off screens and stress. For others, it's about the satisfaction of watching something you planted grow and thrive, which gives a real sense of achievement. And for some, especially older people, it's simply a routine that keeps them busy and gives their day structure. So the appeal is both emotional and practical.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 原因有几个：很多人把它当放松方式，种花种菜是安静的手工活动，能让人远离屏幕和压力；也有人享受看着自己种的东西长大的成就感；对老人来说，它还是让日子有规律的日常。吸引力既有情感层面也有实用层面。

questions.question_en: Why do some people prefer to grow their own fruits and vegetables instead of buying them from the market?
questions.answer_en: I think the main reason is trust in food safety. Many people worry about pesticides and preservatives in store-bought produce, so growing their own gives them full control over what they eat. There's also the freshness factor, since you can pick vegetables right before cooking, which tastes noticeably better. On top of that, some people simply enjoy the process and the sense of self-sufficiency it brings. So it's a mix of health concerns and personal satisfaction.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 主要是对食品安全的信任问题。很多人担心买来的菜有农药和防腐剂，自己种就能完全掌控吃进嘴里的东西；而且现摘现做更新鲜更好吃；还有人享受这个过程和自给自足的感觉。是健康顾虑加个人满足感的结合。

questions.question_en: Do you think choosing a college major is closely related to a future career?
questions.answer_en: To some extent, yes, but it's not a fixed link. For professional fields like medicine or law, the major directly determines the career path, since you need specific qualifications. However, for many other subjects, especially in the humanities, graduates often end up in completely different jobs, because employers care more about skills and experience than the exact major. So I'd say a major opens doors, but it doesn't lock you in, and lifelong learning matters just as much.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 有一定关系，但不是固定联系。医学、法律这类专业领域，专业直接决定职业路径，因为需要特定资格；但很多其他专业，尤其文科，毕业生常常做完全不同的工作，因为雇主更看重技能和经验而不是具体专业。所以专业是开门，不是锁门，终身学习同样重要。

topics.title_zh: 描述一个你认识的想从事医疗行业的人
topics.title_en: Describe a person you know who would like to choose a career in the medical field

questions.question_en: Describe a person you know who would like to choose a career in the medical field (e.g. a doctor, a nurse)
questions.question_zh: 描述一个你认识的想从事医疗行业(医生、护士等)的人。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about my younger sister, who has decided she wants to build a career in the medical field. She's a few years younger than me, and we've lived together our whole lives, so I know her really well.

As for when she started thinking about it, I'd say it was around middle school. I remember she got really interested in biology classes, and she often talked about how much she admired the nurses she saw in hospital dramas and in real life. From then on, the idea just stuck with her.

What she'd like to do specifically is become a nurse. She's told me she prefers nursing over being a doctor, because it involves more direct contact with patients, which suits her caring personality. She's currently working hard on her science subjects to get into a good nursing programme, and she even volunteers at a community health centre during holidays.

The reason she wants this career, I think, is that she genuinely enjoys helping people. She's always been the kind of person who looks after others, whether it's our family or her friends, and she says nursing lets her turn that instinct into a profession. She also values the stability of the job, since healthcare is always in demand. Looking at her, I can see she's found something she truly believes in, and I'm really proud of her for that.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲的是我妹妹，她决定从事医疗行业。她比我小几岁，我们从小一起长大。她大概初中时开始有这个想法，那时她特别喜欢生物课，常说自己很佩服电视剧和现实里见到的护士，这个念头就一直留了下来。她想当护士，因为觉得护士和病人接触更多，适合她爱照顾人的性格。她正在努力学理科想考护理专业，假期还会去社区健康中心做志愿者。她选这行是因为真心喜欢帮助别人，也看重这行稳定、社会一直需要。我为她感到骄傲。

questions.question_en: Do you think being a doctor is easy or difficult?
questions.answer_en: I'd say it's one of the most difficult professions, without a doubt. For one thing, the training takes years, and the workload is extremely heavy, with long shifts and constant pressure. Doctors also carry a huge responsibility, since a single mistake can seriously affect a patient's life. On top of that, they have to keep learning throughout their careers, because medicine is always advancing. So while it's a respected and rewarding job, it demands a lot of sacrifice.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 医生绝对是最难的职业之一：培训要很多年，工作强度大、轮班长、压力大；责任也重，一个失误就可能严重影响病人生命；而且医学不断进步，要终身学习。虽然受人尊敬、回报高，但牺牲也很大。

questions.question_en: Do you think learning biology is interesting for children?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think it can be, if it's taught in the right way. Children are naturally curious about living things, like animals, plants and their own bodies, so biology connects well with their everyday experience. When lessons involve experiments or real examples, kids tend to find it fascinating. That said, if it's taught purely from textbooks with lots of memorisation, it can quickly become boring. So the subject itself is interesting, but the teaching method makes all the difference.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 可以很有趣，关键看怎么教。孩子天生对动物、植物、自己的身体好奇，生物和日常生活联系紧密；有实验和真实例子时孩子会觉得着迷。但如果只照课本背知识点，很快就会无聊。所以学科本身有趣，教学方式决定一切。

questions.question_en: 待补充
questions.answer_en: I think there are several reasons. For many, it's a genuine desire to help others, since caring for sick people gives the work real meaning. For others, it's the stability and respect that come with the profession, since medical jobs are always needed and well regarded in society. Some are also drawn to the intellectual challenge, because medicine requires constant learning and problem-solving. So the motivation is usually a combination of compassion, practicality and ambition.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 原因有几个：很多人是真心想帮助别人，照顾病人让工作有意义；也有人看重这行的稳定和受尊重，医疗岗位社会永远需要；还有人被智力挑战吸引，医学需要不断学习和解决问题。动机通常是同情心、现实考量和抱负的结合。

topics.title_zh: 描述一个总做计划且擅长规划的人
topics.title_en: Describe a person who makes plans a lot and is good at planning

questions.question_en: Describe a person who makes plans a lot and is good at planning
questions.question_zh: 描述一个总做计划且擅长规划的人。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about my girlfriend, who is probably the most organised person I've ever met. She's a university student like me, and we've been together for about two years now.

As for how I knew her, we actually met in the same class during our first year of university. We sat next to each other, started chatting about assignments, and eventually became close. It didn't take long for me to notice how disciplined she was with her studies.

In terms of what plans she makes, she plans almost everything. She keeps a detailed study schedule, breaking each semester into weekly goals, and she always knows exactly what she needs to finish each day. Before exams, she maps out a revision timetable weeks in advance, and she even plans her weekends, balancing study with rest. Thanks to that habit, she's won scholarships two years in a row, which I think says a lot about her.

The reason I admire her so much is that her planning isn't rigid or stressful, it actually gives her freedom. Because she knows what needs to be done, she never panics at the last minute, and she still finds time to relax. Watching her, I've learned that good planning isn't about controlling every minute, it's about staying calm and in control. Honestly, she's inspired me to be more organised myself, and I'm grateful to have her as a role model.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲的是我女朋友，她是我见过最有条理的人。我们大一同班认识的，坐邻座聊作业慢慢熟起来。她几乎什么都做计划：把每学期拆成每周目标，每天该完成什么清清楚楚；考前几周就排好复习表，连周末都规划好学习和休息。靠这个习惯她连续两年拿奖学金。我佩服她是因为她的计划不僵化也不累人，反而给她自由，从不临时慌乱，还有时间放松。她让我学会有条理，我很感激有她这个榜样。

questions.question_en: Do you think it's important to plan ahead?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think it's very important, though the level of detail can vary. Planning ahead helps people use their time efficiently and reduces stress, because you always know what's coming next. It also makes goals more achievable, since a big task becomes manageable when it's broken into smaller steps. That said, I don't think every minute needs to be planned, since being too rigid can make life feel mechanical. So the key is to plan enough to stay organised, but stay flexible.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 非常重要，但详细程度可以不同。提前计划能高效利用时间、减少压力，因为你知道接下来要做什么；把大任务拆成小步骤也更容易达成。但不必每分钟都规划，太死板会让生活变得机械。关键是计划到有条理，同时保持灵活。

questions.question_en: What activities do we need to plan ahead?
questions.answer_en: I'd say anything that involves limited resources or high stakes. For example, travel definitely needs planning, since you have to book transport and accommodation in advance. Big purchases, like buying a house or a car, also require long-term financial planning. On top of that, career and education decisions need careful thought, because they shape your future for years. Even everyday things, like cooking for a family, benefit from a bit of planning. So basically, the more costly or complex the activity, the more planning it needs.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 凡是涉及有限资源或高风险的事都需要计划。比如旅行必须提前订交通和住宿；买房买车这类大额消费需要长期财务规划；职业和教育决定影响未来很多年，更要慎重考虑；就连给家人做饭这类日常事，有点计划也更好。总之越花钱越复杂的事越需要计划。

questions.question_en: Do you think children should plan their future careers?
questions.answer_en: I think it's good for children to have a general sense of direction, but not to be locked into a specific career too early. At a young age, interests change quickly, so a rigid plan could limit their exploration. That said, exposing them to different fields and helping them understand their strengths is valuable, since it gives them a starting point. I'd say the ideal approach is to encourage curiosity and let the plan develop gradually, rather than forcing a decision in childhood.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 孩子应该有大方向，但不宜过早锁定具体职业。小时候兴趣变得快，死板的计划会限制探索。不过让他们接触不同领域、了解自己的长处很有价值，能给他们一个起点。理想做法是鼓励好奇心，让计划慢慢成形，而不是小时候就逼着做决定。

questions.question_en: Should children ask their teachers or parents for advice when making plans?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think they should, because adults have experience that children simply don't have yet. Teachers understand a child's academic strengths and can suggest suitable directions, while parents know their child's personality and can offer practical guidance. That said, the final decision should still be the child's, since a plan only works if the person actually wants to follow it. So adults should act as advisors, not decision-makers, and children should learn to weigh advice against their own interests.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 应该问，因为大人有孩子没有的经验。老师了解孩子的学业强项，能建议合适的方向；父母了解孩子的性格，能给出实际指导。但最终决定权还是应该在孩子手里，因为计划只有本人愿意执行才有效。大人应该当顾问而不是决策者，孩子要学会权衡建议和自己的兴趣。

questions.question_en: Is making study plans popular among young people?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I'd say it's quite popular these days, especially among students. With so much competition, many young people feel they need to organise their time carefully to keep up, so study plans have become a common habit. Apps and online tools have also made planning easier, which encourages more people to try it. That said, I think many plans are made but not strictly followed, since young people often get distracted. So it's popular in theory, but sticking to the plan is the real challenge.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 现在挺流行的，尤其学生。竞争激烈，很多年轻人觉得必须好好安排时间才能跟上，做学习计划成了常见习惯；各种 App 和在线工具也让规划更容易。但我觉得很多人是做了计划却没严格执行，年轻人容易分心。所以理论上流行，坚持执行才是真正的挑战。

questions.question_en: 待补充
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think it's an excellent hobby for elderly people. For one thing, it gives them gentle daily exercise and a reason to move around, which is good for their health. It also provides a sense of purpose and routine after retirement, which can prevent loneliness and boredom. On top of that, watching plants grow is genuinely rewarding, and it gives them something to share with their families. So I'd say it's one of the most beneficial hobbies for older people.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 对老人来说是非常好的爱好：每天有轻量的活动量，对身体好；退休后有了寄托和规律，能避免孤独无聊；看着植物长大很有成就感，还能和家人分享。可以说是最适合老人的爱好之一。

topics.title_zh: 描述一个喜欢画画的小孩
topics.title_en: Describe a child who loves drawing/painting

questions.question_en: Describe a child who loves drawing/painting
questions.question_zh: 描述一个喜欢画画/绘画的小孩。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about my little cousin, who is about six years old now. She's my aunt's daughter, and she absolutely loves drawing, which is why she came to mind right away.

Actually, I've known her since she was born, but I really noticed her passion for drawing about two years ago, when she started kindergarten. Her mum told me she would come home and spend ages at the table with her crayons, drawing characters from the cartoons she watches.

As for how often she draws, it's basically every day. Whenever I visit my aunt's place, she's usually sitting there with a pile of paper, and she'll happily show me her latest pictures. She mostly draws anime characters and cartoon versions of our family, which I find really cute.

The reason I think she genuinely loves drawing is that she gets completely absorbed in it. When she's drawing, she goes quiet and focused, which is rare for a kid her age, since she's normally full of energy and running around. She doesn't draw because anyone tells her to, she just does it for fun, and she's always proud to show off the result. Looking back, I think that kind of pure enjoyment is what real passion looks like, and I hope she keeps it as she grows up.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲的是六岁的表妹，阿姨的女儿，特别喜欢画画。两年前上幼儿园时注意到她的热情，每天回家都用蜡笔画动画片里的角色。她几乎天天画，去阿姨家总能看到她趴桌上画，画动画角色和家人的卡通形象。觉得她真爱画画是因为她画的时候特别专注安静，没人逼她，纯粹为了开心，画完还骄傲地展示。

questions.question_en: What is the right age for a child to learn drawing?
questions.answer_en: I'd say there isn't really a fixed right age, but around four or five seems natural. At that age, children have enough control over their hands to hold a crayon properly, and they're curious about everything. I don't think formal classes are necessary either, since giving them paper and pencils at home is enough to get started. The key is that they enjoy it, rather than learning it as a serious skill.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 没有固定年龄，四五岁比较自然，那时手部控制力够、好奇心强；不需要正式培训班，家里给纸笔就行，关键是孩子享受画画本身。

questions.question_en: Why do most children draw more often than adults do?
questions.answer_en: I think the main reason is that children draw purely for fun, without worrying about whether the result looks good. They just put whatever is in their imagination onto paper, and they're happy with it. Adults, on the other hand, tend to judge their own work, comparing it with professional art, so they feel discouraged and stop. In other words, children draw because they enjoy the process, while adults are too concerned with the outcome.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 孩子画画纯粹为了好玩，不担心画得好不好看，想到什么画什么就很满足；大人反而会评判自己的作品、跟专业画作比较，容易受挫放弃。孩子享受过程，大人太在意结果。

questions.question_en: Why do some people visit galleries or museums instead of viewing artworks online?
questions.answer_en: I think it's because seeing art in person is a completely different experience. In a gallery, you can see the actual size, the texture of the paint and the details that photos simply can't capture. There's also the atmosphere, the quiet rooms and the lighting, which help you focus on the work. Online, you tend to scroll past images quickly, whereas in a museum you naturally slow down and really look.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 现场看画是完全不同的体验：能看到真实尺寸、颜料质感和照片拍不出的细节；还有安静的房间和灯光营造的氛围，让人专注。网上看画容易快速划过，在博物馆里会自然慢下来认真看。

questions.question_en: Do you think galleries and museums should be free of charge?
questions.answer_en: I'd say yes, at least for the main collections. Museums play an educational role, so charging a high entrance fee would stop many people, especially students and low-income families, from visiting. That said, I think it's reasonable for special exhibitions to charge a fee, since they cost a lot to organise. On balance, keeping the core collections free encourages more people to engage with art and culture.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 基本同意免费，至少常设展应该免费，因为博物馆有教育功能，高票价会挡住学生和低收入家庭；但特展收费合理，因为布展成本高。总体常设展免费能鼓励更多人接触艺术文化。

questions.question_en: How do artworks inspire people?
questions.answer_en: Artworks can inspire people in several ways. For one thing, they show us different perspectives, helping us see familiar things in a new light. They also express emotions that are hard to put into words, which can make people feel understood. And for some, a powerful piece of art sparks creativity, encouraging them to try making something themselves. So inspiration often comes from the way art opens up new ways of thinking.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 艺术作品从几个方面启发人：展示不同视角让人重新看待熟悉的事物；表达难以言说的情感让人感到被理解；强大的作品还能激发创造力，鼓励人自己动手创作。

questions.question_en: What are the differences between reading a book and visiting a museum?
questions.answer_en: I think the main difference is that reading is a private, imaginative experience, while visiting a museum is physical and social. When you read, you build the scenes in your own mind, and you can go at your own pace. In a museum, you see real objects with your own eyes, which is more direct, and you often go with other people, discussing what you see. So books engage your imagination, whereas museums engage your senses.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 主要区别：读书是私人的、靠想象力的体验，场景在脑中构建、节奏自己掌握；逛博物馆是实体的、社交的体验，亲眼看到真实物品更直接，还常和别人一起边看边讨论。书激发想象，博物馆调动感官。

topics.title_zh: 描述一个没老师自学的朋友
topics.title_en: Describe one of your friends who learned something without a teacher

questions.question_en: Describe one of your friends who learned something without a teacher
questions.question_zh: 描述一个没老师自学的朋友。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about my university roommate, who taught himself to program without taking a single class. He's a really determined guy, and his story still impresses me.

First of all, who he is: he's my roommate from university, and we've shared a dorm since our first year. What he learned was Python, which he picked up entirely on his own. He never attended any programming course or paid for a tutor, he just watched tutorial videos on Bilibili and read the official documentation, practising a little every day.

As for why he learned it, he told me he was simply curious. He liked computers and wanted to understand how software works, and he felt the free resources online were good enough, so there was no point spending money on a class. By our second year, he could already write small tools to help our class organise information, which was genuinely useful.

Now, would it have been easier with a teacher? Honestly, I think it might have been faster in some ways, since a teacher can point out mistakes and answer questions directly. But my roommate proved that with motivation and good resources, you can go a long way on your own. What I admire most is his patience, because self-learning means solving every problem yourself, and he never gave up. Looking back, he's the reason I believe curiosity is the best teacher.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲的是大学室友，完全自学编程没上过课。他自学 Python，没报班没请家教，就看 B 站教学视频和官方文档，每天练一点。自学原因是单纯好奇、觉得网上免费资源够用。大二时已经能写小工具帮班级统计信息。有老师教可能更快，但他证明靠动力和好资源自学也能走很远；最佩服他的耐心，自学意味着每个问题都要自己解决，他从不放弃。

questions.question_en: Is it necessary to keep learning after graduating from school?
questions.answer_en: Absolutely, I think it's necessary, and it's becoming more important every year. The main reason is that technology and industries change so quickly that skills learned at school can become outdated within a few years. For example, in my field, programming languages and tools are constantly being updated, so professionals have to keep learning to stay competitive. In that sense, graduation is really just the beginning of lifelong learning.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 非常必要，而且越来越重要。技术和行业变化太快，学校学的技能几年内就可能过时；比如编程语言和工具不断更新，从业者必须持续学习才能保持竞争力。毕业只是终身学习的开始。

questions.question_en: Should teachers make learning in their classes fun?
questions.answer_en: I'd say yes, making classes fun is valuable, though it shouldn't be the only goal. When students enjoy a lesson, they pay more attention and remember more, so fun activities can genuinely improve learning. That said, the content still needs to be solid, because entertainment without substance doesn't help anyone in the long run. So I think the ideal is a teacher who makes the material engaging while keeping the learning meaningful.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 让课堂有趣很有价值，但不该是唯一目标。学生喜欢一节课就会更专注、记得更牢，有趣的活动确实能提升学习效果；但内容本身要扎实，光有趣没实质长期没用。理想是老师既让内容吸引人又保持学习有意义。

questions.question_en: Do you think there are too many subjects for students to learn?
questions.answer_en: I think it depends on the stage of education. In primary and secondary school, students in my country do study quite a lot of subjects, and some of them feel unnecessary for most people. This can leave students tired and unable to go deep into anything. Having said that, a broad range of subjects helps children discover their interests. So I'd say the number is reasonable in theory, but the pressure around exams makes it feel like too much.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 取决于教育阶段。中小学科目确实很多，有些对多数人显得没必要，让学生疲惫、无法深入任何一门；但科目广有助于孩子发现兴趣。理论上数量合理，是考试压力让它显得太多。

questions.question_en: Is it better to focus on a few subjects or to learn many subjects?
questions.answer_en: I think a balance is ideal, though it depends on the person's goals. Focusing on a few subjects allows you to go deep and build real expertise, which matters for a career. On the other hand, learning many subjects broadens your horizons and helps you find what you're good at. For students, I'd say it's wise to explore widely at first, then gradually focus on the areas that interest them most.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 平衡最理想，取决于个人目标。专注少数科目能深入、建立真正的专业能力，对职业重要；学很多科目能开阔视野、帮人发现擅长什么。学生最好先广泛探索，再逐渐聚焦最感兴趣的领域。

questions.question_en: Do you think enterprises should provide training for their employees?
questions.answer_en: Definitely, I think companies should invest in training their employees. The main reason is that it benefits both sides: employees gain new skills and feel valued, while the company gets a more capable workforce. In fast-moving industries, training is almost essential, because new technology appears constantly. Of course, it costs money and time, but in the long run, I believe it's a worthwhile investment that reduces staff turnover.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 公司应该投资员工培训，对双方都有利：员工获得新技能、感到被重视，公司得到更有能力的团队。在快速变化的行业培训几乎是必需的，因为新技术不断出现。虽然花钱花时间，但长期是值得的投资，还能降低员工流失率。

questions.question_en: Do you think it is good for older adults to continue learning?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think it's very good for older adults to keep learning. For one thing, learning new things keeps the brain active, which may help delay mental decline. It also gives them a sense of purpose and something meaningful to do after retirement. Many older people in my country take up things like calligraphy, dancing or even using smartphones, and they seem much happier for it. So I'd say learning is beneficial at any age.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 老年人持续学习非常好：学新东西让大脑保持活跃，可能延缓认知衰退；退休后也有目标感和有意义的事做。国内很多老人学书法、跳舞甚至用智能手机，看起来更快乐。学习在任何年龄都有益。

topics.title_zh: 描述一个你想见面的名人
topics.title_en: Describe a famous person you would like to meet

questions.question_en: Describe a famous person you would like to meet
questions.question_zh: 描述一个你想见面的名人。
questions.answer_en:
The famous person I'd love to meet is Ma Huateng, better known as Pony Ma, the founder of Tencent. He's from Shenzhen, which is also my hometown, and he built one of the biggest tech companies in China from scratch.

I first knew about him through the products his company makes. I've been using QQ and WeChat since I was a kid, and honestly, it's hard to imagine daily life without them, since almost everyone I know communicates through WeChat. Later, I read more about his story and learned that Tencent started in Shenzhen and grew into a global company, which made me respect him even more.

If I had the chance, I'd like to meet him at Tencent's headquarters in Shenzhen, maybe at a tech conference or a campus talk. I imagine it would be a fairly formal setting, but I'd just be happy to hear him speak in person.

The reason I want to meet him is that I'm studying computer science, and I'm curious about how he turned a small startup into such a giant. I'd love to ask him about the biggest difficulties in the early days, and how he kept the company going through tough times. Looking back, I think meeting someone who built something that touches everyone's life would be genuinely inspiring for my own future.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 想见的名人是马化腾，腾讯创始人，也是深圳人。从小用 QQ 和微信，日常生活离不开腾讯的产品，后来读到腾讯从深圳起家成长为全球公司的故事，更佩服他。希望能在深圳腾讯总部、科技大会或校园讲座见到他。想见他的原因：自己学计算机，好奇他怎么把小公司做成巨头，想问他创业初期最大的困难和如何挺过难关。

questions.question_en: What are the advantages and disadvantages of being a famous child?
questions.answer_en: I think being a famous child comes with both sides. On the positive side, famous children often get more opportunities, like roles in films or brand deals, and they may enjoy financial security from a young age. On the negative side, they lose their privacy, since cameras follow them everywhere, and they face enormous pressure to meet public expectations. Many of them also miss out on a normal childhood. So on balance, the fame brings opportunities, but the cost can be quite high.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 出名的小孩有利有弊。好处：机会多（电影角色、品牌合作）、从小有经济保障；坏处：失去隐私、被镜头跟随、承受巨大的公众期望压力，很多人还错过正常童年。总体名气带来机会，但代价很高。

questions.question_en: What can today's children do to become famous?
questions.answer_en: These days, the most common path is through social media. Children can post videos of their talents, like singing, dancing or gaming, and if the content gets popular, they can gain a large following quickly. Some also become famous through competitions or talent shows. That said, becoming famous still involves a lot of luck, since countless children post content every day, and only a tiny fraction get noticed. So talent and effort matter, but timing and luck play a big role too.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 现在最常见的路径是社交媒体：孩子发唱歌、跳舞、打游戏的视频，内容火了就能快速涨粉；也有人通过比赛和选秀出名。但出名仍很靠运气，每天无数孩子发内容，只有极小部分被看到。才华和努力重要，时机和运气也起很大作用。

questions.question_en: What can children do with their fame?
questions.answer_en: I think famous children can use their fame in positive ways. For example, they can raise awareness about issues that matter to young people, or support charities and encourage their fans to do good. Some use their earnings to fund their education, which is sensible. The key is having responsible adults around them to guide how the fame is used, because without guidance, fame can easily lead them astray.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 出名的小孩可以用名气做正面的事：为年轻人关心的问题发声、支持慈善、带动粉丝做好事；也有人用收入供自己读书，这很明智。关键是有负责任的成年人引导，否则名气容易把孩子带偏。

questions.question_en: Do people become famous because of their talent?
questions.answer_en: I'd say talent is important, but it's rarely the only reason. Many talented people never become famous, while some famous people are not especially talented in the traditional sense. What often matters more is timing, promotion and being in the right place at the right time. For example, in the entertainment industry, a good song or performance needs the right platform to reach people. So talent gives you a foundation, but luck and exposure decide whether you're noticed.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 才华重要但很少是唯一原因。很多有才华的人没出名，有些出名的人传统意义上并不特别有才。更关键的是时机、推广和对的时间地点；比如娱乐圈里好歌好表演也需要合适的平台触达观众。才华是基础，运气和曝光决定是否被看见。

questions.question_en: Is it easy to become famous in your country?
questions.answer_en: I think it's easier than it used to be, mainly because of the internet. In the past, you needed connections in the media industry, but now anyone can post content online and potentially reach millions of people. That said, becoming famous is still not easy, because the competition is fierce and attention spans are short. Many people gain a little fame briefly, but very few manage to stay famous for long. So the barrier to entry has dropped, but the barrier to lasting fame remains high.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 比以前容易，主要因为互联网：过去需要媒体圈人脉，现在任何人都能发内容、可能触达几百万人。但出名仍不容易，竞争激烈、注意力短暂，很多人短暂走红，极少人能长久保持名气。进入门槛降低了，但持久出名的门槛仍然很高。

questions.question_en: Do you want to be a famous person?
questions.answer_en: Honestly, no, I don't think I'd want to be famous. The main reason is that I value my privacy, and being famous means constantly being watched and judged by others. I also think fame brings a lot of pressure, since every mistake gets magnified publicly. I'd rather live a normal life, focus on my career and enjoy time with family and friends, without cameras following me around.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 说实话不想出名。主要原因是重视隐私，出名意味着时刻被围观和评判；名气还带来很大压力，每个错误都会被公开放大。宁愿过普通生活，专注事业、享受和家人朋友在一起的时光，没有镜头跟着。

topics.title_zh: 描述一个经常帮助他人的人
topics.title_en: Describe a person who often helps others

questions.question_en: Describe a person who often helps others
questions.question_zh: 描述一个经常帮助他人的人。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about a classmate of mine from university, who is probably the most helpful person I've ever met. He's in the same class as me, and everyone knows him as the guy you can always turn to.

First of all, who he is: he's a student in my class, and we've studied together for a couple of years now. As for how often he helps others, it's honestly all the time. Before exams, he lends his notes to the whole class, and whenever someone has trouble installing software or setting up their computer, he's the first to offer a hand.

The way he helps is what stands out most. He never makes you feel like you're bothering him, and he explains things patiently instead of just doing them for you. I remember once I was stuck on a homework problem, and he spent a whole evening going through it with me until I understood. He said he helps because he remembers how it feels to be confused, and he thinks helping others makes the whole class stronger.

As for how I feel about him, I genuinely admire him. People like him are rare, because most of us are busy with our own stuff. Having him as a classmate has made my university life much easier, and honestly, he's inspired me to be more helpful to others too. So that's why I'd describe him as a person who truly cares about the people around him.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲的是大学同班同学，是我见过最热心的人。他几乎随时都在帮人：考试前把笔记借给全班，有人装软件、弄电脑出问题他第一个帮忙。他帮人的方式最突出：从不让人觉得麻烦他，耐心讲解而不是直接代劳；有一次我作业卡住，他花了一整晚陪我弄懂。他说帮人是因为记得自己困惑时的感受，帮别人也让全班更强。我很佩服他，他让我也想变得更乐于助人。

questions.question_en: What can children do to help their parents?
questions.answer_en: Children can help their parents in quite simple ways. For example, they can do small household chores, like tidying their own room, washing dishes or taking out the rubbish. They can also help by being considerate, such as not making a mess and studying hard, which reduces their parents' worries. Even small gestures, like helping carry shopping bags, show that they care. I think the key is that the help doesn't need to be big, just consistent.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 孩子帮父母的方式很简单：做小家务，比如整理自己房间、洗碗、倒垃圾；也可以懂事一点，不弄乱、认真学习，减少父母操心；甚至帮忙拎购物袋这样的小举动都能体现关心。关键不是帮多大忙，而是持续。

questions.question_en: Should children help their parents with household chores?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think they should, and it's actually good for them. Doing chores teaches children responsibility and basic life skills that they'll need as adults, like cooking and cleaning. It also helps them understand how much work their parents do, which builds appreciation. Of course, the chores should be suitable for their age, but starting early is beneficial. In my view, children who help at home tend to grow up more independent and considerate.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 应该帮，而且对孩子有好处。做家务教会孩子责任感和成年后需要的基本生活技能，比如做饭、打扫；也让他们理解父母有多辛苦，学会感恩。家务要适合年龄，但早点开始有益。在家帮忙的孩子长大后往往更独立、更体贴。

questions.question_en: What kind of help do people need when looking for a new job?
questions.answer_en: When people are job hunting, they need several kinds of help. Firstly, practical advice, like how to write a good CV and prepare for interviews. Secondly, connections, since many jobs are found through referrals from friends or former colleagues. They also need emotional support, because job hunting can be stressful and full of rejection. So I'd say the most valuable help combines information, connections and encouragement.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 求职时需要几种帮助：一是实用建议，比如怎么写好简历、怎么准备面试；二是人脉，很多工作靠朋友或前同事推荐；三是情感支持，求职压力大、常被拒绝。最有价值的帮助是信息、人脉和鼓励的结合。

questions.question_en: Who should people ask for help, colleagues or family members?
questions.answer_en: I think it depends on the kind of help needed. For work-related problems, colleagues are usually the better choice, because they understand the situation and can give practical advice. Family members, on the other hand, are better for emotional support, since they care about you personally and are less likely to judge. So I'd say people should ask colleagues for professional help and family for personal support, rather than relying on only one side.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 取决于需要什么帮助。工作上的问题找同事更好，因为他们了解情况、能给实用建议；情感支持找家人更好，因为他们真心关心你、不太会评判。所以专业问题问同事、个人问题问家人，不要只依赖一边。

questions.question_en: Do you think schools should teach children to do household chores?
questions.answer_en: I think it's a good idea, though it should be done in a light way. Schools could include simple life skills in their curriculum, like cooking, cleaning or basic repairs, because not every child learns these at home. This would help children become more independent and prepared for adult life. That said, schools shouldn't overload students with extra requirements, since they already have a heavy workload. So I'd support it as an optional or practical part of education.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 好主意，但应该轻松地进行。学校可以在课程里加入简单生活技能，比如做饭、打扫、基础维修，因为不是每个孩子都在家学到这些；这能让孩子更独立、为成年生活做准备。但学校不该给学生加太多负担，他们课业已经很重。支持作为选修或实践部分。

questions.question_en: Why are employees reluctant to ask their managers for help?
questions.answer_en: I think the main reason is fear of looking incompetent. Many employees worry that asking for help will make their manager think they can't handle the job, which could hurt their chances of promotion. There's also the power gap, since in many workplaces, including mine, managers are seen as authority figures, which makes employees hesitate. And some managers are simply too busy or unapproachable. So the reluctance often comes from workplace culture rather than the employees themselves.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 主要原因是怕显得无能：员工担心求助会让经理觉得自己干不了活，影响晋升机会。还有权力差距，很多职场里经理被视为权威人物，员工会犹豫；有些经理也确实太忙或不好接近。所以这种犹豫往往来自职场文化，而不是员工本身。

topics.title_zh: 描述一个用聪明方式解决问题的人
topics.title_en: Describe a person who solved a problem in a smart way

questions.question_en: Describe a person who solved a problem in a smart way
questions.question_zh: 描述一个用聪明方式解决问题的人。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about my cousin, who solved a computer problem for me in a way that still amazes me. He's a few years older than me, and he's always been the person in the family who fixes things.

First of all, who he is: he's my cousin, and he's really good with his hands. He repairs routers and computers at home, so when something breaks, everyone calls him. The problem happened about a year ago, when my computer suddenly wouldn't turn on. I was in a panic, because I had an assignment due the next day, and I had no idea what was wrong. I was already imagining having to take it to a repair shop and paying a lot of money.

How he solved it was the impressive part. He came over, looked at the computer for about two minutes, and then calmly opened the case. He found that the memory stick was loose, so he simply took it out and pushed it back in firmly. The computer started up right away, and the whole thing took him less than five minutes.

The reason I think it was smart is that he didn't panic or try random fixes. He knew where to look, because he understood how the machine works, and he solved the problem at the root instead of guessing. Looking back, I realised that being smart isn't just about knowledge, it's about staying calm and thinking clearly when everyone else is panicking.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲的是表哥，动手能力强，家里路由器、电脑坏了都找他修。一年前我电脑突然开不了机，第二天要交作业，急得不行，都想着要送修花钱了。他来了看了两分钟，冷静打开机箱，发现内存条松了，拔出来重新插紧，电脑马上就好了，全程不到五分钟。觉得他聪明是因为他不慌不乱、不瞎试，懂机器原理所以知道该看哪里，从根源解决问题。聪明不只是知识，更是别人慌乱时保持冷静、想清楚。

questions.question_en: Do you think children are born smart or they learn to become smart?
questions.answer_en: I think it's a combination of both. Some children are born with natural advantages, like quick thinking or a good memory, which gives them a head start. However, intelligence is mostly developed through learning and experience. A child who reads, asks questions and practises will become smarter over time, regardless of their starting point. So I'd say everyone is born with potential, but it's the learning that turns that potential into real ability.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 两者结合。有些孩子天生有优势，比如反应快、记性好，起点更高；但智力主要靠学习和经验发展。爱读书、爱提问、勤练习的孩子会越来越聪明，不管起点如何。人人天生有潜力，是学习把潜力变成真正的能力。

questions.question_en: How do children become smart at school?
questions.answer_en: Children become smart at school mainly through good habits and curiosity. Asking questions is a big part of it, because it shows they're thinking deeply rather than just memorising. Practising regularly also matters, since skills like maths and writing improve with repetition. On top of that, learning from mistakes helps them grow, because smart children treat errors as chances to improve. So I'd say it's a mix of curiosity, practice and the right attitude.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 孩子在学校变聪明主要靠好习惯和好奇心。提问很重要，说明他们在深入思考而不是死记硬背；定期练习也关键，数学写作这类技能靠重复提高；还要从错误中学习，聪明的孩子把错误当改进的机会。是好奇心、练习和正确态度的结合。

questions.question_en: Why are some people well-rounded and others only good at one thing?
questions.answer_en: I think it comes down to interests, opportunities and personality. People who are curious about many things and have the chance to try different activities tend to become well-rounded. Others may find one thing they love early on and pour all their time into it, which naturally makes them specialists. There's nothing wrong with either path, since society needs both generalists and specialists. So it's largely about how people choose to spend their time and energy.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 取决于兴趣、机会和性格。对很多事好奇、有机会尝试不同活动的人往往全面发展；另一些人很早就找到热爱的一件事，把所有时间投入进去，自然成为专家。两条路都没错，社会既需要通才也需要专才。主要看人怎么分配时间和精力。

questions.question_en: Why does modern society need talents of all kinds?
questions.answer_en: Modern society is so complex that no single type of talent can solve all its problems. We need engineers to build technology, doctors to keep people healthy, artists to enrich culture and teachers to pass on knowledge. Each field depends on the others, so a society with only one kind of talent would quickly fall apart. In that sense, diversity of talent is what keeps society balanced and moving forward.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 现代社会太复杂，单一类型的人才解决不了所有问题。需要工程师造技术、医生保健康、艺术家丰富文化、教师传承知识。每个领域都依赖其他领域，只有一种人才的社会很快就会崩溃。人才多样性让社会保持平衡、向前发展。

questions.question_en: Do you think smart children are happier than other children?
questions.answer_en: I don't think smart children are automatically happier. Intelligence can bring advantages, like doing well at school and solving problems easily, but it can also bring pressure, since people expect more from them. Happiness depends more on things like family support, friendships and whether they can pursue what they love. A smart child under too much pressure might actually be less happy than an average child with a relaxed life. So intelligence and happiness aren't directly connected.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 聪明的孩子不一定更快乐。智力带来优势，比如学习好、解决问题轻松，但也带来压力，因为别人对他们期望更高。快乐更取决于家庭支持、友谊和能否追求所爱。压力过大的聪明孩子可能还不如生活轻松的普通孩子快乐。智力和快乐没有直接关系。

questions.question_en: Is it important for schools to identify and develop each student's talents?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think it's important, because every student has strengths that might not show up in regular exams. If schools can identify these talents early, they can help students develop them, which builds confidence and motivation. That said, schools should be careful not to label children or push them too hard in one direction. The goal should be to support each student's potential while keeping a broad education, rather than forcing everyone into the same mould.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 重要，因为每个学生都有常规考试看不出的长处。学校早点发现这些才能并帮助发展，能建立自信和动力。但学校要小心不要给孩子贴标签或往一个方向逼太狠。目标应该是支持每个学生的潜力，同时保持全面教育，而不是把所有人塞进同一个模子。
