topics.title_zh: 描述一个喜欢保护自然的人
topics.title_en: Describe a person who likes to look after the natural world

questions.question_en: Describe a person who likes to look after the natural world
questions.question_zh: 描述一个喜欢保护自然的人。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about my girlfriend, who is the most nature-loving person I know. She genuinely cares about the environment, and being around her has changed the way I see nature.

First of all, who she is: she's my girlfriend, and we've been together for a while now. What she does to protect nature is quite simple but meaningful. She loves the sea, so we often go to Qianhai and Shenzhen Bay, which are both by the water. Every time we go, she brings a bag with her, and she picks up any litter she sees on the beach, like plastic bottles and food wrappers.

The way she does it is what impresses me. She doesn't make a big show of it, she just quietly collects rubbish while we walk, and she always takes her own drink bottles home instead of leaving them behind. When we went hiking in Yangjiang, she did the same thing on the mountain, reminding me not to drop anything either.

As for how often, it's basically every time we're outdoors, so at least a couple of times a month. The reason I admire her is that she doesn't just say she loves nature, she actually acts on it. I used to think nature was just something nice to look at, but she's taught me that caring for it means taking responsibility. Looking back, I think people like her make the world a better place, one small action at a time.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲的是女朋友，我认识的最爱自然的人。她爱海，我们常去前海和深圳湾，每次去她都带个袋子，把沙滩上的塑料瓶、食品包装等垃圾捡走。她做这些很低调，不张扬，边走边默默捡，自己的饮料瓶也带回家；去阳江爬山时她在山上也这么做，还提醒我不要乱扔。频率是每次户外活动都这样，一个月至少几次。佩服她是因为她不只是嘴上说爱自然，而是真的行动；她让我明白爱护自然意味着承担责任。

questions.question_en: Do you think parents should teach their children how to protect the environment?
questions.answer_en: Definitely, I think parents play a crucial role here. Children learn most of their habits at home, so if parents teach them to sort rubbish, save water and not litter, these behaviours become natural. It's much easier to form good habits in childhood than to change bad ones later. Parents can also lead by example, since children tend to copy what they see. So I'd say environmental education should definitely start at home.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 父母绝对扮演关键角色。孩子大部分习惯是在家养成的，如果父母教他们垃圾分类、节约用水、不乱扔垃圾，这些行为就会变成自然习惯。童年养成好习惯比以后改掉坏习惯容易得多。父母还可以以身作则，孩子会模仿看到的行为。环保教育应该从家里开始。

questions.question_en: What laws about the environment are effective in your country?
questions.answer_en: In my country, a few environmental laws have been quite effective. The most visible one is the waste sorting policy in major cities, which requires people to separate their rubbish into different categories, and it has noticeably changed daily habits. There are also restrictions on single-use plastics, like plastic bags, which are no longer free in supermarkets. On top of that, strict emission standards for factories have helped improve air quality in many areas. So I'd say these practical regulations have made a real difference.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 国内有几项环保法律效果不错。最明显的是大城市的垃圾分类政策，要求居民把垃圾分门别类，明显改变了日常习惯；还有一次性塑料限制，超市塑料袋不再免费；另外工厂严格的排放标准改善了很多地区的空气质量。这些务实的法规确实带来了实际改变。

questions.question_en: Which do you think people prefer, rewards or punishment, when it comes to government intervention in environmental protection?
questions.answer_en: I think most people prefer rewards, because they feel positive and encouraging. For example, subsidies for buying electric cars or discounts for recycling make people want to participate. Punishment, like fines for littering, works too, but it can feel unfair and create resentment. That said, some punishment is necessary for serious violations, since not everyone responds to encouragement. So on balance, I'd say a combination works best, with rewards as the main tool and punishment as a backup.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 多数人更喜欢奖励，因为奖励让人感觉积极、受鼓励；比如买电动车的补贴、回收的折扣会让人愿意参与。惩罚（如乱扔垃圾罚款）也有效，但可能让人觉得不公平、产生抵触。不过对严重违规，一定惩罚是必要的，因为不是所有人都吃鼓励这套。总体奖励为主、惩罚为辅的组合最好。

questions.question_en: Is it easy for children in cities to get close to the natural world?
questions.answer_en: I'd say it's harder for city children than for those in the countryside. In cities, nature is often limited to parks and gardens, and many children spend most of their time indoors with screens. That said, it's not impossible, since most cities have parks, and some families take children to the seaside or mountains on weekends. So while city children have fewer chances to connect with nature, it's still possible if parents make an effort.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 城市孩子比农村孩子更难亲近自然。城市里自然往往只有公园和花园，很多孩子大部分时间待在室内对着屏幕。但也不是不可能：大多数城市有公园，有些家庭周末带孩子去海边或山里。城市孩子接触自然的机会少，但只要父母用心还是可以的。

questions.question_en: What can people do to protect the natural world?
questions.answer_en: There are many things ordinary people can do. The most basic ones are reducing waste, like using fewer plastic bags and recycling properly, and saving energy, such as turning off lights and using public transport. People can also make greener choices when shopping, like buying products with less packaging. On a larger scale, supporting environmental organisations or joining clean-up activities makes a difference too. I think small daily actions, done consistently, add up to real change.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 普通人能做的事很多。最基本的：减少浪费（少用塑料袋、正确回收）、节约能源（关灯、坐公共交通）；购物时做更环保的选择，比如买包装少的产品；更大层面，支持环保组织或参加清理活动也有作用。小的日常行动坚持做，累积起来就是真正的改变。

questions.question_en: Is it important to teach students environmental protection at school?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think it's very important. Schools are where children spend most of their time, so environmental education there can reach almost everyone. Teaching students about issues like climate change and waste helps them understand why protecting nature matters, and practical activities, like recycling programmes or tree planting, turn that understanding into habits. Since environmental problems are getting more serious, I believe this kind of education should be a regular part of the curriculum.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 非常重要。学校是孩子待得最久的地方，环保教育在那里能覆盖几乎所有人。教学生了解气候变化、垃圾等问题，让他们明白保护自然为什么重要；回收项目、植树这类实践活动把理解变成习惯。环境问题越来越严重，这类教育应该成为课程的常规部分。

topics.title_zh: 描述一项你想在国内推行的新法律
topics.title_en: Describe a new law you would like to introduce in your country

questions.question_en: Describe a new law you would like to introduce in your country
questions.question_zh: 描述一项你想在国内推行的新法律。
questions.answer_en:
The law I'd like to introduce is one that guarantees workers two full rest days every week, which people often call the double rest day policy. In my country, many companies already promise weekends off on paper, but in reality employees still receive work messages and tasks on Saturdays and Sundays, so the law would make it illegal for employers to contact staff about work during those two days.

As for the changes it would bring, I think the biggest one is that people would finally have proper time to recover. They could spend weekends with their families, take up hobbies, or simply sleep in, which would improve both their physical and mental health in the long run.

Would it be popular? I believe so, at least among ordinary workers. Most of my friends complain about working overtime, so I'm fairly confident a law like this would be welcomed. Of course, some companies might resist it, because they rely on employees being available all the time.

I came up with this idea after seeing a news report about a young man who collapsed from overwork. It really struck me that rest is not a luxury, it's a basic right.

Honestly, I feel quite strongly about this law. To me, it's not just about having free time, it's about respecting people's lives outside work.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 我想推行的新法是保障双休落地，强制企业保证员工每周两天完整休息；会带来生活质量的提升，普通上班族会欢迎，但企业可能抵触；灵感来自过劳新闻，我认为休息是基本权利。

questions.question_en: What rules should students follow at school?
questions.answer_en: I think the most essential rules are about respect and safety. Students should respect their teachers and classmates, which means no bullying and no disruptive behavior in class. They should also follow basic safety rules, like not running in the corridors or leaving school without permission. Having said that, I don't think schools should be too strict, because some freedom helps students develop independence. On the whole, rules should create a safe environment without killing creativity.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 学校规则核心是尊重与安全：尊重师生、不欺凌、守安全规则；但不宜过严，要给自由发展空间。

questions.question_en: Do people in your country usually obey the law?
questions.answer_en: Generally speaking, I'd say most people in my country obey the law in their daily lives, like following traffic rules and paying taxes. However, there are some gray areas, for example, jaywalking or minor parking violations are quite common, because people don't see them as serious. I think this comes down to enforcement, when people believe they won't be caught, they tend to take shortcuts. That said, for major laws, like criminal ones, the vast majority of people follow them without question.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 多数人日常守法（交通、纳税），但闯红灯、乱停车等灰色地带常见，因为觉得不会被抓；重大法律基本人人遵守。

questions.question_en: What kinds of behavior are considered as good behavior?
questions.answer_en: I think good behavior generally means actions that show respect for others and for society. For example, being polite, helping people in need, and following public rules are all widely considered good. In my country, there's also a strong emphasis on filial piety, so taking care of elderly parents is seen as very admirable. Of course, what counts as good behavior can vary across cultures, but I believe the core idea is the same, treating others the way you'd like to be treated.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 好行为=尊重他人与社会：礼貌、助人、守公共规则；中国还强调孝道，照顾父母很受尊敬；文化不同但核心相同。

questions.question_en: Do you think children can learn about the law outside of school?
questions.answer_en: Absolutely, I think children can learn a lot about the law outside school, and in many ways it's more effective. For instance, parents can explain simple rules at home, like why we shouldn't take things that don't belong to us. Also, everyday experiences teach children about rules, such as waiting in line or following traffic lights. I mean, real-life situations make the law feel relevant, whereas school lessons can seem abstract. So I'd say family and daily life play a huge role in legal education.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 完全可以，而且更有效：父母在家讲简单规则，日常排队、看红绿灯都是法律教育；真实情境比课堂更贴近生活。

questions.question_en: What are the benefits for people to obey rules?
questions.answer_en: I think the benefits are both personal and social. On a personal level, obeying rules keeps people safe and helps them avoid trouble, like fines or accidents. On a social level, when everyone follows the same rules, society runs more smoothly, for example, traffic flows better when drivers respect the signals. There's also a sense of fairness, because rules protect everyone equally. So on the whole, following rules isn't just about restriction, it actually creates order and trust, which benefit everybody.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 个人层面保安全、免麻烦；社会层面秩序更顺、更公平；守规则创造秩序与信任，人人受益。

questions.question_en: How can parents teach children to obey rules?
questions.answer_en: I believe the most effective way is to lead by example. Children learn more from what their parents do than from what they say, so if parents always follow rules themselves, kids are likely to copy that behavior. Parents can also explain the reasons behind rules in simple language, rather than just saying 'because I told you so'. Another useful approach is to give children small responsibilities, like tidying their own toys, which teaches them that rules create order. Consistency is key, I think.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 最有效是言传身教，孩子模仿父母；用简单语言解释规则背后的原因；给孩子小责任（收拾玩具）培养规则意识；坚持一致。

topics.title_zh: 描述你最近不得不改变的一个计划
topics.title_en: Describe a plan that you had to change recently

questions.question_en: Describe a plan that you had to change recently
questions.question_zh: 描述你最近不得不改变的一个计划。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about a plan I had to change last month. I was supposed to go hiking with two of my friends on a Saturday, and we'd been looking forward to it for weeks, because we'd booked the tickets and everything.

However, the night before, one of my friends called to say he had a sudden family emergency and couldn't make it. At first, I thought we could just go without him, but then the weather forecast said there would be heavy rain all weekend, so we had no choice but to cancel the whole trip.

Instead, we changed the plan to a simple indoor gathering. We met at a hotpot restaurant near my place, and honestly, it turned out to be quite enjoyable. We still got to catch up and talk about our lives, which was the real reason we wanted to meet in the first place.

As for how I felt, I have to admit I was pretty frustrated at the beginning. I'm the kind of person who doesn't handle sudden changes well, because my schedule gets completely messed up. But looking back, I think it was a blessing in disguise, since we avoided getting soaked in the rain and still had a good time together.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 上个月和朋友约好周六去爬山，结果朋友临时有家事、天气预报又说下大雨，只好改成在附近火锅店聚餐；一开始很难受，因为我不喜欢安排被打乱，但后来觉得因祸得福，躲过了大雨还聊得很开心。

questions.question_en: Do people often change their plans?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think changing plans is very common in modern life. The main reason is that life is unpredictable, things like work emergencies, bad weather or sudden illness can easily force people to adjust. Also, with so many options available these days, people tend to change their minds more easily, for example, they might book a trip and then switch destinations after seeing better deals. That said, I think frequent changes can be stressful, so most people try to keep their important plans stable.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 很常见，生活不可预测（工作突发、天气、生病）；选择多也让人更容易改主意；但频繁改动会带来压力。

questions.question_en: Would you tell others if you change your plan?
questions.answer_en: I think it depends on the situation. If the change affects other people, like a group gathering or a work meeting, then yes, I'd definitely inform them as soon as possible, because it's a matter of respect. However, if it's a personal plan that only involves me, like what to cook for dinner, then I wouldn't bother telling anyone. I mean, communication is important, but it should be proportional to how much the change affects others.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 看情况：影响别人的计划一定尽早告知，这是尊重；只涉及自己的小事就不用说；沟通要与影响程度成正比。

questions.question_en: Why do you think parents still make plans for their children nowadays?
questions.answer_en: I think there are a couple of reasons. Firstly, many parents believe they know what's best for their children, based on their own life experience, so they plan things like study schedules or extracurricular activities. Secondly, society is quite competitive these days, and parents worry that without careful planning, their children might fall behind. Having said that, I think parents should leave some room for children to make their own choices, because over-planning can actually reduce a child's independence.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 一是父母觉得凭经验知道什么对孩子最好，二是社会竞争激烈怕孩子落后；但过度规划会削弱孩子的独立性。

questions.question_en: How does technology help people make plans?
questions.answer_en: Technology has made planning much easier and more efficient. For example, calendar apps remind people of upcoming events, and note-taking tools help them organize their tasks. Also, with online booking systems, people can arrange travel, restaurants and tickets in just a few minutes, which was unthinkable twenty years ago. I think the biggest advantage is flexibility, because if a plan changes, people can adjust everything online instantly. That said, technology can't replace careful thinking, it's just a tool that supports decision-making.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 日历提醒、笔记工具、在线预订让规划更高效灵活；计划变了可以随时在线调整；但技术只是工具，不能替代思考。

topics.title_zh: 描述一个有趣的视频
topics.title_en: Describe an interesting video

questions.question_en: Describe an interesting video
questions.question_zh: 描述一个有趣的视频。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about a funny video I watched on Bilibili, which is a popular video platform in my country. I came across it about two weeks ago, late at night, when I was scrolling through my feed on my phone before going to bed.

The video was a short comedy sketch made by a young creator. In it, he tried to cook a complicated dish for the first time, and everything went wrong, the oil splashed everywhere, the pan caught fire, and he ended up ordering takeout anyway. The editing was really clever, with funny sound effects and captions, so I couldn't stop laughing.

I watched it mainly because I needed a break after a long day at work. I often search for funny videos when I feel tired, and this one happened to appear in my recommendations. What's interesting is that I ended up saving it to my collection, because I knew I'd want to watch it again when I was in a bad mood.

Honestly, I think this kind of video is really valuable. It only lasts a few minutes, but it can completely change my mood. I mean, laughter is such a simple way to relieve stress, and I'm glad platforms like Bilibili make it so easy to find.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 两周前深夜在B站刷到一个搞笑做饭视频，UP主第一次做复杂菜式各种翻车，最后点了外卖；我累的时候爱看搞笑视频放松，看完笑个不停，还收藏了准备心情不好时再看。

questions.question_en: What kind of videos do people in your country like to watch?
questions.answer_en: I think it varies a lot by age group. Young people tend to enjoy short videos, like funny clips, gaming content and vlogs, mostly on platforms such as Douyin and Bilibili. Older people, on the other hand, often prefer news, cooking shows and health-related content. Generally speaking, entertainment is the most popular category overall, because most people watch videos to relax after work or study. That said, educational videos are also growing quickly, especially among students.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 分年龄：年轻人爱短视频（搞笑、游戏、vlog），老人爱新闻、做饭、健康内容；娱乐类整体最受欢迎，教育类增长快。

questions.question_en: Which is more helpful, watching videos or reading books?
questions.answer_en: I'd say it depends on what you want to learn. For practical skills, like cooking or fixing things, videos are definitely more helpful, because you can see the exact steps and imitate them. However, for deep understanding, like philosophy or history, books are better, since they allow you to think slowly and in depth. I mean, videos are efficient but often shallow, whereas books require more effort but give more lasting knowledge. So on the whole, they complement each other rather than compete.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 看学什么：实用技能视频更直观，深度知识书更好；视频高效但浅，书费劲但持久；两者互补。

questions.question_en: What skills can people learn from watching videos?
questions.answer_en: People can learn a surprisingly wide range of skills from videos. Practical ones are the most obvious, like cooking, repairing electronics or learning a language, because you can watch and repeat. There are also softer skills, such as public speaking or time management, which many people learn from online courses. I think the key is that videos make learning accessible, you can pause, rewind and watch at your own pace. Having said that, skills that require physical practice, like playing an instrument, still need real hands-on training.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 实用技能（做饭、修电器、学语言）最明显，还有软技能（演讲、时间管理）；视频可暂停回放，但需要动手的技能仍要实操。

questions.question_en: Are there any differences between the videos that young people and old people like to watch?
questions.answer_en: Yes, there are quite clear differences. Young people usually prefer fast-paced content, like short comedy clips, music videos and gaming streams, which match their shorter attention spans. Older people, in contrast, tend to watch slower, more informative content, such as documentaries, news and traditional opera performances. I think this difference mainly comes from their habits and interests, but it's also changing, because many older people are now getting used to short videos as well. So the gap is narrowing, to some extent.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 年轻人爱快节奏内容，老人爱慢而信息量大的内容；差异来自习惯和兴趣，但老人也在适应短视频，差距在缩小。

topics.title_zh: 描述一部你最近看并喜欢的电影
topics.title_en: Describe a movie you watched and enjoyed recently

questions.question_en: Describe a movie you watched and enjoyed recently
questions.question_zh: 描述一部你最近看并喜欢的电影。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to describe a movie I watched recently, Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse. I saw it about a month ago at a cinema in Buji, which is a district in Shenzhen where I live. It was a weekend afternoon, and the cinema was quite crowded, which surprised me a little.

I watched it with my girlfriend. We usually go to the cinema together once or twice a month, and this time she was the one who suggested it, because she'd heard great things about the animation style.

The movie is about a teenage boy named Miles Morales, who discovers he can travel between different universes where other Spider-Man versions exist. What impressed me most was the visual style, every frame looked like a moving comic book, with bright colors and creative action scenes. The story also had a lot of heart, especially the relationship between Miles and his parents.

As for why I watched it, apart from my girlfriend's recommendation, I'm a big fan of superhero movies, and I'd enjoyed the first Spider-Verse film a lot. I have to say, I wasn't disappointed. We both left the cinema talking about our favorite scenes, and I'd definitely watch it again.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 一个月前和女朋友在深圳布吉的电影院看了《蜘蛛侠：纵横宇宙》，讲少年迈尔斯穿越多元宇宙的故事；动画风格惊艳，故事也有温度，女朋友推荐加上我本来就喜欢超级英雄电影。

questions.question_en: What kinds of movies do you think are successful in your country?
questions.answer_en: I think comedy and action movies tend to be the most successful in my country, because they appeal to a wide audience and are easy to enjoy. In recent years, patriotic blockbusters have also done extremely well, especially during national holidays. That said, I believe success isn't only about box office numbers, some art films win awards and gain respect even with small audiences. So I'd say commercial success and artistic success are two different things, and both exist in our film industry.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 喜剧和动作片最卖座，近年主旋律大片在假期也很火；但成功不只是票房，艺术片获奖也受尊重。

questions.question_en: What are the factors that make a successful movie?
questions.answer_en: I think there are several key factors. Firstly, a strong story is essential, because no matter how good the visuals are, a weak plot will disappoint the audience. Secondly, good acting and directing bring the story to life, and famous actors can attract initial attention. Also, timing matters, for example, a movie released during a holiday often performs better. I'd say the most important factor is emotional connection, because if the audience relates to the characters, they'll recommend it to others.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 好故事是根本，演技和导演加分，档期也重要；最关键是与观众产生情感共鸣，口碑带动长期成功。

questions.question_en: Do Chinese people prefer to watch domestic movies or foreign movies?
questions.answer_en: I think it's mixed, but domestic movies have become increasingly popular in recent years. One reason is that local films often reflect Chinese culture and daily life, which makes them easier to relate to. Also, the quality of domestic productions has improved a lot, with better special effects and storytelling. That said, foreign movies, especially Hollywood blockbusters, still have a loyal audience, particularly among young people who enjoy their visual effects. So I'd say both have their place, and the choice often depends on the genre.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 国产片近年越来越受欢迎（贴近生活、质量提升），但好莱坞大片在年轻人中仍有市场；看类型而定。

questions.question_en: Do you think only well-known directors can create the best movies?
questions.answer_en: No, I don't think so at all. While famous directors have more resources and experience, many great movies have been made by newcomers with fresh ideas. For example, some low-budget films directed by first-time directors have become huge hits because of their originality. I think creativity matters more than reputation, and the industry needs new voices to keep evolving. Having said that, well-known directors do have advantages, like easier access to funding and distribution, but that doesn't mean they always produce better work.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不一定，新导演常有新鲜创意，低成本黑马不少；创造力比名气重要，但名导在资金和发行上有优势。

questions.question_en: Do you think successful movies should have well-known actors or actresses in leading roles?
questions.answer_en: I'd say it helps, but it's not a guarantee of success. Well-known actors can attract audiences at the beginning, because people are curious about their favorite stars. However, if the movie itself is weak, even famous actors can't save it, and audiences will quickly lose interest. On the other hand, some movies with unknown actors have become massive successes purely because of their stories. So I think the script and direction matter more, while star power is just an extra advantage.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 有名演员能吸引初期关注，但电影本身弱的话救不回来；也有无名演员靠故事大获成功的例子；剧本和导演更重要。

questions.question_en: Why do people prefer to watch movies in the cinema?
questions.answer_en: I think the main reason is the immersive experience. The big screen, surround sound and dark environment make people feel like they're inside the story, which a home TV can't fully provide. Also, going to the cinema is a social activity, since people often go with friends or family and share the experience. That said, with streaming services becoming so convenient, some people now prefer watching at home. So I'd say the cinema still wins for big blockbusters, but not for every movie.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 沉浸感（大屏、环绕声、黑暗环境）是主因，也是社交活动；但流媒体方便，大片去影院、普通片在家看。

topics.title_zh: 描述一件你想拥有的科技产品(非手机)
topics.title_en: Describe a piece of technology (not a phone) that you would like to own

questions.question_en: Describe a piece of technology (not a phone) that you would like to own
questions.question_zh: 描述一件你想拥有的科技产品(非手机)。
questions.answer_en:
The piece of technology I'd love to own is a 3D printer. For those who don't know, it's a machine that builds physical objects layer by layer from digital designs, using materials like plastic filament. You can print anything from small toys to replacement parts for household items.

In terms of price, a decent entry-level 3D printer costs around two to three thousand yuan, which is not cheap, but it's affordable enough for a hobby. The higher-end models can cost much more, but I think a basic one would be enough for me to start with.

I first learned about 3D printers a few years ago from videos online. I remember watching a creator print a fully working mechanical gear, and I was amazed that a machine at home could produce something so precise. Since then, I've followed quite a few makers on Bilibili who share their printing projects.

The main reason I want one is that I'd like to experience hands-on making. I've always been curious about how things are built, and a 3D printer would let me turn my own ideas into real objects. I mean, there's a big difference between looking at a design on a screen and actually holding the finished product in your hand. So for me, it's not just a gadget, it's a way to learn and create.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 我想拥有一台3D打印机，入门款大概两三千元；几年前在网上看到有人打印出精密齿轮，从此关注了很多B站创作者的打印项目；想亲手把想法变成实物，体验动手创造的乐趣。

questions.question_en: What are the differences between the technology of the past and that of today?
questions.answer_en: I think the biggest difference is speed and connectivity. In the past, technology was mostly mechanical and slow, for example, people communicated through letters that took days to arrive. Today, everything is digital and instant, we can video call someone on the other side of the world in seconds. Also, modern technology is much smaller and more portable, a smartphone today has more power than computers from thirty years ago. I'd say the pace of change itself is also a difference, technology now updates almost every year.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 过去机械、慢（信件要几天），现在数字、即时（视频通话秒连）；现代设备更小更便携，更新换代更快。

questions.question_en: What technology do young people like to use?
questions.answer_en: Young people are usually drawn to technology that is fast, visual and social. Smartphones are obviously the most essential, since they combine communication, entertainment and work in one device. Beyond that, many young people enjoy gaming consoles, wireless earphones and smartwatches, which fit their active lifestyles. Social media apps are also a big part of their daily routine. I think the common thread is convenience, young people prefer technology that saves time and connects them with others instantly.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 年轻人爱快、视觉化、社交化的科技：手机最核心，还有游戏机、无线耳机、智能手表；共同点是方便、即时连接。

questions.question_en: What are the differences between online and face-to-face communication?
questions.answer_en: I think the main difference is the level of emotional connection. Face-to-face communication includes body language, eye contact and tone of voice, which help people understand each other more deeply. Online communication, on the other hand, is more convenient and efficient, especially for long-distance relationships or work meetings. However, it can easily lead to misunderstandings, because text messages lack emotion. So I'd say face-to-face is warmer and more genuine, while online is faster and more practical, and both have their place in modern life.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 面对面有肢体语言和语气，情感更深；线上方便高效但容易误解；面对面更温暖，线上更实用。

questions.question_en: Do you think technology has changed the way people communicate?
questions.answer_en: Definitely, I think technology has transformed communication completely. In the past, people mainly communicated face to face or through letters, which took time and effort. Nowadays, we send messages, share photos and make video calls instantly, and we can stay in touch with people across the world. I think this has made communication more frequent but also more casual, for example, people now send quick messages instead of writing long letters. Having said that, I believe the quality of deep conversations hasn't improved, and might even have declined.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 彻底改变了：从面对面/信件到即时消息和视频通话；交流更频繁但更随意，深度对话反而可能变少。

questions.question_en: What negative effects does technology have on people's relationships?
questions.answer_en: I think there are several negative effects. Firstly, people spend so much time on their phones that they sometimes ignore the people physically around them, which weakens family bonds. Secondly, online communication can create misunderstandings, because it's hard to read emotions through text. Also, social media sometimes causes jealousy or comparison, which puts pressure on relationships. That said, I don't think technology itself is the problem, it's how people use it. If used wisely, it can actually strengthen relationships by keeping people connected.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 沉迷手机忽略身边人、文字交流易误解、社交媒体引发攀比；但问题在用法不在技术本身。

questions.question_en: What are the differences between making friends in real life and online?
questions.answer_en: I think the biggest difference is depth. Friends made in real life usually develop trust gradually through shared experiences, like studying together or playing sports, so the bond tends to be stronger. Online friendships, in contrast, are often based on common interests and can form very quickly, but they may stay superficial. Also, real-life friends can offer practical support, while online friends mainly provide emotional company. Having said that, online friendships can become real ones if people eventually meet, so I'd say both types have value.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 现实友谊靠共同经历建立信任，更深；网上友谊基于共同兴趣、来得快但可能浅；网上友谊见面后也能变真。

topics.title_zh: 描述一件家里长期保存的重要物品
topics.title_en: Describe something important that has been kept in your family for a long time

questions.question_en: Describe something important that has been kept in your family for a long time
questions.question_zh: 描述一件家里长期保存的重要物品。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about a box of old family photos, which my parents have kept for as long as I can remember. It's not valuable in terms of money, but it means a lot to us.

First of all, what it is: it's a worn cardboard box full of printed photos, most of them taken before I was born. There are pictures of my grandparents when they were young, my parents' wedding, and a lot of shots of me and my brother as little kids, some of them faded and slightly yellowed.

As for when we got it, my parents started collecting these photos in the 1990s, before digital cameras existed. They used to take the film to a shop to be developed, and they kept every print in this box. I remember my mum telling me that the box has moved with us every time we changed homes, which is why it's still in one piece.

The reason it's important to my family is that it carries our childhood memories. Whenever relatives come to visit, we open the box together and look through the photos, and everyone starts telling stories about the past. For me, those pictures are a bridge to my childhood, they remind me of the summers I spent at my grandparents' house and the people who are no longer with us. Looking back, I think this box is one of the few things in our home that money can't replace, because it holds the history of our whole family.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲的是家里一盒老照片，爸妈保存了很久。它不值钱但对我们意义重大。它是装满了打印照片的旧纸盒，大多是出生前拍的：爷爷奶奶年轻时的照片、爸妈的结婚照、我和弟弟小时候的照片，有些已经褪色发黄。爸妈从 90 年代开始收集，那时还没有数码相机，胶卷拿去店里冲洗，每张都收进这个盒子；搬家几次盒子都跟着走。它重要是因为承载着儿时回忆：亲戚来访时一起翻照片讲故事，对我来说这些照片是通往童年的桥，让我想起在爷爷奶奶家度过的夏天和已经不在的人。这是家里用钱换不来的东西，装着全家人的历史。

questions.question_en: What things do families keep for a long time?
questions.answer_en: Generally speaking, families tend to keep things that carry memories or practical value. Photos, letters and jewellery are common, because they remind people of important moments and loved ones. Some families also keep furniture or tools that have been passed down, especially if they were handmade or expensive. I think the common thread is that these objects connect people to their past, which is why they're hard to throw away.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 家庭一般会保存承载回忆或有实用价值的东西：照片、信件、首饰很常见，因为它们让人想起重要时刻和亲人；有些家庭还保存传下来的家具或工具，尤其是手工制作或昂贵的。共同点是这些物品把人和过去连在一起，所以舍不得扔。

questions.question_en: What's the difference between things valued by people in the past and today?
questions.answer_en: Compared with the past, the things people value have changed quite a lot. In the past, objects were often kept because they were rare or expensive, like a watch or a piece of furniture, and people repaired things instead of replacing them. Nowadays, most products are cheap and easy to buy, so people tend to value experiences and digital memories more, like photos on their phones. That said, I think the emotional value of certain items, like family photos, hasn't really changed.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 和过去相比，人们看重的东西变化很大。过去物品常因稀有或昂贵而被保存，比如手表、家具，东西坏了会修而不是换；现在产品便宜易得，人们更看重体验和数字记忆，比如手机里的照片。不过某些物品的情感价值，比如家庭照片，其实没怎么变。

questions.question_en: What kinds of things are kept in museums?
questions.answer_en: Museums usually keep objects that have historical, cultural or artistic value. For example, ancient pottery, paintings, old documents and traditional costumes are all common exhibits. Some museums also display everyday items from the past, like old tools or household goods, which help visitors understand how people lived. I think the purpose is to preserve things that would otherwise be lost, so future generations can see and learn from them.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 博物馆通常保存有历史、文化或艺术价值的物品：古代陶器、绘画、旧文献、传统服饰都是常见展品；有些博物馆还展出过去的日常用品，如旧工具、家用物品，帮助参观者了解当时人们的生活。目的是保存那些否则会消失的东西，让后代能看到和学习。

questions.question_en: What's the influence of technology on museums?
questions.answer_en: Technology has changed museums in quite positive ways. Many museums now use screens, audio guides and even virtual reality to make exhibits more engaging, so visitors can see how ancient buildings looked or how people lived. Technology also makes museums more accessible, since people can take virtual tours online without travelling. Having said that, I don't think technology replaces the real objects, it just makes the experience richer and easier to understand.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 科技给博物馆带来了相当积极的变化。很多博物馆用屏幕、语音导览甚至虚拟现实让展品更有吸引力，参观者能看到古代建筑的样子或人们的生活；科技也让博物馆更容易接近，人们不用出门就能在线虚拟参观。不过科技不会取代真实展品，只是让体验更丰富、更容易理解。

questions.question_en: What are the benefits of technology for learning history?
questions.answer_en: I think technology makes history much easier to learn. With videos, 3D models and online archives, students can see historical events and objects in a vivid way, instead of just reading about them in textbooks. For example, a 3D model of an ancient city is far more memorable than a written description. Technology also allows people to access historical materials from anywhere, which means learning history is no longer limited to the classroom.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 科技让学历史容易得多。通过视频、3D 模型和在线档案，学生能生动地看到历史事件和文物，而不是只读课本；比如古代城市的 3D 模型比文字描述好记得多。科技还让人随时随地获取历史资料，学历史不再局限于教室。

questions.question_en: Why do people visit museums?
questions.answer_en: People visit museums for different reasons. Some go to learn about history and culture, because museums present information in a reliable and organised way. Others go for entertainment, especially when museums hold special exhibitions or interactive displays. In my country, many young people also visit museums to take photos and share them online. I think the main attraction is that museums offer both knowledge and experience in one place.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 人们去博物馆的原因各不相同。有人为了了解历史和文化，因为博物馆以可靠、有条理的方式呈现信息；有人为了娱乐，尤其是特展或互动展览；国内很多年轻人还去拍照发网上。主要吸引力是博物馆把知识和体验放在了一起。

topics.title_zh: 描述一个未来你想做的完美工作
topics.title_en: Describe a perfect job you would like to have in the future

questions.question_en: Describe a perfect job you would like to have in the future
questions.question_zh: 描述一个未来你想做的完美工作。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about a job I think would be perfect for me, and that's being a librarian. It might sound unusual for a computer science student, but the more I think about it, the more it appeals to me.

First of all, what the job is: a librarian manages books and other resources in a library, helping people find what they need, organising the collection and keeping the space quiet and welcoming. It's not a high-pressure job, and it involves working with books and people all day, which sounds quite pleasant to me.

As for how I knew about it, I actually spent a lot of time in libraries during high school and university. I used to go to the city library to study, and I noticed how calm and organised the librarians were. They always seemed relaxed, and I remember thinking that if I could work in such a peaceful environment, I'd enjoy going to work every day.

To get this job, I'd need to learn library science, including how to classify books, manage digital catalogues and use library software. Since I'm studying computer science, the digital side wouldn't be too hard for me to pick up.

The reason it's my perfect job is that it combines a quiet environment with meaningful work. I'm not a fan of stressful, fast-paced jobs, and being surrounded by books while helping people find information sounds ideal. Looking back, I think a job that lets me stay calm and useful at the same time is exactly what I want.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲的是理想工作：图书管理员。对计算机专业学生来说可能有点意外，但越想越喜欢。工作内容是管理图书馆的书籍和资源，帮人找书、整理馆藏、保持环境安静舒适，不是高压工作，整天和书与人打交道。怎么知道的：高中和大学常去图书馆自习，注意到图书管理员都很平静、有条理，看起来轻松，心想能在这么安静的环境工作，每天上班都会开心。要得到这份工作需要学图书馆学：图书分类、数字目录管理、图书馆软件；因为学计算机，数字部分不难上手。为什么完美：安静的环境加有意义的工作，我不喜欢压力大节奏快的工作，被书包围着帮人找信息听起来很理想。

questions.question_en: What kind of job can be called a 'dream job'?
questions.answer_en: I think a dream job is one that matches a person's interests and gives them a sense of satisfaction, rather than just a high salary. For example, someone who loves music might dream of being a musician, even if it doesn't pay well. A dream job usually also offers a good work-life balance, so people don't feel exhausted after work. Of course, what counts as a dream job varies from person to person, since everyone values different things.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 理想工作应该是符合个人兴趣、带来满足感的工作，而不只是高薪。比如爱音乐的人可能梦想当音乐家，即使收入不高。理想工作通常还有好的工作生活平衡，下班后不会精疲力竭。当然，什么算理想工作因人而异，每个人看重的东西不同。

questions.question_en: What jobs do children want to do when they grow up?
questions.answer_en: Children usually dream of jobs that seem exciting or impressive, like being a doctor, a pilot, a teacher or a scientist. These jobs are often shown in cartoons and storybooks, so children find them attractive. Some children also copy what their parents do, especially if their parents talk about their work at home. I think children's choices are mostly based on imagination, since they don't really understand what the jobs involve yet.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 孩子通常梦想看起来刺激或了不起的工作：医生、飞行员、老师、科学家。这些职业常在动画片和故事书里出现，所以对孩子有吸引力；有些孩子还会模仿父母，尤其当父母在家谈论工作时。孩子的选择大多基于想象，因为他们还不真正了解这些工作具体做什么。

questions.question_en: Do people's ideal jobs change as they grow up?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think people's ideal jobs change quite a lot as they grow up. When they're young, people often choose jobs based on interest or fame, but as they get older, they start to consider practical factors like salary, stability and work-life balance. For example, a teenager might want to be a professional gamer, but later realise it's not a reliable career. So I'd say ideal jobs become more realistic with age and experience.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 是的，人的理想工作会随成长变化很大。年轻时往往凭兴趣或名气选职业，长大后开始考虑实际因素：薪水、稳定性、工作生活平衡。比如青少年可能想当职业电竞选手，后来发现这不是可靠的职业。理想工作会随年龄和经验变得更现实。

questions.question_en: What should people consider when choosing jobs?
questions.answer_en: People should consider several factors when choosing a job. First, whether the job matches their skills and interests, since it's hard to do well in something you don't enjoy. Second, practical matters like salary, working hours and job security, because these affect daily life. Third, the opportunities for growth, since a job with no future can feel like a dead end. On balance, I think the key is to find a balance between personal satisfaction and practical needs.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 选工作要考虑几个因素：第一，工作是否匹配自己的技能和兴趣，不喜欢的事很难做好；第二，实际因素如薪水、工时、工作保障，这些影响日常生活；第三，成长机会，没有前途的工作像死胡同。关键是找到个人满足感和实际需求之间的平衡。

questions.question_en: Is salary the main reason why people choose a certain job?
questions.answer_en: I'd say salary is important, but it's not the only reason people choose a job. For many people, especially those supporting a family, a good salary is essential, and it can be the deciding factor. However, other things matter too, like job satisfaction, work environment and career prospects. In fact, some people leave well-paid jobs because they find the work stressful or boring. So I think salary is a major factor, but not the main one for everyone.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 薪水重要，但不是人们选工作的唯一原因。对很多人，尤其是养家的人，好薪水是必须的，可能是决定因素；但其他东西也重要：工作满意度、工作环境、职业前景。事实上有人离开高薪工作是因为觉得压力大或无聊。薪水是主要因素，但不是对所有人都是最主要的。

questions.question_en: What kind of jobs are the most popular in your country?
questions.answer_en: In my country, jobs in technology and finance are very popular, because they offer high salaries and good career prospects. Many young people study computer science or business with the hope of working for big tech companies or banks. Government jobs are also popular, since they're stable and secure. That said, I think popularity changes over time, and these days more people are also interested in creative and service industries.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 国内科技和金融类工作很受欢迎，因为薪水高、前景好。很多年轻人学计算机或商科，希望进大科技公司或银行；公务员工作也受欢迎，因为稳定有保障。不过受欢迎程度随时间变化，现在也有更多人关注创意和服务行业。

topics.title_zh: 描述一个你想在国外做的短期工作
topics.title_en: Describe a short-term job you want to have in a foreign country

questions.question_en: Describe a short-term job you want to have in a foreign country
questions.question_zh: 描述一个你想在国外做的短期工作。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about a short-term job I'd love to do in a foreign country, and that's teaching Chinese. I've been thinking about this for a while, and it seems like a perfect fit for me.

First of all, where it is: I'd like to do this in a country where Chinese isn't widely spoken, maybe in Europe or Southeast Asia, like Thailand or France. The idea is to spend a few months there, teaching basic Chinese to local students or adults who are interested in the language.

As for how I know about it, I've seen a lot of videos and articles about Chinese teachers working abroad, and some of my friends have done volunteer teaching programmes. They said it was a great experience, because you get to travel, meet new people and share your culture at the same time. That really inspired me.

What the job involves is teaching everyday Chinese, like greetings, numbers and simple conversations, and sometimes introducing Chinese culture, such as festivals and food. Since I'm a native speaker, I can handle the language part easily, and I'm good at explaining things clearly.

The reason I want to do it is that it combines travel with something I'm actually good at. I've always wanted to see more of the world, and teaching Chinese would let me earn a little money while I'm there, instead of just spending. Looking back, I think it would be a meaningful way to spend a few months, and it might even help me decide what to do in the future.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲的是想在国外做的短期工作：教中文。地点：中文不普及的国家，欧洲或东南亚，比如泰国、法国，待几个月，教当地学生或成人基础中文。怎么知道的：看过很多中国老师出国教书的视频和文章，有朋友做过志愿教学项目，说既能旅行、认识新朋友又能分享文化，很受启发。工作内容：教日常中文，问候语、数字、简单对话，有时介绍中国文化如节日和美食；作为母语者语言部分轻松，而且我擅长清楚讲解。为什么想做：把旅行和自己擅长的事结合起来，一直想多看看世界，教中文还能边赚点钱；可能还会帮自己决定未来的方向。

questions.question_en: What short-term jobs do young people do in other countries?
questions.answer_en: Young people often take short-term jobs like working in cafés, restaurants or shops, especially during holidays. Some also do farm work, like picking fruit, or teach languages, such as English or Chinese. These jobs are popular because they don't require long-term commitment and they allow young people to earn money while travelling. I think the main appeal is that they offer a chance to experience life in another country without staying there permanently.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 年轻人常做短期工作，比如假期在咖啡馆、餐厅或商店打工；也有人做农活，如摘水果，或教语言，如英语、中文。这些工作受欢迎是因为不需要长期承诺，还能边旅行边赚钱。主要吸引力是能体验另一个国家的生活，又不用永久留下。

questions.question_en: What challenges do young people face when working abroad?
questions.answer_en: There are several challenges. The most obvious one is the language barrier, since it's hard to communicate with colleagues and customers if you don't speak the local language well. Another challenge is adapting to a different culture, including food, working habits and social rules, which can be stressful at first. On top of that, young people may feel lonely or homesick, especially if they're far from family and friends. So I'd say working abroad requires both language skills and emotional strength.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 挑战有几个。最明显的是语言障碍，当地语言不好就很难和同事、顾客沟通；另一个是适应不同文化，包括食物、工作习惯、社交规则，一开始会有压力；此外年轻人可能感到孤独或想家，尤其远离亲友。在国外工作既需要语言能力也需要心理承受力。

questions.question_en: What are the benefits of working for an international company?
questions.answer_en: Working for an international company has quite a few benefits. First, employees get to work with people from different countries, which broadens their view and improves their communication skills. Second, international companies often offer better training and clearer career paths, since they follow global standards. Third, the experience looks good on a resume and can open doors to opportunities abroad. Having said that, the pressure can be higher, but on the whole I think the benefits outweigh the drawbacks.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 在国际公司工作好处不少：第一，能和来自不同国家的人共事，开阔眼界、提升沟通能力；第二，国际公司通常培训更好、职业路径更清晰，因为遵循全球标准；第三，这段经历写在简历上很好看，还能打开海外机会。不过压力可能更大，但总体利大于弊。

questions.question_en: What personal skills are required to work in an international company?
questions.answer_en: I think the most important skill is communication, because you need to work with people from different backgrounds and express your ideas clearly. Language ability is part of this, but so is the ability to listen and understand different perspectives. Flexibility is also essential, since international companies often have different working styles and time zones. On top of that, being open-minded and willing to learn helps a lot, because you'll constantly meet new situations.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 最重要的技能是沟通，因为要和不同背景的人共事、清楚表达想法；语言能力是其中一部分，倾听和理解不同视角的能力同样重要。灵活性也必不可少，国际公司常有不同的工作风格和时区；此外开放心态和愿意学习很有帮助，因为会不断遇到新情况。

questions.question_en: What kind of work can young people do in foreign countries?
questions.answer_en: Young people can do quite a wide range of work abroad. Many start with service jobs, like working in restaurants, hotels or shops, which are easy to find and don't require special qualifications. Others do teaching, especially teaching their native language, or work as au pairs looking after children. Some young people also do internships or seasonal work, like working at ski resorts or summer camps. I think the choice depends on their skills and how long they plan to stay.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 年轻人在国外能做的工作范围很广。很多人从服务行业开始，如餐厅、酒店、商店，容易找且不需要特殊资质；也有人做教学，尤其是教母语，或做互惠生照看孩子；还有人做实习或季节性工作，如在滑雪场或夏令营。选择取决于技能和计划停留的时间。

questions.question_en: Why are some people unwilling to work in other countries?
questions.answer_en: There are several reasons why people are unwilling to work abroad. The biggest one is probably family, since many people don't want to be far from their parents, spouse or children. Language and cultural differences also make people hesitate, because they worry about not fitting in or struggling to communicate. On top of that, some people are satisfied with their jobs at home and don't see the need to take such a big risk. So I'd say it's a combination of practical and emotional concerns.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 人们不愿出国工作的原因有几个。最大的可能是家庭，很多人不想离父母、配偶或孩子太远；语言和文化差异也让人犹豫，担心融入不了或沟通困难；此外有些人对国内的工作满意，觉得没必要冒这么大风险。这是实际和情感因素的综合。

topics.title_zh: 描述你电脑或手机上的一个程序或APP
topics.title_en: Describe a program or app on your computer or phone

questions.question_en: Describe a program or app on your computer or phone
questions.question_zh: 描述你电脑或手机上的一个程序或APP。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about WeChat, which is the app I use most often on my phone. It's basically a messaging app, but in my country it's become much more than that.

First of all, what it is: WeChat is a social and messaging app developed in China. You can send text messages, voice messages and photos, make video calls, and share moments with your friends, which is like a personal feed. It's also used for payments, so many people use it to pay for things in shops and restaurants.

As for how often I use it, honestly, I use it every day, probably dozens of times. It's the first app I open in the morning and the last one I check before I go to sleep. I mainly use it to chat with my friends and family, especially my girlfriend, and to keep up with group chats for my classes and hobbies.

I found it a long time ago, back in middle school, when everyone around me started using it. At first I only used it to message friends, but over the years it's become a part of daily life, since almost everything, from paying bills to booking things, can be done through it.

The reason I feel so strongly about it is that it keeps me connected to the people I care about. Even though I don't see my friends every day, we can still share what's happening in our lives through WeChat. Looking back, I think it's not just an app for me, it's how I stay close to the people around me.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲的是微信，我手机上用得最多的应用。它本质是聊天软件，但在国内已经远不止如此。功能：发文字、语音、照片，视频通话，发朋友圈（像个人动态），还能支付，很多人用它付款。使用频率：每天用，一天几十次，早上第一个打开、睡前最后一个看；主要和亲友聊天，尤其是女朋友，还有班级和兴趣群聊。怎么发现的：初中时周围人都在用，一开始只用来发消息，后来成了生活的一部分，缴费、订东西都能用它。感受：它让我和在乎的人保持联系，即使不每天见面也能分享生活。对我来说它不只是应用，而是和身边人保持亲近的方式。

questions.question_en: What are the differences between old and young people when using apps?
questions.answer_en: I think the main difference is how easily they adapt. Young people pick up new apps quickly and use them for many purposes, like entertainment, shopping and socialising. Older people, on the other hand, tend to use only a few apps and prefer simple ones, like messaging or news apps. They also need more time to learn new features and sometimes ask younger family members for help. So I'd say young people are more flexible, while older people value simplicity.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 主要区别是适应能力。年轻人学新应用很快，用途也多：娱乐、购物、社交；老年人往往只用少数几个应用，偏好简单的，如聊天或新闻应用，学新功能需要更多时间，有时还向年轻家人求助。年轻人更灵活，老年人更看重简单。

questions.question_en: Why do some people not like using apps?
questions.answer_en: There are a few reasons. Some people find apps complicated and confusing, especially older users who didn't grow up with smartphones. Others worry about privacy, since many apps collect personal data, and some people are concerned about spending too much time on their phones. On top of that, some people simply prefer face-to-face communication and feel that apps make relationships less personal. So I think it's a mix of practical difficulty and personal preference.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 原因有几个。有些人觉得应用复杂难懂，尤其是没在智能手机时代长大的老年用户；有人担心隐私，因为很多应用收集个人数据，还有人担心在手机上花太多时间；此外有些人就是更喜欢面对面交流，觉得应用让关系变得不那么个人化。这是实际困难和个人偏好的混合。

questions.question_en: What apps are popular in your country? Why?
questions.answer_en: In my country, WeChat is probably the most popular app, because it combines messaging, payments and social media in one place, which means people use it for almost everything. Short video apps like Douyin are also extremely popular, since they're entertaining and easy to use. Shopping apps like Taobao are widely used too, because they make buying things convenient. I think these apps succeed because they're simple, useful and deeply connected to daily life.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 国内最流行的应用大概是微信，因为它把聊天、支付和社交媒体合在一起，人们几乎用它做所有事；抖音这类短视频应用也非常流行，有趣又易用；淘宝等购物应用也广泛使用，因为买东西方便。这些应用成功是因为简单、实用、和日常生活紧密相连。

questions.question_en: Should parents limit their children's use of computer programs and computer games? Why and how?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think parents should set some limits, because too much screen time can affect children's health, eyesight and schoolwork. That said, completely banning games isn't a good idea either, since games can be a way to relax and even learn. A better approach is to set reasonable time limits, like one or two hours a day, and to encourage children to balance gaming with outdoor activities and homework. I think the key is guidance rather than strict control.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 是的，父母应该设一些限制，因为屏幕时间过长会影响孩子的健康、视力和学业。不过完全禁止游戏也不好，游戏可以是放松甚至学习的方式。更好的做法是设合理的时间限制，比如每天一两小时，并鼓励孩子平衡游戏、户外活动和作业。关键是引导而不是严格控制。

questions.question_en: Do you think young people are more and more reliant on these programs?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think young people are becoming increasingly reliant on apps, and it's hard to imagine life without them. We use apps for communication, study, work, shopping and entertainment, so almost every part of daily life depends on them. This has made things more convenient, but it also means young people may struggle when they can't use their phones, and some find it hard to focus without checking apps constantly. So I'd say the reliance is real, and it has both positive and negative sides.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 是的，年轻人越来越依赖应用，很难想象没有它们的生活。我们用应用沟通、学习、工作、购物、娱乐，日常生活几乎每个部分都依赖它们。这让事情更方便，但也意味着不能用手机时年轻人会难受，有些人总忍不住刷应用、难以专注。依赖是真实的，有好有坏。

questions.question_en: What do you think about some countries banning children from using social media?
questions.answer_en: I think the intention behind such bans is understandable, since social media can expose children to harmful content and affect their mental health. However, I'm not sure a complete ban is the best solution, because social media also helps children stay connected with friends and learn new things. A more practical approach might be age limits and parental supervision, so children can use these platforms safely. On balance, I'd say the goal is right, but the method needs to be more flexible.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 这类禁令的初衷可以理解，社交媒体可能让孩子接触有害内容、影响心理健康。但我不确定完全禁止是最好的办法，因为社交媒体也帮孩子和朋友保持联系、学习新东西。更实际的做法可能是年龄限制和家长监督，让孩子安全使用。总体目标是对的，但方式需要更灵活。

topics.title_zh: 描述一件你花钱超过预期的物品
topics.title_en: Describe an item on which you spent more than expected

questions.question_en: Describe an item on which you spent more than expected
questions.question_zh: 描述一件你花钱超过预期的物品。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about a graphics card I bought last year, which ended up costing me much more than I planned. It's a piece of computer hardware that makes games and software run smoothly.

First of all, what it is: a graphics card, or GPU, is the part of a computer that handles images and video. It's essential for gaming, and it also helps with tasks like video editing and running certain programs. I bought a mid-to-high-end model, which was a big upgrade from my old one.

As for how much I spent, I originally planned to spend around one thousand yuan, but in the end I paid more than double that. I remember hesitating for a long time before I finally clicked the buy button, because it was a lot of money for me as a student.

The reason I bought it was mainly for gaming. My old card couldn't run newer games smoothly, and I'd been saving up for a while. But while I was researching, I watched a lot of reviews, and the more I saw, the more I wanted a better model. I also realised that a stronger card would help with my coding work, since some programs run much faster with a good GPU.

The reason I spent more than expected is that I kept convincing myself that the extra money was worth it. Looking back, I do feel a bit guilty about the cost, but the card has worked well for both gaming and study, so I think it was a reasonable decision in the end.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲的是去年买的一张显卡，最后花的钱远超计划。显卡是电脑里处理图像和视频的部件，打游戏必需，也帮助视频剪辑和运行某些程序；我买的是中高端型号，比旧卡升级很大。花了多少：原本计划一千多块，最后付了超过两倍的钱，下单前犹豫了很久，对学生来说是一大笔钱。为什么买：主要是打游戏，旧卡跑不动新游戏，攒了一段时间钱；但研究时看了很多测评，越看越想要更好的型号，还意识到好显卡对写代码也有帮助，有些程序跑得快很多。为什么超支：一直说服自己多花的钱值得。回头看有点心疼，但显卡打游戏和学习都好用，所以觉得最终是合理的决定。

questions.question_en: Do you often buy more than you expected?
questions.answer_en: Not very often, but it does happen sometimes. Usually it's with things I'm really interested in, like electronics, because I start comparing models and end up choosing a more expensive one. For everyday items, though, I tend to stick to my budget. I think it's easy to overspend when you're excited about something, but I try to remind myself to think twice before paying.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不常发生，但偶尔会有。通常是对真正感兴趣的东西，比如电子产品，因为开始比较型号，最后选了更贵的。日常用品一般会守住预算。对某样东西兴奋时容易超支，但我尽量提醒自己付款前多想一下。

questions.question_en: What do you think young people spend most of their money on?
questions.answer_en: I think young people spend most of their money on entertainment and technology. Many spend a lot on phones, computers and games, since these are central to their daily lives. Eating out and ordering food is another big expense, because it's convenient and social. Some also spend on clothes and travel. I'd say the common pattern is that young people prefer spending on experiences and things that make life more enjoyable, rather than saving for the future.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 年轻人大部分钱花在娱乐和科技上。很多人在手机、电脑、游戏上花很多，因为这些是日常生活的核心；外出吃饭和点外卖是另一大开销，方便又社交；也有人花在衣服和旅行上。共同模式是年轻人更喜欢把钱花在体验和让生活更有趣的东西上，而不是为未来存钱。

questions.question_en: Do you think it is important to save money? Why?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think saving money is very important, even though it's not always easy. Life is unpredictable, and having savings means you can deal with emergencies, like sudden medical costs or losing a job, without panicking. Saving also makes it possible to achieve bigger goals, like buying a house or travelling. That said, I don't think people should save every penny, since enjoying life now also matters. So I'd say the key is to save regularly but keep a balance.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 是的，存钱非常重要，虽然不容易。生活不可预测，有存款就能应对突发情况，比如突然的医疗费用或失业，不至于慌乱；存钱也让人能实现更大的目标，如买房或旅行。不过我不认为应该省下每一分钱，享受当下也很重要。关键是定期存钱但保持平衡。

questions.question_en: Do people buy things they don't need?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think almost everyone buys things they don't really need from time to time. This often happens because of advertising and promotions, which make people feel they're getting a good deal. Online shopping makes it even easier, since you can buy something with one click without thinking much. Social media also plays a role, because people see others with new products and want the same. So I'd say unnecessary buying is very common, and it's something most people need to watch out for.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 是的，几乎每个人都会时不时买不需要的东西。这常因为广告和促销让人觉得自己占了便宜；网购让这更容易，一键下单不用多想；社交媒体也有影响，看到别人有新东西就想要同款。不必要的购买很常见，是大多数人需要警惕的事。

questions.question_en: Do you think it is the rich people's responsibility to donate money to people in need?
questions.answer_en: I think it's a moral responsibility rather than a legal one. Rich people have more resources, so it's reasonable to expect them to contribute more to society, and many of them do donate to charities. However, I don't think it should be forced, because people should give willingly, and some rich people already create jobs and pay taxes, which also helps society. On balance, I'd say donating is admirable and encouraged, but it shouldn't be made compulsory.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 我认为这是道德责任而不是法律责任。富人资源更多，期望他们为社会贡献更多是合理的，很多富人确实捐给慈善机构。但我不认为应该强制，因为人应该自愿给予，而且有些富人已经创造就业、纳税，同样帮助社会。总体捐款值得赞赏和鼓励，但不应该强制。

questions.question_en: What kind of things are people happy to pay a high price for?
questions.answer_en: People are usually happy to pay a high price for things that matter to them personally. For example, many people spend a lot on health, like good medical care or gym memberships, because they value their wellbeing. Others pay for experiences, such as travel or concerts, since these create lasting memories. Technology is another example, as people are willing to pay for the latest phones or computers. I think the common factor is that people pay more for things that bring them happiness or convenience.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 人们通常愿意为对自己重要的东西付高价。比如很多人花很多钱在健康上，如好的医疗服务或健身房会员，因为重视健康；有人为体验付费，如旅行或演唱会，因为这些创造持久的回忆；科技是另一个例子，人们愿意为最新款手机或电脑付钱。共同点是人们为带来快乐或便利的东西付更多钱。

topics.title_zh: 描述你做过的一个重大决定
topics.title_en: Describe an important decision that you made

questions.question_en: Describe an important decision that you made
questions.question_zh: 描述你做过的一个重大决定。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about the decision to choose computer science as my major at university, which I made when I was filling in my college application forms in my final year of high school.

The decision itself was pretty clear in the end, but getting there took a while. I'd loved computers since I was a kid, always playing around with them, and in high school I had an IT teacher who taught me some basic programming during lunch breaks. He told me that if I was that interested, I should seriously consider it as a career. So when it came to choosing a major, I did a lot of research online, compared different universities, and talked it over with my parents, who were supportive as long as I was sure about it.

As for the results, I'd say they've been very positive so far. I enjoy most of my courses, I've picked up skills that feel genuinely useful, and I've even built a few small projects on my own. It's confirmed that I made the right call.

The reason it was so important is that it basically decided my career path. Everything I study now, and probably the job I'll do later, flows from that one choice. Looking back, I think it was the first really big decision I made entirely for myself, and it taught me to trust my own interests.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 我讲的是高考填志愿时选择计算机科学与技术专业这个决定。我从小就爱玩电脑，高中信息技术老师午休时教我基础编程，鼓励我考虑这个方向；报志愿时我上网查资料、对比学校，也和爸妈商量，他们支持我。结果很正面：课程喜欢、学到实用技能、还自己做了小项目。之所以重要，是因为它基本决定了我的职业方向，也是我第一次完全为自己做的重大决定。

questions.question_en: Do you think children sometimes have to make important decisions?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think they do, though the decisions are important in a different way from adults'. For example, children often have to choose which subjects to focus on, or which hobbies to keep, and those choices can shape their interests for years. Having said that, I don't think children should carry the full weight of big decisions, because they lack experience. So I'd say they make important decisions, but usually with guidance from adults.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 是的，孩子也会做重要决定，只是和成人的重要方式不同。比如选重点科目、保留哪个爱好，这些会影响兴趣好几年。但孩子缺乏经验，不该独自承担重大决定的分量，通常需要大人引导。

questions.question_en: What important decisions do teenagers need to make after graduation?
questions.answer_en: I'd say the biggest one is choosing their further education path, whether to go to university, which major to pick, or whether to enter the workforce directly. In my country, this choice basically decides a person's career direction, so it carries a lot of pressure. Another important decision is where to live, since many teenagers move to bigger cities for study or work. These choices are hard because teenagers often don't know yet what they really want.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 最大的决定是升学路径：上不上大学、选什么专业、还是直接工作。在我国这基本决定职业方向，压力很大。另一个是去哪生活，很多青少年会去大城市。难就难在青少年往往还不知道自己真正想要什么。

questions.question_en: Who can children turn to for help when making a decision?
questions.answer_en: Generally speaking, children usually turn to their parents first, because parents know them best and have more life experience. Teachers are also a common source of help, especially for academic decisions, since they see the child's strengths in a school setting. These days, I'd also say the internet plays a role, because children can research options themselves. Having said that, I think the most reliable advice still comes from people who know the child personally.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 孩子一般先找父母，因为父母最了解他们、经验也更多。老师也常被求助，尤其学业决定，因为老师看得见孩子的长处。现在网络也起作用，孩子能自己查资料。但最可靠的建议还是来自真正了解孩子的人。

questions.question_en: Do you think advertisements can influence our decisions when shopping?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think advertisements influence us more than we realise. They work by creating desire, so when we see a product presented in an attractive way, we start to believe we need it. For example, in my country, online ads follow people around based on what they've searched, which makes it very hard to resist. Having said that, I think most people are becoming more aware of this, and they compare reviews before buying, so the influence isn't total.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 是的，广告对我们的影响比想象中大。它通过制造欲望起作用，把产品包装得吸引人，我们就开始觉得需要它。比如国内线上广告会根据搜索记录追着人推，很难抗拒。但多数人越来越有意识，买前会看评价，所以影响不是绝对的。

questions.question_en: Do you think the influence of advertising is good?
questions.answer_en: I'd say it's a mixed picture. On one hand, advertising helps people discover new products and services, and it supports a lot of free content online, which is clearly beneficial. On the other hand, it can push people to buy things they don't need, and some ads are misleading. On balance, I think advertising itself is neutral, but it becomes a problem when it's dishonest or targets vulnerable people, like children. So the influence depends a lot on how it's used.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 好坏参半。一方面广告帮人发现新产品、支撑大量免费内容，明显有益；另一方面会推着人买不需要的东西，有些广告还误导人。总体看广告本身是中性的，但一旦不诚实或针对儿童等弱势群体就成了问题，所以影响取决于怎么用。

questions.question_en: How do people usually make important decisions?
questions.answer_en: I think most people start by gathering information, so they research the options and compare the pros and cons. After that, many people ask for advice from family or friends, because a second opinion can reveal things they've missed. Some people also rely on their gut feeling, especially when the options seem equally good. Having said that, I believe the most sensible approach is a combination, using both careful analysis and personal instinct.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 多数人先收集信息，查选项、对比利弊；然后会问家人朋友的意见，因为旁观者能看出自己漏掉的东西。也有人靠直觉，尤其当选项看起来差不多时。最明智的做法是两者结合：认真分析加个人直觉。

topics.title_zh: 描述一次你很早就起床的经历
topics.title_en: Describe a time when you got up early

questions.question_en: Describe a time when you got up early
questions.question_zh: 描述一次你很早就起床的经历。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to describe a time when I got up really early, earlier than I ever do normally. It happened about a year ago, during the summer holidays, when I was staying at home with my family.

The funny thing is, I didn't plan to get up early at all. I woke up around five in the morning, before the sun had even come up, and I just couldn't get back to sleep. I lay there for a while, but my mind was already wide awake, so eventually I gave up and got out of bed.

Since there was nothing else to do at that hour, I went straight to my computer. I remember the house was completely quiet, and the sky outside was still dark. I spent the time browsing the internet, watching a few videos, and messing around with some code, which is what I usually do anyway. It felt strange to be doing my normal evening routine in the early morning.

As for how I felt, it was actually a mixed experience. On one hand, I enjoyed the peace and quiet, because there were no messages, no noise, nobody asking me anything. On the other hand, I felt a bit tired later in the day, and I ended up taking a long nap in the afternoon. Looking back, I think it was a nice change of pace, even though I wouldn't want to do it every day.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 我讲的是去年暑假一次特别早的早起。我根本没打算早起，早上五点左右醒来，太阳还没出来，就是睡不着，躺了一会儿干脆起床。那个点没事做，我就去开电脑，家里特别安静、窗外还黑着，我上网、看视频、写点代码，感觉像把晚上的日常搬到了清晨。感受很复杂：一方面享受安静，没人打扰；另一方面白天犯困，下午补了个长觉。偶尔一次不错，但不想天天这样。

questions.question_en: Do you know anyone who likes to get up early?
questions.answer_en: Yes, my grandfather is a good example. He gets up before sunrise every day and goes for a walk in the park, and he says it makes him feel healthy and energetic. I also have a classmate who wakes up at six to study before class, because she says the morning is the quietest time. So I do know early risers, though I have to admit I'm not one of them myself.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 有，我爷爷就是。他每天日出前起床去公园散步，说这样身体舒服、精神好。我还有个同学六点起来学习，说早上最安静。我确实认识爱早起的人，不过我自己不是。

questions.question_en: Why do people get up early?
questions.answer_en: There are several reasons. Some people get up early because of work or school, since they have to commute or start their day early. Others do it for health, because morning exercise is good for the body, and the air is fresher. A more personal reason is that some people simply enjoy the quiet time before the rest of the world wakes up, which lets them focus on their own things. So it's usually a mix of necessity and preference.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 原因有好几个。有人因为工作学习必须早起，要通勤或早开工；有人为了健康，晨练对身体好、空气也新鲜；还有人纯粹喜欢世界醒来前的安静，能专心做自己的事。通常是必要加偏好。

questions.question_en: What kinds of occasions need people to arrive early?
questions.answer_en: I'd say any occasion where being late would cause trouble for others. For example, exams, flights and trains all require people to arrive early, because they have fixed schedules. Job interviews and important meetings are similar, since arriving late creates a bad impression. In my country, people also arrive early for weddings and family gatherings, out of respect. So generally speaking, the more formal or time-sensitive the occasion, the earlier people should arrive.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 凡是迟到会给别人添麻烦的场合都要早到。比如考试、飞机、火车都有固定时间；面试和重要会议迟到会留下坏印象。在我国，婚礼和家庭聚会也会早到以示尊重。越正式、越讲究时间的场合越该早到。

questions.question_en: Why do some people like to stay up late?
questions.answer_en: I think the main reason is that the night is the only time that truly belongs to them. During the day, students and workers have to follow other people's schedules, so they only get free time in the evening, and they don't want to waste it by sleeping. Another factor is that phones and games are designed to keep people engaged, so it's easy to lose track of time. Having said that, I think staying up late is often a habit rather than a real preference.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 主要原因是夜晚才是真正属于自己的时间。白天学生和上班族都跟着别人的安排走，只有晚上有空，舍不得用来睡觉。另外手机和游戏设计得让人停不下来，很容易忘了时间。不过我觉得熬夜更多是习惯，不是真喜欢。

questions.question_en: Is it good to arrive early in any situation?
questions.answer_en: Not necessarily, I'd say. Arriving early is usually good, because it shows responsibility and gives you time to prepare. However, in some situations it can be wasteful, for example if you arrive an hour early for a meeting, you just end up waiting. There's also a social aspect, because in some cultures arriving too early for a dinner party can actually be inconvenient for the host. So on the whole, being early is safer than being late, but timing should still be sensible.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不一定。早到通常好，显得负责、有时间准备。但有些场合会浪费，比如开会早到一小时只能干等。还有社交因素，有些文化里赴宴到太早反而让主人不方便。总体早到比迟到安全，但时间也要合理。

questions.question_en: 待补充
questions.answer_en: First of all, I think it has to be gradual, because suddenly waking up at five after months of sleeping late rarely works. People can start by going to bed a little earlier each night, and setting a fixed alarm even on weekends. Another useful trick is to have a reason to get up, like exercise or a hobby, because motivation makes it much easier. Having said that, I think consistency matters most, since the body eventually adapts to a regular routine.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 首先得循序渐进，长期晚睡的人突然五点起很难坚持。可以每晚早睡一点，周末也定固定闹钟。另一个办法是给早起找个理由，比如锻炼或爱好，有动力就容易多了。但最重要的还是坚持，身体最终会适应规律作息。

topics.title_zh: 描述一次你团队合作的经验
topics.title_en: Describe a time when you worked in a group

questions.question_en: Describe a time when you worked in a group
questions.question_zh: 描述一次你团队合作的经验。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about a time when I worked in a group to organise a film screening for our university film club. It happened in my second year, and it was one of the first big events I helped arrange.

What I did was basically coordinate the whole thing. I was in charge of the schedule, which meant booking the room, picking a time that worked for most members, and making sure everything was ready on the day. I worked with a few classmates from the club, and we split the tasks, so some handled the posters and promotion while others dealt with the equipment.

The main problem we faced was that one of our teammates arrived late on the day of the event. We'd planned to start the screening at seven, but he was the one holding the projector, so we had to delay the whole thing by about twenty minutes. I remember feeling quite stressed, because people were already seated and waiting. In the end, I had to quickly rearrange the order of the programme and start with a short introduction to fill the time.

The reason I worked in the group, rather than doing it alone, is that an event like that simply needs more than one person. You need people to promote it, to set up the equipment, and to handle problems as they come up. Looking back, I think the experience taught me how important clear communication and backup plans are in teamwork.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 我讲的是大二时和电影社团的同学一起组织一次观影活动。我负责统筹：订场地、定时间、当天确认一切就绪；队友们分工，有人做海报宣传、有人管设备。最大的问题是活动当天有个队友迟到，他拿着投影仪，我们只好推迟二十分钟，观众都坐好了，我很紧张，最后临时调整流程、先放了个简短介绍来填时间。之所以要团队合作，是因为这种活动一个人做不来，需要有人宣传、有人装设备、有人处理突发状况。这次经历让我明白沟通和备用方案在团队里有多重要。

questions.question_en: Why do some people prefer to work by themselves?
questions.answer_en: I think it mainly comes down to control and pace. When people work alone, they can decide their own schedule, and they don't have to wait for others or explain their choices. Some people also find group work frustrating, because the workload isn't always shared fairly, and disagreements waste time. Having said that, I think working alone suits certain tasks better, while group work is better for bigger projects, so it really depends on the situation.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 主要在于掌控感和节奏。一个人做事能自己定时间，不用等别人、也不用解释自己的选择。还有人觉得团队合作烦人，因为分工不一定公平，争论也浪费时间。不过独立工作适合某些任务，大项目更适合团队，要看情况。

questions.question_en: What should a leader do to make team members want to follow him or her?
questions.answer_en: I'd say the most important thing is to communicate clearly, so everyone knows what they're responsible for and what the goal is. A good leader also listens to the team's ideas and gives credit where it's due, because people follow someone who respects them. In my experience, leaders who stay calm under pressure and solve problems quickly earn the most trust. So I think it's a combination of clear direction, fairness and reliability.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 最重要的是沟通清楚，让每个人知道自己的职责和目标。好领导还会听团队的想法、该表扬就表扬，因为人们愿意跟随尊重自己的人。以我的经验，压力下保持冷静、能快速解决问题的领导最受信任。所以是明确方向、公平和可靠三者的结合。

questions.question_en: Should students learn to do group work?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think it's essential, because almost every job today involves working with other people. Group work teaches students how to communicate, how to divide tasks, and how to handle disagreements, which are skills you can't learn from textbooks alone. In my country, employers often complain that graduates are technically strong but weak at collaboration, which shows how important this is. Having said that, group work should be well designed, so that everyone actually contributes.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 是的，非常必要，因为现在几乎每份工作都要和人合作。团队作业教学生怎么沟通、怎么分工、怎么处理分歧，这些是课本学不来的。在我国，雇主常抱怨毕业生技术强但协作弱，可见其重要性。不过团队任务要设计好，保证每个人都真正出力。

questions.question_en: What group tasks are there in schools?
questions.answer_en: There are quite a few. The most common one is group projects, where students research a topic together and present it as a team. Schools also organise group activities like sports competitions, drama performances and club events, such as our film club's screenings. In science classes, students often do experiments in small groups as well. So I'd say group tasks are everywhere in schools, and they all aim to teach students how to cooperate.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 挺多的。最常见的是小组作业，一起研究一个主题再上台展示。学校还有体育比赛、戏剧表演、社团活动这类团队任务，比如我们电影社团的观影活动。理科课上学生也常分组做实验。可以说学校里的团队任务无处不在，目的都是教学生合作。

questions.question_en: 待补充
questions.answer_en: I'd say it depends on the task. For simple tasks, working alone is usually faster, because there's no need to coordinate or discuss. But for complex projects, group work can be more efficient, since different people bring different skills, and tasks can be done in parallel. Having said that, group work only becomes efficient when the team is well organised, because poor communication can actually slow everything down. So on the whole, it's not the group itself, but how it's managed, that decides efficiency.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 要看任务。简单任务独自做更快，不用协调讨论；复杂项目团队更高效，因为不同人带来不同技能，还能并行推进。但团队只有在组织良好的时候才高效，沟通不畅反而拖慢一切。所以决定效率的不是团队本身，而是怎么管理。
