topics.title_zh: 描述一个你看过并喜欢的现场体育赛事
topics.title_en: Describe a live sports event you watched and liked

questions.question_en: Describe a live sports event you watched and liked
questions.question_zh: 描述一个你看过并喜欢的现场体育赛事。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about a live esports event I watched and really enjoyed, which was the final of a big League of Legends tournament. It took place last year, and I watched it at home, alone, on my computer.

The event itself was the world championship final, where two top teams from different regions were competing for the title. I'd been following the tournament for weeks, so I was really excited about the final match. I watched it live on a streaming platform, with the chat going crazy in the background, which made it feel almost like being in a stadium.

I watched it by myself, which might sound a bit lonely, but honestly it was perfect for me. I could focus completely on the game, pause to grab a snack, and cheer as loudly as I wanted without bothering anyone. The match went to five games, and the last one was incredibly tense, with both teams trading leads until the very end.

The reason I liked it so much is that I've played the game myself for years, so I could appreciate the skill and the strategy behind every move. Watching professional players do things I could never pull off was genuinely thrilling. All in all, it was one of the most exciting evenings I've had, and I still remember the final team fight clearly.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 我讲的是去年在家独自看的一场英雄联盟世界赛总决赛。我追了好几周，特别期待决赛，在直播平台看，弹幕刷得飞快，像在体育馆里一样。一个人看其实正合我意：能完全专注、随时暂停拿零食、想怎么喊就怎么喊。比赛打满五局，最后一局双方交替领先，紧张到极点。我之所以这么喜欢，是因为我自己玩这个游戏好几年，能看懂每一步背后的技巧和策略，看职业选手打出我永远做不到的操作真的很过瘾。那是我最兴奋的夜晚之一，最后那波团战我现在还记得。

questions.question_en: Why do some people like to watch sports events?
questions.answer_en: I think there are several reasons. First, watching sports is exciting, because the result is unpredictable and the tension keeps people engaged. Second, many people watch because they play the sport themselves, and they can appreciate the skill and learn from it. There's also a social side, because watching a match with friends or discussing it online creates a sense of belonging. So I'd say it's a mix of entertainment, interest and community.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 原因有好几个。首先看比赛很刺激，结果不可预测，紧张感让人投入；其次很多人自己也玩这项运动，能欣赏技巧、从中学习；还有社交因素，和朋友一起看或网上讨论会产生归属感。所以是娱乐、兴趣和社群感的结合。

questions.question_en: Where do people normally watch sports events?
questions.answer_en: These days, most people watch sports at home, either on television or on streaming platforms, because it's convenient and cheap. Some people also watch in public places like sports bars or cafes, especially when there's a big match, because the atmosphere is more exciting. Of course, fans who can afford it go to the stadium to watch live, which offers the most intense experience. So I'd say the choice depends on budget and how much people care about the atmosphere.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 现在多数人在家看，电视或流媒体平台，方便又便宜。也有人去体育酒吧、咖啡馆这类公共场所看，尤其大赛时气氛更带劲。当然，预算够的球迷会去现场，体验最强烈。所以选哪里取决于预算和对气氛的在意程度。

questions.question_en: What are the advantages of watching sports events online?
questions.answer_en: I think the biggest advantage is convenience, because people can watch from anywhere, on their phone or computer, without buying a ticket. Online platforms also offer more choice, since you can watch matches from other countries that aren't shown on local TV. Another benefit is flexibility, because you can pause, rewind, or watch highlights if you miss part of the game. Having said that, the main downside is that the atmosphere at home can't compare to being there in person.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 最大优势是方便，不用买票，手机电脑上随时能看。线上平台选择也多，能看本地电视不播的国外比赛。还有灵活性，可以暂停、回放，错过部分还能看集锦。不过缺点是家里的气氛没法跟现场比。

questions.question_en: What sports matches are suitable for children to attend?
questions.answer_en: I'd say matches that are relaxed and family-friendly are the most suitable. For example, school sports days and local amateur games are perfect, because the atmosphere is friendly and there's no risk of crowd trouble. Professional matches can also be fine, especially sports like swimming or athletics, where the crowd is generally calm. Having said that, I think parents should avoid very intense matches, like big football derbies, where the crowd can get aggressive and the noise might scare young children.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 轻松、适合家庭的比赛最合适。比如学校运动会和本地业余比赛就很好，气氛友好、没有人群风险。职业比赛也可以，尤其游泳、田径这类观众比较平静的项目。但家长应避免太激烈的比赛，比如大型足球德比，人群可能激动，噪音也会吓到小孩。

questions.question_en: 待补充
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think it can be, for many people. Watching a match takes your mind off daily stress, because you focus completely on the game, and the excitement can be a great release. For example, after a long week of work, many people look forward to watching their favourite team play. Having said that, it doesn't work for everyone, because some people get too nervous or angry when their team loses, which is the opposite of relaxing. So it depends on the person.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 对很多人来说是的。看比赛能把注意力从日常压力上移开，完全投入比赛，兴奋感本身就是一种释放。比如辛苦一周后，很多人就盼着看主队比赛。但对有些人不行，球队输了他们会紧张、生气，反而更累。所以因人而异。

topics.title_zh: 描述一次你为家人感到骄傲的时刻
topics.title_en: Describe a time when you felt proud of a family member

questions.question_en: Describe a time when you felt proud of a family member
questions.question_zh: 描述一次你为家人感到骄傲的时刻。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about a moment when I felt really proud of my younger brother. It happened last summer, when the results of his final exams came out, the big national exam that decides which university you get into. I remember sitting at home with my parents, all of us waiting nervously for the results to be released online.

My brother is two years younger than me, and honestly, he's always been the quieter one in the family. He never boasted about his studies, so we had no idea how well he had prepared. When the results finally appeared, he had scored far above the top-tier university line, which was way beyond what any of us expected. My parents were overjoyed, and my mum actually called all her relatives to share the news.

The reason I felt so proud of him is that I knew how much effort he had put in. For the whole year, he got up at six every morning to study, and he gave up most of his weekends. What struck me most was his calmness, because he never once complained about the pressure. To be honest, I also felt a little envious, because I wished my own scores had been as good as his. But mostly, I was genuinely proud, and I told him so that evening. Looking back, it's a moment I won't forget, because it showed me what quiet determination can achieve.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 去年夏天弟弟高考出分，远超一本线，全家惊喜；他一年来每天六点起床学习、放弃周末，从不抱怨，我既骄傲又有点羡慕，希望自己分数也那么高。

questions.question_en: When would parents feel proud of their children?
questions.answer_en: Generally speaking, parents feel proud when their children achieve something meaningful, like doing well in exams, winning a competition or showing kindness to others. In my country, academic success is probably the most common source of pride, because education is seen as the key to a better future. That said, I think parents feel even prouder when their children become independent and responsible, because that shows the values they taught have really taken root.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 父母在孩子取得成就时骄傲，如考试好、获奖、善良；我国最看重学业成功，但孩子独立负责更让父母自豪。

questions.question_en: Should parents reward children? Why and how?
questions.answer_en: I'd say yes, rewards can be helpful, but they need to be used sensibly. The main reason is that rewards give children a clear sense of achievement and encourage them to keep trying. However, I think the reward should be more about recognition than money, like extra family time or a favourite meal, so that children learn to value effort rather than just the prize.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 奖励有用但要适度；奖励给孩子成就感、鼓励坚持，但应重认可而非金钱，如家庭时间或喜欢的饭菜，让孩子重视努力本身。

questions.question_en: Is it good to reward children too often? Why?
questions.answer_en: Not really, I don't think so. If children are rewarded too often, they may start to expect a prize for everything they do, and they might lose their inner motivation. Having said that, occasional rewards are fine, as long as they are linked to real effort, because the goal is to build good habits, not to create a habit of bargaining.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 频繁奖励不好；孩子会期待事事有奖、失去内在动力，可能没奖励就不做事；偶尔奖励且与真实努力挂钩才合适。

questions.question_en: On what occasions would adults be proud of themselves?
questions.answer_en: I think adults feel proud of themselves when they overcome a real challenge, like getting a promotion, buying their first home or completing a difficult project. These moments matter because they represent years of effort. In my country, many adults also feel proud when they can support their parents financially, since that is seen as a sign of maturity. On the whole, I'd say pride for adults usually comes from achievements that prove their independence and capability.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 成年人克服真正挑战时自豪，如升职、买房、完成难项目；我国很多人以能赡养父母为傲，骄傲多来自证明独立与能力。

questions.question_en: Do rewards help a child become better?
questions.answer_en: To some extent, yes, they do. Rewards can encourage a child to repeat good behaviour, especially in the early years, when children are still learning what is right and wrong. For example, praising a child for sharing toys can make sharing a habit. However, I believe long-term improvement depends more on internal motivation, like curiosity and a sense of responsibility. So rewards are a useful starting point, but they shouldn't be the only reason a child behaves well.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 奖励有一定帮助，能鼓励孩子重复好行为；但长期进步更靠内在动力如好奇心和责任感，奖励只是起点。

questions.question_en: Do you think choosing a college major is closely related to a future career?
questions.answer_en: I'd say it's related, but not as closely as people often think. In my country, many graduates end up working in fields completely different from their major, because the job market changes quickly. For example, a friend of mine studied history but now works in marketing. Having said that, certain majors, like medicine or engineering, do lead directly to specific careers. So on the whole, a major opens doors, but it doesn't lock you into one path.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 专业与职业有关联但没那么紧密；我国很多毕业生转行，如学历史做营销；但医学、工程等专业直接对应职业，专业开门但不锁死道路。

topics.title_zh: 描述一次你需要发挥想象力的时刻
topics.title_en: Describe a time you needed to use your imagination

questions.question_en: Describe a time you needed to use your imagination
questions.question_zh: 描述一次你需要发挥想象力的时刻。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about a time when I really needed to use my imagination, and that was during my final year of high school. It was a period when I had to sit through long revision sessions, and honestly, I often felt extremely bored, especially during the afternoon classes when the teacher was just going over the same material again and again.

The reason I needed to use my imagination was simple, I had nothing else to do. We weren't allowed to use our phones in class, so whenever my mind drifted, I would start daydreaming to pass the time. I remember creating whole imaginary worlds in my head, like planning a trip around the world, designing my dream apartment, or even imagining what my life would be like after the exams, which university I would attend and what kind of job I might get.

As for how difficult it was, I'd say it was actually quite easy, because daydreaming comes naturally to me. The hard part was snapping back to reality when the teacher suddenly asked me a question. I remember being caught off guard a couple of times, which was a bit embarrassing.

Looking back, I think those daydreams were more than just a way to kill time. They gave me a sense of hope and motivation during a stressful period, and they made the boring hours pass much faster. So even though it sounds a little silly, I'm actually grateful for my imagination, because it turned dull moments into something enjoyable.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 高三复习课很无聊，不能玩手机，我就靠脑内异想天开打发时间，想象环球旅行、梦想公寓和考后生活；白日梦很容易做，但被老师点名会尴尬；它给了我希望和动力。

questions.question_en: Do you think adults can have lots of imagination?
questions.answer_en: Absolutely, I think adults can be just as imaginative as children, although they often hide it. The difference is that adults usually apply their imagination to practical things, like solving problems at work or planning for the future. For example, entrepreneurs need imagination to invent new products. Having said that, adults may lose some of their playful imagination because of daily routines and stress, and I think it's important for them to make time for creative activities.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 成年人同样有想象力，只是常隐藏；他们更多把想象用于实际，如工作解决问题、规划未来；但日常压力会消磨玩心，应留时间做创造性活动。

questions.question_en: Do you think imagination is essential for scientists?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I believe it's absolutely essential. Science isn't just about memorising facts, it's about imagining possibilities that don't exist yet. For instance, Einstein imagined riding on a beam of light before he developed his theory of relativity. Scientists also need imagination to design experiments and to picture how things might work. So in my view, imagination and logic work together in science, and without imagination, many great discoveries would never have been made.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 想象力对科学家至关重要；科学不只是记事实，而是想象尚未存在的可能，如爱因斯坦想象骑光束；设计实验也需要想象，想象与逻辑相辅相成。

questions.question_en: What kinds of jobs need imagination?
questions.answer_en: Quite a few jobs need imagination, but the most obvious ones are in the creative industries, like writers, designers, architects and advertising professionals, because they have to come up with original ideas every day. However, I'd argue that imagination matters in almost every job. For example, a teacher needs imagination to make lessons interesting, and even an engineer needs it to solve unusual problems. So I think imagination is valuable everywhere, it's just more visible in creative roles.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 创意行业最需要想象力，如作家、设计师、建筑师、广告人；但几乎所有工作都需要，老师要想象让课有趣，工程师要想象解决难题，只是创意岗位更明显。

questions.question_en: What subjects are helpful for children's imagination?
questions.answer_en: I'd say arts subjects are the most helpful, like drawing, music and drama, because they encourage children to express themselves freely. Literature is also great, since reading stories lets children picture whole worlds in their minds. That said, I don't think imagination is limited to the arts, because subjects like science and maths can also spark curiosity when taught well. So on the whole, the subject matters less than how it's taught, and children need a mix of both.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 艺术类科目最有助于想象力，如绘画、音乐、戏剧，文学也能让孩子在脑中构建世界；但科学数学教得好同样激发好奇，关键在教法而非科目本身。

questions.question_en: What games help develop children's imagination?
questions.answer_en: I think role-playing games are the best for developing imagination, because children have to create characters and stories themselves. Building games, like blocks or LEGO, are also great, since children have to picture what they want to create before they build it. Having said that, I think the key is that the game should be open-ended, so children can use their own ideas rather than just following rules.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 角色扮演游戏最能培养想象力，孩子要自己创造角色和故事，如过家家、扮医生；积木类搭建游戏也好，关键是游戏要开放，让孩子用自己的想法而非只守规则。

questions.question_en: How important is imagination to children?
questions.answer_en: I'd say imagination is extremely important for children's development. It helps them understand the world, solve problems and express their emotions, especially when they can't put feelings into words. For example, a child who imagines being a superhero may be practising courage. Imagination also supports learning, because children who can picture things in their minds often understand new concepts more easily. So in my view, imagination isn't just play, it's a foundation for creativity and confidence later in life.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 想象力对孩子发展极其重要；帮他们理解世界、解决问题、表达情绪，如想象自己是超级英雄是在练习勇气；也促进学习，是未来创造力和自信的基础。

topics.title_zh: 描述一个很多人都微笑的场合
topics.title_en: Describe an occasion when many people were smiling

questions.question_en: Describe an occasion when many people were smiling
questions.question_zh: 描述一个很多人都微笑的场合。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to describe an occasion when almost everyone around me was smiling, and that was the evening performance at my school's sports event. It happened in my second year of high school, on the last day of the annual sports meeting. The whole school gathered in the big outdoor stadium, and the evening show was the grand finale of the event.

I was there with my classmates, and we had all been looking forward to it for weeks, because each class had prepared a performance. The stage was set up in the middle of the field, with colourful lights and loud music, and the atmosphere was electric. I remember our class performed a dance routine, and although we had practised for a month, we were all nervous. When we finished, the whole crowd cheered, and I could see everyone in the audience smiling and clapping.

The reason most people were smiling is that the performances were genuinely entertaining, and the whole event had a joyful, competitive spirit. Teachers were smiling too, which was rare, because they were proud of their students. What struck me most was how the smiles spread across the whole stadium, from the performers on stage to the parents in the stands. Looking back, it was one of the happiest evenings of my school life, and I still remember the warmth of that moment whenever I think about it.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 高二学校运动会最后一天的晚上表演，全校聚在操场，我们班跳了练一个月的舞蹈，表演很精彩；全场欢呼，老师家长都在微笑，是我校园生活最快乐的夜晚之一。

questions.question_en: Do you think people who like to smile are more friendly?
questions.answer_en: Generally speaking, yes, I think people who smile often come across as more friendly and approachable. A smile is a universal signal of warmth, and it makes others feel comfortable. Having said that, a smile doesn't always mean genuine friendliness, because some people smile out of politeness. So I'd say smiling helps, but real friendliness is shown through actions as well.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 爱笑的人通常显得更友好、易接近，微笑是温暖的通用信号；但微笑不一定代表真心友好，有人出于礼貌，真正的友好还要看行动。

questions.question_en: Why do most people smile in photographs?
questions.answer_en: I think most people smile in photographs because a smile is seen as the standard way to look happy and presentable. When we take a photo, we want to record a pleasant moment, and a smile makes the picture look warm and positive. In my country, people often say 'say cheese' to get everyone to smile naturally. Having said that, some people prefer a serious or stylish look in photos, so it really depends on the person and the occasion.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 拍照时多数人微笑，因为微笑是显得开心得体的标准方式，让照片温暖积极；我国常说"茄子"让大家自然笑；也有人喜欢酷酷的表情，看人和场合。

questions.question_en: Do women smile more than men? Why?
questions.answer_en: I'd say, in many cultures, women do tend to smile more than men, although it's not a biological rule. One reason is social expectation, because women are often taught to be pleasant and agreeable, while men are expected to appear serious or strong. That said, this is changing, and nowadays more men feel free to smile openly, especially in casual settings.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 很多文化里女性确实比男性笑得多，但这不是生理规律；社会期待女性亲切随和、男性严肃坚强；正式照片里女性常大笑而男性微笑或面无表情，不过现在正在改变。

questions.question_en: Do people smile more when they are younger or older?
questions.answer_en: I think people smile more when they are younger, generally speaking. Children smile easily because they experience joy more directly and don't worry about appearances. As people grow older, they face more stress, like work and family responsibilities, which can make them smile less. So I'd say smiling tends to decrease in the middle years, but can return later.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 总体说人年轻时笑得多，孩子直接感受快乐不担心形象；成年后面临工作家庭压力笑得更少；但退休老人比中年人笑得多，因为时间多了，微笑在中年减少、晚年回归。

questions.question_en: Is smiling important in your culture?
questions.answer_en: Yes, smiling is quite important in my culture, especially in social and business situations. A smile is seen as a sign of politeness and goodwill, and it helps build relationships. Having said that, in my country, people sometimes smile to hide embarrassment or to avoid conflict, so a smile doesn't always mean happiness. On the whole, though, smiling is definitely valued as a social skill.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 微笑在我国文化中很重要，尤其在社交和商务场合，被视为礼貌和善意的标志；初次见面微笑让交流更顺畅；但有时人们用微笑掩饰尴尬或避免冲突，微笑不一定代表开心。

questions.question_en: Are there any occasions when people need to pretend to smile?
questions.answer_en: Yes, there are quite a few occasions when people have to pretend to smile. For example, in customer service, workers are expected to smile even when they're tired or dealing with difficult customers. I think this kind of smile is more about social harmony than genuine emotion. Having said that, pretending to smile too often can be exhausting, which is why some people find service jobs quite draining.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 有不少场合需要假笑，如客服人员再累也要对难缠顾客微笑，婚礼、商务晚宴上为礼貌而笑；这种微笑更多为社交和谐而非真实情感，但常假笑很累人。

topics.title_zh: 描述一次你不被允许使用手机的场合
topics.title_en: Describe an occasion when you were not allowed to use your mobile phone

questions.question_en: Describe an occasion when you were not allowed to use your mobile phone
questions.question_zh: 描述一次你不被允许使用手机的场合。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about a time when I was not allowed to use my mobile phone, and that was during my three years of high school. The school had a strict rule that banned phones on campus, so from Monday to Friday, I had to hand in my phone every morning and could only get it back on Friday evening.

The rule applied everywhere in the school, in the classrooms, the dormitory and even the canteen. The reason behind it was that the school believed phones distracted students from their studies, and they wanted us to focus entirely on preparing for the university entrance exam. Teachers would check our desks and lockers from time to time, and anyone caught with a phone would have it confiscated for a whole month.

To be honest, I hated the rule at first, because I felt extremely bored without my phone. In the evenings, after finishing my homework, I had nothing to do, and I remember staring at the ceiling in the dorm, counting down the days until the weekend. However, as time went on, I got used to it, and I started reading novels and playing basketball with my classmates instead. Looking back, although I wouldn't want to repeat it, I think the rule actually helped me concentrate, and it taught me that life without a phone can be quite enjoyable.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 高中三年学校禁止带手机，周一到周五每天上交、周五晚才拿回；学校认为手机会分散学习注意力；起初很无聊，晚上没事做，后来习惯后改读小说、打篮球，反而更专注。

questions.question_en: How do young and old people use mobile phones differently?
questions.answer_en: I think the difference is quite clear. Young people use phones for almost everything, like social media, games, videos and chatting with friends, so their phones are basically an extension of their social life. Older people, on the other hand, tend to use phones for practical purposes, like making calls, checking the news or using payment apps. Having said that, the gap is narrowing as older people become more tech-savvy.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 年轻人几乎用手机做所有事，社交、游戏、视频，手机是社交生活的延伸；老年人主要用于打电话、看新闻、支付等实用功能；不过随着老人更懂科技，差距在缩小。

questions.question_en: What positive and negative impact do mobile phones have on friendship?
questions.answer_en: Mobile phones have both sides, I think. On the positive side, they make it easy to stay in touch, especially with friends who live far away, and they help people organise meet-ups quickly. On the negative side, phones can weaken friendships, because people may spend time scrolling instead of talking face to face. So on balance, phones are a useful tool, but they work best when people remember to put them down and connect in person.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 手机对友谊有利有弊；好处是方便联系远方朋友、快速约见面；坏处是大家只顾刷手机不面对面聊天，如聚餐各看各的屏幕；手机是好工具，但要记得放下它。

questions.question_en: Is it a waste of time to take pictures with mobile phones?
questions.answer_en: I wouldn't say it's a complete waste of time, because photos help us remember special moments. However, I do think people sometimes overdo it, spending so much time taking pictures that they forget to enjoy the moment itself. In my country, it's common to see people filming entire concerts through their phones instead of watching the show. So I'd say taking a few photos is fine, but it becomes a waste when it replaces real experience.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 拍照不完全是浪费时间，照片帮我们记住特别时刻，多年后看假期照片能唤起回忆；但有人过度，只顾拍照忘了享受当下，如整场演唱会都举着手机拍；拍几张可以，取代真实体验才是浪费。

questions.question_en: Do you think it is necessary to have laws on the use of mobile phones?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think some laws are necessary, especially for safety. For example, many countries have banned using phones while driving, because distracted driving causes serious accidents. Having said that, I don't think laws should control every aspect of phone use, because that would be too restrictive. So on the whole, laws should focus on situations where phone use clearly harms others, rather than on personal habits.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 有些法律是必要的，尤其为安全，如多国禁止开车用手机，因为分心驾驶导致严重事故；医院、影院等场所也需限制；但法律不应管到所有细节，应聚焦明显危害他人的情形。

questions.question_en: What are examples of good and poor phone manners?
questions.answer_en: Good phone manners include keeping your phone on silent in meetings, not checking it while someone is talking to you, and stepping outside to take a call. Poor manners, on the other hand, include playing loud videos in public, answering calls during a conversation, or scrolling through your phone at the dinner table. I think these manners matter because they show respect for the people around you.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 好的手机礼仪包括会议静音、别人说话时不看手机、接电话到外面；坏礼仪包括公共场合外放视频、谈话中接电话、饭桌上刷手机；我国认为家庭聚餐用手机不礼貌，礼仪体现对身边人的尊重。

questions.question_en: How does the internet benefit people?
questions.answer_en: The internet benefits people in countless ways, I think. It gives us instant access to information, so we can learn almost anything online, from cooking to coding. It also connects people across the world, which is especially valuable for families separated by distance. Having said that, the internet has downsides too, like misinformation and addiction, but on the whole, its benefits clearly outweigh the problems.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 互联网好处无数；让我们即时获取信息，几乎什么都能在线学；连接世界各地的人，对异地家庭尤其宝贵；我国网购、支付、预订都很方便；虽有虚假信息和成瘾等弊端，但总体利大于弊。

topics.title_zh: 描述一次你给别人建议的经历
topics.title_en: Describe a time when you gave advice to others

questions.question_en: Describe a time when you gave advice to others
questions.question_zh: 描述一次你给别人建议的经历。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about a time when I gave advice to a classmate about learning programming. This happened during my second year at university, when I was already studying computer science.

The person I gave advice to was a classmate of mine, a guy who shared a few courses with me. He'd been thinking about learning to code for a while, but he kept putting it off because he didn't know where to start. One day he came up to me after class and asked which programming language he should begin with.

The advice I gave him was to start with Python. I told him that Python has a very simple and readable syntax, which makes it much easier for beginners to pick up. I also mentioned that there are tons of free resources online, like tutorials and practice websites, so he wouldn't have to spend any money. Most importantly, I said that starting with an easy language means you're less likely to give up in the first few weeks, which is exactly when most people quit.

The reason I gave this advice is that I'd been through the same struggle myself. When I first started, I tried a difficult language and almost gave up, so I knew from experience how important it is to build confidence early. He listened to my suggestion, and a few months later he told me he could already write small tools with Python. I felt genuinely happy that my advice had helped him get started.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲的是大二时给一个同学学编程的建议。给谁：一个同班同学，想学编程但一直拖着，不知道从哪开始，课后问我该先学哪门语言。什么建议：建议他从 Python 入手，语法简单易读，新手容易上手；网上免费资源多，不用花钱；最重要的是从简单的语言开始，头几周不容易放弃，而大多数人正是在这时候放弃的。为什么给：我自己踩过同样的坑，一开始学了门难的语言差点放弃，所以知道早期建立信心有多重要。结果：他听了建议，几个月后说已经能用 Python 写小工具了，我很开心建议帮到了他。

questions.question_en: Should people prepare before giving advice?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think people should prepare before giving advice, especially when the topic is serious. If you give advice without understanding the person's situation, it can easily be misleading or even harmful. For example, when someone asks about career choices, you need to know their background and interests first. That said, for small everyday matters, a quick and honest opinion is usually fine. So I'd say preparation matters more when the stakes are higher.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 是的，给建议前应该准备，尤其是严肃话题。不了解对方情况就建议容易误导甚至有害，比如职业选择要先了解背景和兴趣。不过日常小事随口给个诚实意见就行。事情越重要越需要准备。

questions.question_en: Is it good to ask advice from strangers online?
questions.answer_en: I think it can be helpful in some ways, but it also has risks. Online, you can get a wide range of opinions from people with different experiences, which is useful for things like choosing a phone or planning a trip. However, strangers don't know your personal situation, and some advice online is simply wrong or even dangerous, especially about health or money. So I'd say it's fine for general questions, but for important decisions, you should rely on people you trust.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 网上问陌生人建议有好处也有风险。好处是能听到各种不同经验的人的意见，适合选手机、规划旅行这类事；但陌生人不知道你的个人情况，网上有些建议是错的甚至危险的，尤其是健康和钱的事。一般问题可以问，重要决定要靠信任的人。

questions.question_en: What are the personalities of people whose job is to give advice to others?
questions.answer_en: I think people who give advice professionally, like consultants or career counsellors, usually share some common traits. They tend to be patient and good listeners, because they need to understand the problem fully before saying anything. They're also quite analytical, since they have to weigh different options and explain them clearly. On top of that, they need to be empathetic, because people often come to them when they're worried or confused. So I'd say listening skills and empathy are probably the most important qualities.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 以给建议为职业的人，比如顾问、职业咨询师，通常有共同特质：耐心、善于倾听，因为要先完全理解问题才能开口；分析能力强，要权衡各种选项并解释清楚；还要有同理心，因为人们往往在焦虑困惑时来找他们。倾听和同理心最重要。

questions.question_en: What are the problems if you ask too many people for advice?
questions.answer_en: The main problem is that you end up with too many conflicting opinions, which makes it harder to decide, not easier. Different people will give different suggestions based on their own experiences, and some of them will contradict each other. As a result, you might spend so much time comparing opinions that you never actually make a move. I think it's better to ask one or two people you trust, and then make your own decision, because in the end, you're the one who has to live with it.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 主要问题是会得到太多互相矛盾的意见，反而更难决定。不同人基于自己的经验给不同建议，有些还互相冲突，结果你可能花大量时间比较意见，最后根本没行动。最好问一两个信任的人，然后自己做决定，因为最终承担后果的是你自己。

questions.question_en: Why do some people think it is better to ask for advice from friends than from parents?
questions.answer_en: I think it's mainly because friends are closer to your own age and situation, which makes their advice feel more relevant. Parents, on the other hand, grew up in a different era, and their suggestions can sometimes feel out of touch with modern life. Friends also understand your daily struggles better, and they're less likely to judge you. That said, parents usually have more life experience, so I think the ideal approach is to listen to both and take what makes sense.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 主要是因为朋友年龄和处境更接近，建议更贴合实际；父母成长于不同年代，建议有时显得跟不上现代生活。朋友也更懂你日常的难处，更不会评判你。不过父母人生经验更多，理想做法是两边都听，取有用的部分。

questions.question_en: When would old people ask young people for advice?
questions.answer_en: Old people would usually ask young people for advice about technology and modern trends. For example, many older people ask their children or grandchildren how to use smartphones, pay online, or set up video calls. They might also ask about new things like social media or electric cars, which they didn't grow up with. I think this is a natural exchange, because young people are more familiar with the digital world, while older people have more experience in other areas of life.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 老人通常向年轻人请教科技和现代潮流方面的事。比如很多老人问子女或孙辈怎么用智能手机、在线支付、开视频通话；也会问社交媒体、电动车这类他们没经历过的新事物。这是自然的互补，年轻人更熟悉数字世界，老人则在生活其他方面经验更多。

topics.title_zh: 描述一个你参加过的、你不喜欢所放音乐的活动
topics.title_en: Describe an event you attended in which you didn't enjoy the music played

questions.question_en: Describe an event you attended in which you didn't enjoy the music played
questions.question_zh: 描述一个你参加过的、你不喜欢所放音乐的活动。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to describe an event I attended where I really didn't enjoy the music. It was a promotion event at a shopping mall, and it happened about half a year ago, on a weekend afternoon.

I went there with my girlfriend. We had planned to spend the afternoon shopping and having a look around the mall, and when we arrived, we noticed that a big stage had been set up on the ground floor. A local store was holding a sales promotion, and they'd hired a singer to perform live to attract customers.

The music itself was the main problem. The singer was clearly not very experienced, and he kept going off-key, especially on the high notes. On top of that, the speakers were turned up extremely loud, so the sound was harsh and uncomfortable to listen to. It was the kind of noise that made you want to cover your ears, and it echoed through the whole building.

The reason I didn't enjoy it is that the combination of bad singing and excessive volume made the whole experience unpleasant. We had planned to browse the shops for a while, but after a few minutes we decided to go inside the stores instead, just to get away from the noise. Looking back, I remember the day mainly because of how bad the music was, which is a shame, because the mall itself is usually a nice place to visit.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲的是半年前一个周末下午，在商场参加的一场促销活动，音乐很难听。和谁去：和女朋友，本来计划下午逛街，到商场发现一楼搭了大舞台，一家店搞促销，请了个歌手现场唱歌招揽顾客。音乐问题：歌手明显没什么经验，一直跑调，尤其高音部分；音响还开得特别大，声音刺耳难受，整个楼都在回响。为什么不喜欢：难听的演唱加过大的音量让整个体验很不舒服，本来想逛一会儿，结果没几分钟就躲进店里避开噪音。回想起来那天只记得音乐有多难听，挺可惜的，因为商场平时是个不错的地方。

questions.question_en: What kind of music events do people like today?
questions.answer_en: I think people today prefer music events that are interactive and visually impressive. For example, concerts and music festivals are very popular, because they combine live performance with a lively atmosphere. Many young people also enjoy events where they can take photos and share them on social media, so lighting and stage design matter a lot. Compared to the past, I'd say people now care almost as much about the experience around the music as the music itself.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 现在的人喜欢互动性强、视觉效果好的音乐活动。演唱会和音乐节很受欢迎，因为现场表演加热闹的氛围；很多年轻人还喜欢能拍照发社交媒体的活动，所以灯光和舞台设计很重要。和过去比，人们现在几乎同样看重音乐周边的体验。

questions.question_en: Do you think children should receive some musical education?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I think musical education is valuable for children, even if they don't become musicians. Learning an instrument or singing helps children develop patience and concentration, because it takes regular practice to improve. It also gives them a way to express emotions and relieve stress. Of course, it shouldn't be forced, since children who are pushed too hard may end up hating music. So I'd say a light and enjoyable introduction to music is beneficial for most children.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 是的，音乐教育对孩子有价值，即使他们不当音乐家。学乐器或唱歌能培养耐心和专注力，因为需要规律练习才能进步；也给孩子表达情绪、缓解压力的方式。当然不能强迫，逼太紧孩子反而会讨厌音乐。轻松愉快的音乐启蒙对大多数孩子有益。

questions.question_en: What are the differences between old and young people's music preferences?
questions.answer_en: I think the differences are quite obvious. Young people tend to prefer pop music, K-pop and electronic music, which they often discover through social media and streaming platforms. Older people, on the other hand, usually enjoy classic songs and traditional music from their own generation, because those songs carry memories of their youth. Another difference is that young people listen to music more frequently, often while studying or commuting, whereas older people might listen mainly for relaxation.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 差异很明显。年轻人喜欢流行乐、K-pop 和电子乐，通常通过社交媒体和流媒体平台发现；老一辈喜欢自己年代的经典老歌和传统音乐，因为这些歌承载着他们年轻时的回忆。另一个区别是年轻人听音乐更频繁，学习或通勤时都听，老人则主要为了放松。

questions.question_en: What kind of music events are there in your country?
questions.answer_en: In my country, there are quite a few kinds of music events. Big concerts by famous singers are very common, and they're usually held in large stadiums or arenas. Music festivals have also become popular in recent years, especially among young people, with multiple bands performing over a day or two. On a smaller scale, there are live performances in bars and cafes, and shopping malls often hold promotional events with singers, like the one I mentioned earlier. So there's really something for every taste.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 我国音乐活动种类不少。知名歌手的演唱会很常见，通常在大型体育馆或场馆举行；音乐节近几年也流行起来，尤其受年轻人欢迎，一两天内多支乐队演出；小规模的有酒吧和咖啡馆的现场表演，商场也常办带歌手的促销活动，就像我之前提到的那个。各种口味都有得选。

questions.question_en: Why do many people like listening to music while doing sports?
questions.answer_en: I think music helps people exercise in several ways. First, a fast rhythm can help you keep a steady pace, especially when running or cycling, so you don't slow down without noticing. Music also distracts you from the physical discomfort, which makes the workout feel easier and more enjoyable. On top of that, a good playlist can boost your mood and give you extra energy. So I'd say music and sports go together very naturally for most people.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 音乐从几个方面帮助运动。快节奏能帮你保持稳定步频，尤其跑步骑车时，不会不知不觉慢下来；音乐还能分散对身体不适的注意力，让锻炼感觉更轻松愉快；好的歌单还能提升心情、给你额外能量。对大多数人来说音乐和运动很自然地搭配。

questions.question_en: What are the differences between listening to music at home and at a live concert?
questions.answer_en: The differences are mainly about sound quality and atmosphere. At home, you can listen in a comfortable environment with good speakers or headphones, and you can control the volume and choose exactly what you want to hear. At a live concert, the sound is much louder and more powerful, and you experience the music together with hundreds of other people, which creates a strong sense of excitement. However, concerts can be tiring and expensive, and the sound isn't always perfect. So I'd say home listening is for relaxation, while concerts are for the experience.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 区别主要在音质和氛围。在家可以在舒适环境里用好音响或耳机听，能控制音量、选自己想听的；现场演唱会声音更响更有冲击力，和几百人一起体验音乐，兴奋感很强。不过演唱会累人又贵，音效也不总是完美。在家听是放松，去现场是为了体验。

topics.title_zh: 描述一次你鼓励别人做他/她不想做的事
topics.title_en: Describe a time when you encouraged someone to do something that he/she didn't want to do

questions.question_en: Describe a time when you encouraged someone to do something that he/she didn't want to do
questions.question_zh: 描述一次你鼓励别人做他/她不想做的事。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about a time when I encouraged a friend of mine to do something he wasn't really keen on. The person I'm talking about is one of my closest friends, and we've known each other since high school.

What I encouraged him to do was to keep preparing for the graduate school entrance exam, which we call 考研 in China. He had been studying for it for a while, but at some point he lost motivation and started thinking about giving up. He told me he felt the pressure was too much, and he wasn't sure the exam was worth all the effort.

When I heard that, I tried to encourage him. I reminded him that he'd already come a long way, and that giving up now would mean all those months of study were wasted. I also told him that even if he didn't get into his first-choice university, the knowledge he'd gained would still help him in the future. His reaction was a bit mixed, to be honest. He listened to what I said and seemed to agree, but I could tell he was only half-listening, and he didn't really change his attitude afterwards.

The reason I encouraged him is that I genuinely believed he had the ability to succeed. He's a hardworking person, and I thought the exam would open more doors for his career. Even though my encouragement didn't fully work, I still think it was the right thing to do, because sometimes people just need to hear that someone believes in them.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲的是鼓励一个高中就认识的好朋友坚持考研。鼓励什么：他备考考研一段时间后失去动力想放弃，说压力太大，不确定值不值得。我怎么鼓励：提醒他已经走了很长的路，现在放弃等于几个月的努力白费；还告诉他即使没考上第一志愿，学到的知识以后也有用。他的反应：听了似乎同意，但明显只是听听而已，之后态度没真正改变。为什么鼓励：我真心相信他有能力成功，他勤奋，而且考研能为职业打开更多门。虽然鼓励没完全奏效，我仍觉得做对了，因为有时候人只是需要听到有人相信他。

questions.question_en: How can leaders encourage their employees?
questions.answer_en: I think leaders can encourage employees mainly by recognising their efforts and giving them clear goals. When people feel their work is noticed and appreciated, they tend to be more motivated. Leaders can also encourage employees by offering opportunities for growth, like training or promotions, which gives them something to work towards. On top of that, a supportive atmosphere, where mistakes are treated as learning rather than punishment, makes people more willing to try their best.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 领导鼓励员工主要靠认可努力和给出清晰目标。当人们感到工作被看见、被欣赏，就会更有动力；还可以通过提供成长机会，如培训或晋升，让人有奔头；另外支持性的氛围，把错误当学习而不是惩罚，会让人更愿意全力以赴。

questions.question_en: When should parents encourage their children?
questions.answer_en: Parents should encourage their children especially when they face challenges or setbacks. For example, when a child fails an exam or loses a competition, that's the moment they need support the most, because they might feel discouraged and doubt themselves. Parents should also encourage children when they try something new, even if they're not very good at it at first. I think the key is to encourage effort rather than only results, so children learn that trying matters.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 父母尤其应该在孩子面对挑战或挫折时鼓励他们。比如孩子考试失利或比赛输了，那是最需要支持的时刻，因为他们可能灰心、怀疑自己；孩子尝试新事物时也该鼓励，即使一开始做得不好。关键是鼓励努力而不是只看结果，让孩子明白尝试本身很重要。

questions.question_en: What kind of encouragement should parents give?
questions.answer_en: I think the most effective encouragement is specific rather than general. Instead of just saying 'well done', parents can point out what exactly the child did well, like 'you worked really hard on this project'. This kind of feedback helps children understand their strengths. Parents should also encourage children to keep going when things get difficult, rather than praising only easy successes. I'd say encouragement that focuses on effort and improvement is more valuable than praise for natural talent.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 最有效的鼓励是具体的而不是笼统的。与其只说'做得好'，父母可以指出孩子具体哪里做得好，比如'你在这个项目上真的很努力'，这种反馈帮孩子了解自己的长处。父母还应该在困难时鼓励孩子坚持，而不是只表扬轻松的成功。关注努力和进步的鼓励比夸天赋更有价值。

questions.question_en: Do you think some people are better than others at persuading?
questions.answer_en: Yes, I definitely think some people are naturally better at persuading others. Some people have strong communication skills, so they can explain their ideas clearly and make them sound convincing. Others are good at reading people's emotions, which helps them choose the right words at the right moment. That said, persuasion is also a skill that can be learned with practice. People who speak often, like teachers or salespeople, usually become better at it over time, so I'd say it's a mix of natural ability and experience.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 是的，有些人天生更会说服别人。有人沟通能力强，能把想法讲清楚、讲得有说服力；有人擅长读懂别人情绪，能在对的时机说对的话。不过说服也是可以练出来的技能，经常说话的人，比如老师或销售，会越练越好。所以是天分加经验。

questions.question_en: Should children do everything their parents ask them to do?
questions.answer_en: No, I don't think children should do everything their parents ask, because parents aren't always right. Some requests might be unreasonable, or based on outdated ideas, and blindly following them could harm the child's own development. However, I also think children should respect their parents and consider their advice seriously, since parents usually have more life experience. So I'd say the ideal situation is a balance, where children listen to their parents but also learn to make their own decisions as they grow older.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 不，孩子不该什么都听父母的，因为父母不一定总是对的。有些要求可能不合理，或基于过时的观念，盲目服从可能损害孩子自身发展。不过孩子也应该尊重父母、认真考虑他们的建议，因为父母通常经验更多。理想状态是平衡：听父母的，但随着长大也学会自己做决定。

questions.question_en: How can employers encourage their staff?
questions.answer_en: Employers can encourage their staff in several practical ways. Fair pay and reasonable working hours are the basics, because people can't stay motivated if they feel underpaid or overworked. Beyond that, recognising good work publicly, like praising an employee in a meeting, can boost morale a lot. Employers can also encourage staff by giving them more responsibility and trusting them with important tasks, which makes people feel valued. I think a combination of fair treatment and genuine recognition works best.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 雇主可以用几种实际方式鼓励员工。公平的薪酬和合理的工作时间是基础，觉得工资低或过度劳累的人很难保持动力；公开认可好工作，比如在会议上表扬员工，能大大提升士气；还可以给员工更多责任、信任他们做重要任务，让人感到被重视。公平待遇加真诚认可的组合最有效。

topics.title_zh: 描述一次你想骑自行车/摩托车/开车去的小旅行
topics.title_en: Describe a bicycle/motorcycle/car trip you would like to go

questions.question_en: Describe a bicycle/motorcycle/car trip you would like to go
questions.question_zh: 描述一次你想骑自行车/摩托车/开车去的小旅行。
questions.answer_en:
I'd like to talk about a trip I would like to go on by car, which is something I've never actually experienced before. The person I'd like to go with is my girlfriend, because we both enjoy travelling together, and we've talked about this idea several times.

As for where we'd go, we haven't decided on a specific destination yet. We've discussed a few options, like driving along the coast near Shenzhen, or heading to a scenic area in the mountains. The main thing we agree on is that we want a route with beautiful scenery, where we can stop whenever we feel like it, rather than following a fixed schedule.

In terms of timing, I think we'd go during a long holiday, probably in the summer, when the weather is good for driving. We'd probably spend two or three days on the road, staying in small towns along the way. Since neither of us has done this kind of trip before, we'd need to plan it carefully, like booking hotels in advance and checking the car.

The reason I want to go by car is that it gives you a sense of freedom that other transport can't offer. You can change your plans at any moment, pull over to enjoy a view, and carry whatever you need. I also think it would be a great way to spend quality time with my girlfriend, away from the busy city life. So even though we haven't fixed the details yet, I'm really looking forward to making this trip happen.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 讲的是想和女朋友开车去的一次旅行，自己从没体验过。和谁去：女朋友，我们都喜欢一起旅行，聊过好几次这个想法。去哪：还没定具体目的地，讨论过几个选项，比如沿着深圳附近的海岸开，或者去山里的风景区；共识是想要风景好的路线，想停就停，不按固定行程走。什么时候：长假期间，大概夏天，天气适合开车；路上花两三天，沿途住小镇；因为都没经验，需要提前规划，比如订酒店、检查车况。为什么开车：开车给人其他交通方式给不了的自由感，随时能改计划、停下来看风景、带想带的东西；也是和女朋友远离城市忙碌生活、好好相处的机会。虽然细节还没定，但很期待成行。

questions.question_en: Which form of vehicle is more popular in your country, bikes, cars or motorcycles?
questions.answer_en: I think cars are the most popular form of vehicle in my country, especially in recent years, because more and more families can afford them. In big cities, however, bikes and electric bikes are also very common for short trips, since they're cheap and easy to park. Motorcycles are less popular in cities, mainly because of traffic restrictions, but they're still widely used in smaller towns and rural areas. So I'd say cars dominate overall, but bikes play a big role in daily city life.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 我国最普及的交通工具是汽车，尤其近几年越来越多家庭买得起。不过大城市里自行车和电动车短途出行也很常见，便宜又好停；摩托车在城市里因限行不太流行，但在小城镇和农村仍广泛使用。总体汽车占主导，但自行车在城市日常生活中作用很大。

questions.question_en: Do you think air pollution comes mostly from mobile vehicles?
questions.answer_en: I think vehicles are a major source of air pollution, but not necessarily the biggest one in every place. In big cities, car exhaust definitely contributes a lot to smog, especially during rush hours. However, in many areas, factories and power plants produce even more pollution than vehicles. So I'd say vehicles are one of the main causes, but the situation depends on the region. In my country, the government has been promoting electric vehicles partly for this reason.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 机动车是空气污染的主要来源之一，但不一定是每个地方最大的来源。大城市里汽车尾气确实对雾霾贡献很大，尤其高峰时段；但很多地区工厂和发电厂产生的污染比机动车还多。所以机动车是主因之一，但要看地区。我国政府推广电动车部分就是为了这个原因。

questions.question_en: Do you think people need to change the way of transportation drastically to protect the environment?
questions.answer_en: I think some change is necessary, but it doesn't have to be drastic all at once. Encouraging people to use public transport, walk or cycle more would already make a big difference in cities. Promoting electric vehicles is another practical step, since they produce much less pollution than petrol cars. That said, completely changing how everyone travels would be very difficult, because many people depend on cars for work and family reasons. So I'd say gradual but steady changes are more realistic than a sudden revolution.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 改变是必要的，但不一定要一下子大改。鼓励人们多坐公共交通、步行或骑车，在城市里就能带来很大不同；推广电动车是另一个实际步骤，比汽油车污染少得多。不过彻底改变所有人的出行方式很难，因为很多人因工作和家庭原因离不开车。渐进但稳定的改变比突然的革命更现实。

questions.question_en: How are the transportation systems in urban areas and rural areas different?
questions.answer_en: The differences are quite significant. In urban areas, there are usually well-developed systems, like subways, buses and taxis, so people can get around easily without a car. Rural areas, on the other hand, often have limited public transport, with only a few buses running each day, so people rely heavily on private vehicles or motorcycles. Roads in rural areas may also be narrower and less well maintained. I think this gap is one reason why people in the countryside feel they need their own vehicle.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 差异很明显。城市通常有发达的系统，如地铁、公交、出租车，没车也能方便出行；农村公共交通有限，每天只有几班公交，所以人们严重依赖私家车或摩托车；农村道路也可能更窄、维护更差。这个差距正是农村人觉得需要自己买车的原因之一。

questions.question_en: Why do more people own and drive private vehicles now?
questions.answer_en: I think the main reason is that cars have become more affordable, so owning one is no longer a luxury for most families. Rising incomes mean more people can buy a car, and many see it as a necessity for convenience, especially for commuting or taking children to school. Public transport can also be crowded and time-consuming, which pushes people towards driving. On top of that, in some areas, having a car is almost expected for social reasons. So I'd say affordability and convenience are the two biggest factors.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 主要原因是汽车变得更便宜，对大多数家庭来说拥有汽车不再是奢侈品。收入增长让更多人买得起车，很多人把它看作便利的必需品，尤其通勤或接送孩子；公共交通又挤又耗时，也推动人们开车。另外有些地方出于社交原因几乎默认要有车。可负担性和便利性是两个最大因素。

questions.question_en: What do you think of the future of electric cars?
questions.answer_en: I think electric cars will become the mainstream in the future, and this is already happening in my country. They're cheaper to run than petrol cars, and they produce much less pollution, which fits the global push for cleaner energy. As battery technology improves, concerns about charging time and range will gradually disappear. That said, there are still challenges, like building enough charging stations and recycling old batteries. On the whole, I'm quite optimistic that electric cars will dominate the market within a decade or two.
questions.answer_hint_zh: 我认为电动车未来会成为主流，我国已经在发生。它们比汽油车运行成本低，污染少得多，符合全球清洁能源的趋势；随着电池技术进步，充电时间和续航的顾虑会逐渐消失。不过仍有挑战，比如建足够的充电站、回收旧电池。总体我很乐观，一二十年内电动车会主导市场。
